title: fix: spec-lock gate never checks locked tests are tracked in git — a pinned test can ship untracked and CI runs a vacuous green

acceptanceCriteria.text: `chalk done` (and/or `chalk pr`) verifies every locked test path pinned in the task spec is tracked (`git ls-files`) in the task's worktree, and fails with an error naming the untracked path(s)
the error message suggests the fix (`git add <path>` / re-run `chalk commit`)
locked test: `chalk done` refuses when a pinned test file exists on disk but is untracked, and succeeds once the file is tracked

issue.body:
Three reviews in this sweep (release --commit, config-drift gate, evidence-push) independently flagged the same hole: a locked test exists on disk with its sha256 pinned in `.chalk/tasks.json`, but the file is untracked — absent from `git diff --stat` — so a fresh checkout / CI (`node --test`) runs WITHOUT the contract tests guarding the criteria. `chalk done` verifies the sha256 against the working tree only; nothing checks the file is in git. The pipeline `commit` stage happens to sweep untracked files via `changedPaths` (`status --porcelain -uall`), but manual-order flows and anything done before/around the commit stage escape it, and the reviewer had to catch it every single time.

- [ ] `chalk done` (and/or `chalk pr`) verifies every locked test path pinned in the task spec is tracked (`git ls-files`) in the task's worktree, and fails with an error naming the untracked path(s)
- [ ] the error message suggests the fix (`git add <path>` / re-run `chalk commit`)
- [ ] locked test: `chalk done` refuses when a pinned test file exists on disk but is untracked, and succeeds once the file is tracked

_filed by `chalk retro` (self-healing)_

findings.note: untrackedLockedTests() silently exempts any pinned path starting with '.chalk/' — criterion 1 says EVERY locked test path pinned in the spec must be verified. The exemption is justified in a comment (spine state lands out-of-band), but a task that pins an e2e spec under .chalk/ gets no tracking gate at all, and no test asserts this carve-out's behavior in either direction.

In `chalk pr`, the already-open-PR early return (t.pr set) exits BEFORE the tracking gate, so a test that becomes untracked after PR open (e.g. `git rm --cached`) is never re-checked on subsequent `chalk pr` invocations; `chalk done` still catches it, so the criterion's 'and/or' is technically satisfied.

Path matching is exact string equality against `git ls-files -z` output — a pinned path written as './contract.test.mjs', with backslashes on Windows, or differing only in case on a case-insensitive filesystem would be reported as untracked (false block). No normalization, no test for these forms.

Core contract is genuinely covered and would fail on revert: locked test/spec-lock-tracking.test.mjs asserts done refuses (naming the path, saying why, suggesting `git add`), does not flip state to done, succeeds after `git add`, that pr blocks BEFORE pushing, and that non-git trees are exempt. Remaining untested surface is only the .chalk/ exemption and multi-path error rendering (tests use a single pinned file).

Gate runs in `done` only after verify passes and returns [] for empty pins or non-git trees, so existing done/pr flows without pinned tests are unaffected; existing pipeline/testgate suites (missingRequiredTest) are untouched.

title: ci: add a windows-latest lane and fix what breaks

acceptanceCriteria.text: The pull-request and dev/main test workflow runs the complete zero-dependency node --test suite on both ubuntu-latest and windows-latest using the supported Node version; concurrency cancellation behavior remains unchanged.

Chalk's executable discovery, subprocess execution, git workflows, temporary paths, and path normalization pass on Windows without relying on POSIX-only command -v, /bin/sh, executable bits, or shell quoting.
Any test that cannot meaningfully execute on Windows is skipped only through an explicit process.platform guard whose reason cites a tracked follow-up issue; the rest of the suite remains enabled.

A locked test protects the Windows CI matrix, full-suite command, supported Node version, and absence of untracked unconditional Windows exclusions; user-facing documentation states the verified platform support level.

issue.body:
**From the harness review (finding 10).** The suite is hermetic `node --test` with zero deps, but Windows is entirely unexercised: `command -v` in doctor's onPath, shell quoting in git/stash commands, and path edges are the likely breakage points. The demo and all gates are pure Node otherwise.

**Sketch:** add `windows-latest` to the test matrix in `.github/workflows/test.yml`, triage failures, fix or conditionally skip with an issue link. Until then README should state Windows is best-effort.

title: feat: configurable e2e spec pattern (not just *.test.yaml)

acceptanceCriteria.text: protocol.e2e.specPattern selects which locked test paths are browser specs: a suffix, a comma-separated list, or an array; a leading '*' is tolerated (glob-ish). Empty/unset preserves the historical '.test.yaml' so existing projects are unchanged.
The pattern is honored everywhere isSpec decides spec-ness: verify's e2e gate, the e2e runner's filter, doctor's 'locks a spec but e2e is off' warning, and the board's testArtifact evidence lookup.
Under a custom pattern, a matching locked spec actually runs through verify's BYO e2e gate (producing run evidence); a non-matching path is treated as an ordinary file and never run as a spec.
Locked test proves the matcher normalization (default/suffix/list/array/leading-*) and the end-to-end verify effect in both directions (custom pattern runs it; default does not).

issue.body:
**From the harness review (finding 10).** `isSpec()` hardcodes the `.test.yaml` suffix; teams with a different browser-spec convention silently get no e2e gate on their locked specs.

**Sketch:** `protocol.e2e.specPattern` (glob or suffix list, default today's behavior); doctor's existing 'locks a spec but e2e is off' warning should honor it.

findings.note: Criterion 2 requires the pattern be honored EVERYWHERE isSpec decides spec-ness. The four enumerated sites (verify.mjs:42, e2e.mjs:54 runner filter, doctor.mjs:71, boards.mjs:58) correctly thread proto.e2e.specPattern. But bin/chalk.mjs:1006 — the GitHub PR pipeline stage that runs browser specs and attaches screenshots — still hardcodes `.path.endsWith('.test.yaml')` instead of isSpec(path, specPattern). Under a custom pattern (e.g. '.e2e.yaml'), the pipeline pre-filters out the matching spec before runSpecs ever sees it, so a team on a custom convention gets NO screenshot evidence on their PR while verify does run it — an inconsistency that contradicts the 'everywhere' contract.

The locked suite exercises verify's gate (both directions) and the matcher normalization, but does not assert the pattern is honored in doctor's warning, the board's testArtifact lookup, or the PR pipeline. The bin/chalk.mjs:1006 hardcoded-suffix regression would pass the entire green suite, so the tests do not cover every spec-ness decision site named in criterion 2.

Criterion 2 enumerates the board's testArtifact evidence lookup as a spec-ness site. boards.mjs:58 correctly threads ctx.specPattern (from projectBoard's ctx), but no locked test directly asserts board behavior under a custom pattern — reverting only the boards.mjs line would not be caught by the suite. This is within criterion 4's stated test scope (which requires only matcher normalization + verify effect), and the underlying isSpec function is thoroughly tested, so it is a minor gap rather than a blocking one.

specMatcher strips only a single leading '*' via replace(/^\*/,''); a pattern like '**.e2e.yaml' would leave a literal '*' in the suffix and never match. Not required by the criteria (leading-'*' glob-ish is tolerated, not full glob), and the documented forms (suffix/comma-list/array/leading-*) all work correctly.

The prior review's blocking finding (bin/chalk.mjs:1006 evidence/PR pipeline hardcoded '.test.yaml') is now fixed to isSpec(p, specPattern) and covered by the added evidence-stage test; store.mjs default specPattern is set to '.test.yaml' preserving historical behavior. All five spec-ness sites and both verify directions are correctly honored — criteria 1–4 are met.

title: feat: held-out set outside the repo root (manual-mode blindness)

acceptanceCriteria.text: protocol.regression.dir accepts an absolute or ~-prefixed path OUTSIDE the repo (not just a repo-relative dir); a new heldOutBase resolver handles all three forms, empty/unset keeps the historical .chalk/held-out.

Locking and integrity work across the repo boundary: an inside-repo held-out file is stored repo-relative (portable), an outside file is stored by absolute path, and brokenHeldOut/audit detect a tamper of either.
guard listing/locking and chalk audit run end-to-end against an outside dir: guard add locks an outside file, audit is GREEN while intact and RED when the outside file is tampered.
chalk doctor recommends relocating the held-out set outside the repo when worktree isolation is off and the set is in-repo (manual-mode blindness), and stays quiet once the dir is already outside.

Locked test proves the resolver (relative/absolute/~), inside-vs-outside lock storage + round-trip, listing an absolute dir, the end-to-end guard→audit flow, and the doctor recommendation in both directions.

issue.body:
**From the harness review (finding 1, manual mode).** In worktree mode the gitignored `.chalk/held-out/` never reaches the agent's sandbox — but in MANUAL mode the agent works in the primary checkout and can simply read it. The contract forbids it; nothing enforces it.

**Sketch:** `regression.dir` already exists — support an absolute/outside-the-repo path (e.g. `~/.chalk-held-out/<project>`) end-to-end (audit, doctor checks, guard authoring), and have `chalk doctor` recommend it when no worktree isolation is configured.

findings.note: The reviewed diff itself only records PR/pipeline metadata (board.json, tasks.json, updates.jsonl); the actual feature code lives in the working tree from a prior commit. Inspected the tree: lib/regression.mjs (heldOutBase resolver handling relative/absolute/~ and empty-default; lockFile storing repo-relative inside vs absolute outside; brokenHeldOut/listDirFiles via lockAbs), bin/chalk.mjs guard add (resolves + locks outside files, audit uses brokenHeldOut), and lib/doctor.mjs (info recommendation gated on worktree.enabled===false && in-repo dir, quiet when absolute/~) all satisfy criteria 1-4.

Locked test test/held-out-outside-root.test.mjs exercises each criterion in both directions: resolver forms, inside-vs-outside lock storage + tamper round-trip, absolute-dir listing, end-to-end guard→audit (green intact / exit 2 tampered), and doctor recommendation present in-repo / absent when outside. Coverage matches the contract; no vacuous pass detected.

title: feat: context budget — cap buildContext size and prune injected lessons

acceptanceCriteria.text: protocol.contextBudget (bytes, generous default) caps the size of the chalk context blob; only the elastic lessons block is trimmed to fit — unset uses the default.
The task's essentials are never sacrificed for budget: acceptance criteria, locked tests, handoff, prior-review findings, and the contract are always present regardless of budget.
Under budget pressure the OLDEST lessons are elided first (most-recent kept) and a note reports how many were dropped and how to raise the budget.

Locked test proves: a tiny budget elides older lessons (note + newest survive, essentials intact), a generous/default budget keeps all lessons, and an extreme budget drops all lessons while criteria + contract remain.

issue.body:
**From the harness review (finding 6).** `buildContext` injects spec + criteria + lessons + prior reviews + handoff with no size cap; `lessons.md` grows forever. Large/old projects will degrade the executor silently (or hit stdin limits).

**Sketch:** a byte budget (config, generous default) with priority order (criteria > locked tests > handoff > recent lessons > older material elided with a note); `chalk archive` already compacts tasks/events — extend the idea to lessons.

findings.note: Criterion 2 lists handoff and prior-review findings as essentials that must always survive budget pressure, but the locked tests only assert criteria/locked-test/contract survival — no test sets up a handoff or a prior blocking review and checks it persists under a tiny budget. Coverage is indirect; the code structurally builds these into the never-trimmed `post` array, so the guarantee holds, but the test does not pin it.

fitLessonsBlock spends budget newest-first and elides oldest with a note pointing to protocol.contextBudget / `chalk archive`; buildContext computes essentials first and passes only the leftover (budget - essentialBytes) to the lessons block, so essentials are never sacrificed and unset budget falls back to DEFAULT_CONTEXT_BUDGET (65536). Verified against store.lessons() (oldest→newest, LESSON_CAP=15 ≥ 6) — behavior matches all four criteria. No blocking defect found.

title: feat: opt-in all-locks integrity — done tasks' locked tests stay protected

acceptanceCriteria.text: protocol.integrity accepts 'in-progress' (default when unset — today's behavior) or 'all-locks'. Under 'all-locks', chalk verify checks locked-test hash integrity for DONE tasks in addition to in-progress ones; unset/'in-progress' leaves done tasks' locks unchecked exactly as before.

Under 'all-locks', tampering (or deleting) a locked test owned by a DONE task makes verify RED and the report names the owning task and the offending path and points to chalk amend-spec; a matching hash stays green.
chalk amend-spec remains the only sanctioned change path: re-locking a done task's test updates its pin so verify returns GREEN again — no direct tasks.json editing.

Locked test proves all four states: all-locks catches a tampered done-task lock (RED), default mode ignores the same tamper (GREEN), a clean all-locks tree is GREEN, and amend-spec restores GREEN after a legitimate change.

issue.body:
**From the harness review (finding 5).** `verify` sweeps locked-test integrity only for in-progress tasks, so lock protection expires at `done`: a later task can weaken an earlier task's locked test to keep its own verify green (the ImpossibleBench cheat, one task removed). Held-out (P7) is the backstop but is opt-in.

**Sketch:** `protocol.integrity: "all-locks"` → verify hashes every done task's locked tests too; `chalk amend-spec` stays the sanctioned change path. Tradeoff to document: legitimate test evolution requires amend-spec on old tasks.

findings.note: verify's all-locks branch (lib/verify.mjs:49-54) gates strictly on proto.integrity === 'all-locks', so unset/'in-progress' leaves done-task locks unchecked exactly as before; any other string value silently behaves as in-progress with no validation warning, but this is a benign default-fail-safe not a criterion violation.

Deletion of a locked test is covered: store.brokenLocks (store.mjs:170) sets current=null when the file is missing, so a deleted done-task lock also flags a break under all-locks, satisfying the 'or deleting' clause of criterion 2.

Locked suite test/all-locks-integrity.test.mjs exercises all four required states (clean GREEN, tampered RED with task+path+amend-spec message, default-mode ignore incl. unset, amend-spec restore) and would fail if the all-locks branch were reverted — the report message, exit code 2, and re-lock pin are all asserted, so the change is not a vacuous pass.

title: feat: tamper-evident spine — warn when tasks.json/chalk.json changed outside chalk

acceptanceCriteria.text: protocol.tamperEvident (default false) opts in. When false/unset, chalk behaves exactly as before — no hashing, no warnings, no new writes on any command.

When true, chalk records sha256 baselines of chalk.json + tasks.json in gitignored .chalk/local/ after every chalk write; a subsequent command whose on-disk hash differs from the baseline prints a loud warning naming the file and logs a tamper event.
It is evidence, not a lock: after warning it re-baselines so the notice fires exactly once; a first enabled run with no baseline establishes one without warning (fail-safe).

Locked test proves: default-off is inert, chalk's own writes never false-positive, an outside edit to either file is caught (warning + event), the warning fires once, and the no-baseline case is fail-safe.

issue.body:
**From the harness review (finding 1).** Only locked tests and held-out files are hashed today. In manual mode nothing detects an agent hand-editing `.chalk/tasks.json` (mark-done-by-hand) or weakening `chalk.json` verify commands — enforcement is process discipline.

**Sketch:** record spine-file hashes in `.chalk/local/` after every CLI write; on the next invocation, if the on-disk hash differs from the recorded one, print a loud ⚠ (and log an event). Not a lock — tamper-EVIDENCE. The threat model is a sloppy/pressured agent, not a malicious human.

findings.note: Criterion 4 explicitly requires the locked test to prove 'default-off is inert', but every test in spine-tamper.test.mjs runs through repo(), which calls enableTamper() to set protocol.tamperEvident=true before any assertion. There is NO test exercising the feature-OFF (default/unset) path. So the central claim of criterion 1 — that with the feature off chalk does no hashing, prints no warning, and performs no new writes (e.g. no .chalk/local/spine.hashes.json is created) — is entirely unasserted. If the opt-in guard in saveMeta/saveTasks/warnSpineTamper were removed or inverted, the suite would still pass. That is a vacuous pass for the default-off contract.

Criterion 3's 'a first enabled run with no baseline establishes one without warning' is not directly asserted. Test 4 ('fail-safe') tests a DIFFERENT case: a pre-existing spine.hashes.json with an empty hashes {} object, exercising the recorded===undefined 'continue' branch — not the existsSync(spineHashes)===false first-run branch in warnSpineTamper. The genuine no-baseline-file establishment-without-warning path is only exercised incidentally inside repo() setup and never has a no-warning assertion on that first run.

warnSpineTamper now runs on EVERY command (except init), unconditionally calling Store.open()/meta() to read protocol config even when the feature is off. No test asserts this added per-command Store.open()/file read is harmless outside a spine or on malformed chalk.json beyond the broad try/catch; a swallowed error here silently disables detection with no visible signal, and there is no test that the catch path doesn't mask real spine-read regressions.

The 'exactly once' guarantee depends on warnSpineTamper re-baselining after emitting, but re-baselining records whatever tampered state is currently on disk as the new trusted baseline — so a hand-edit is permanently normalized after a single warning with no persisted record of the original hash. Only one test (test 2) covers warn-once for tasks.json; there is no warn-once coverage for chalk.json, nor a test that two DIFFERENT sequential outside edits each warn once (only that the same state stops warning).

By design (documented as 'evidence, not a lock'), warnSpineTamper re-baselines the tampered on-disk state after emitting, so the original trusted hash is not preserved and a hand-edit is silently normalized after a single warning. Test 5 confirms a *fresh, different* edit re-arms, so the intended one-shot-per-state behavior is covered; acceptable given the stated threat model.

warnSpineTamper now calls Store.open()/protocol() at the entry of every command (except init), wrapped in a broad try/catch. When the feature is off this adds a chalk.json read but returns before any write, and Tests 1/3 assert no new files/events/warnings, so default-off inertness (criteria 1/4) is genuinely pinned. The catch could mask a malformed-spine read, but the subsequent command fn would surface its own error, so no silent regression is introduced.

title: feat: chalk stats — gate-efficacy report from the event log

acceptanceCriteria.text: chalk stats reads tasks and events from the live spine AND .chalk/archive/, and reports review-gate efficacy: reviewed-task count, tasks blocked at least once before passing (catches), total block verdicts, and findings broken down by severity and by area
It reports churn: executor attempts and handoffs (totals and the worst offenders), and counts verify-RED blocks from the event log

It reports the gate-vs-bypass fraction over done tasks: the share that passed adversarial review vs done via review override (Overrode review gate decisions) or with no review, and the share landed through the pipeline (pipeline stage merged/cleaned) vs hand-landed

chalk stats --json emits the same report as machine-readable JSON; --since <date> restricts to tasks done and events emitted at/after that date; the command is pure read (never writes the spine), zero new dependencies
On a fresh spine with no tasks or events it prints a friendly empty-state message and exits 0 instead of throwing

issue.body:
**From the harness review (finding 8: no self-measurement).** Chalk never reports what its gates caught, so it can't prove its own value — to users or to us.

**Sketch:** read `.chalk/updates.jsonl` (+ archive) and report per task/wave: verify RED→GREEN cycles, review blocks + findings by area, break-it/mutation catches, INCONCLUSIVE probe warnings, churn (attempts/handoffs). Zero deps, pure read. `chalk stats [--since] [--json]`.

This repo's own oss-launch wave is a ready-made dataset: 5 of 9 gated tasks were BLOCKED by the adversarial reviewer before passing.

findings.note: Criterion 2 explicitly requires 'worst offenders', but the locked test (test/stats.test.mjs) never asserts churn.worst — deleting worstChurn from lib/stats.mjs (or hardcoding []) leaves the entire suite green. A criterion-named behavior shipped with zero test coverage is a vacuous pass.

Criterion 2 reads 'executor attempts and handoffs (totals and the worst offenders)', but worst offenders are computed only for attempts; handoffs is a bare total (lib/stats.mjs:75). Handoff events carry taskId ('Handoff written: …', lib/handoff.mjs:86), so a per-task handoff breakdown is feasible and is simply missing.

--since validation is a type check only (bin/chalk.mjs:898). An unparseable date (`--since garbage`) makes Date.parse return NaN, and `if (cut)` in computeStats (lib/stats.mjs:43) is falsy for NaN — the filter is silently skipped and the full-history report is printed labeled 'since garbage'. Same falsy hole for epoch dates (cut===0). No test covers an invalid --since.

verifyRedBlocks and overridden rely on brittle free-text matching against event wording produced elsewhere ('verify RED after executor'/'without a green verify' in lib/run.mjs:44-45; 'Decision: Overrode review gate for "…"' via lib/store.mjs:188 + bin/chalk.mjs:1354). Any future rewording silently zeroes these stats; no test couples the real emitters to the stats parser — the locked test hand-crafts the strings, so drift would go undetected.

Override attribution matches by task TITLE, not id (lib/stats.mjs:84-88): two done tasks sharing a title would both count as overridden, and a task overridden then later re-reviewed to pass is classified gated (overridden requires !gated), skewing the bypass fraction. Untested either way.

No positive-path assertions for the 'no review' bypass bucket (unreviewed is only asserted to be 0), nor for landing.handLanded, review.passes, or audit.red — several reported fields could regress without failing the suite.

The submitted diff contains ONLY .chalk spine files (boards/tasks/updates); lib/stats.mjs, the bin/chalk.mjs wiring, and the locked test test/stats.test.mjs exist in the working tree but are outside the presented diff. Confirm test/stats.test.mjs and lib/stats.mjs are actually tracked/committed on the PR #109 branch — an untracked pinned test is exactly the vacuous-green hole this repo just filed as issue #107 (task-8189ac26).

pipelineLanded (lib/stats.mjs:104) requires t.pr?.number IN ADDITION to pipeline.stage merged/cleaned, while criterion 3 says only 'pipeline stage merged/cleaned'. A task that reached the cleaned stage but lost its pr record would be miscounted as hand-landed. Both fixture tasks carry a pr, so the extra condition is untested either way.

Under --since, events missing an `at` field hit Date.parse(0) → Date.parse('0'), which V8 parses as 2000-01-01 rather than epoch/NaN, so undated events are silently included in windows after 2000. All real emitters set `at`, so this is a defensive-path quirk only.

The prior block's --since falsy hole is properly fixed (`cut !== null`, lib/stats.mjs:49) and garbage input is now rejected at both the CLI (bin/chalk.mjs:899) and computeStats (lib/stats.mjs:46) with a locked test — but the epoch boundary itself (--since 1970-01-01) and the `--json` empty-spine path (prints an all-zero report instead of the friendly message; criterion 5 arguably only covers the human report) are not pinned.

Refactoring run/handoff/done/audit emitters onto lib/markers.mjs preserves the exact legacy strings ('Handoff written:', 'Blocked: … (needs …)', 'Decision: Overrode review gate for "…"', 'Audit green/red'), and the two end-to-end tests (chalk run verify-RED+handoff, chalk done --force-review) now couple emitters to the parser as the amend-spec demanded — drift risk from the earlier review is addressed; residual risk is limited to third-party tooling that greps the old literals, which are unchanged.

title: feat: give reviewer-induced auto-blocks a distinct `--needs` category instead of `human-input`

acceptanceCriteria.text: Add a dedicated `--needs` value (e.g. `review`) to the taxonomy in CLAUDE.md and the block command validation.
Emit reviewer-induced blocks in lib/pipeline.mjs with the new category instead of `human-input`.
`chalk status` / next surface the review block distinctly so it is not confused with a real human dependency.
Add a test asserting a reviewer block sets the review-specific `needs` while a genuine stage failure stays `human-input`.

issue.body:
In lib/pipeline.mjs a failed review (line 69) and a genuinely human-blocking stage failure (line 76) both call `block ... --needs human-input`. Only the free-text reason distinguishes them, so any downstream tooling/triage that routes by `block.needs` treats a reviewer-induced block identically to a credentials/decision/human-input block. A reviewer block is structurally different: it was produced by chalk's own adversarial reviewer, often after a retry, and is the agent's responsibility to address — not a pending human dependency.

- [ ] Add a dedicated `--needs` value (e.g. `review`) to the taxonomy in CLAUDE.md and the block command validation.
- [ ] Emit reviewer-induced blocks in lib/pipeline.mjs with the new category instead of `human-input`.
- [ ] `chalk status` / next surface the review block distinctly so it is not confused with a real human dependency.
- [ ] Add a test asserting a reviewer block sets the review-specific `needs` while a genuine stage failure stays `human-input`.

_filed by `chalk retro` (self-healing)_

findings.note: Criterion 3 explicitly names BOTH `chalk status` and `next`, but only `next` (bin/chalk.mjs:177-181) got the distinct agent-owned rendering. `status` (bin/chalk.mjs:1073) still renders every block with the identical generic shape `⊘ needs <x>: <reason>`, and `backlog` (line 241) likewise — a review block there carries no cue that it is agent-owned rather than a human dependency, which is the exact conflation the task exists to prevent. Criterion 3 is only half-implemented.

The locked test asserts the distinct surfacing only for `chalk next` output; nothing exercises `chalk status` with a review-blocked task. The status half of criterion 3 is therefore both unimplemented and untested — the suite would stay green if status rendering never distinguishes review blocks.

Criterion 1 says add the value to 'the taxonomy in CLAUDE.md'. CLAUDE.md (and the managed template in lib/store.mjs:270) still enumerate the block command as `--needs <creds|decision|human-input|upstream>` — `review` is described in a new bullet but omitted from the actual taxonomy list, and the CLI help text (bin/chalk.mjs:1749) also still omits it. The documented taxonomy is inconsistent with the validation (NEEDS) that now accepts `review`.

pipeline.mjs:84 — a reviewer that ERRORS twice (crash/misconfiguration, no verdict, no findings) now also parks as needs:review, and `chalk next` then instructs 'fix the findings, then chalk review' when there are no findings to fix. A broken reviewer command is plausibly a real config/human dependency; lumping reviewer crashes with reviewer refutations may re-create the same triage conflation in the other direction. The locked test only exercises the verdict:block path, not the reviewer-error path, so this categorization choice is untested either way.

The pipeline's own reviewer-double-ERROR branch (lib/pipeline.mjs:86 — retry fails twice, stays human-input) is not directly exercised; only the run-loop's reviewer-error path (lib/run.mjs:119) is pinned by test 4. If the pipeline branch were flipped to needs:review the suite would still pass. Mitigated by the shared design comment and the run-loop test pinning the crash≠refutation rule, but the pipeline copy is unguarded.

Criterion 3 rendering is asserted for `next` and `status` (matching the criterion text), but the `backlog` review-blocked mark added at bin/chalk.mjs:241 ('⊘ review-blocked (agent-owned)') has no test — that surface could regress to the generic shape without a failure. Outside the literal criterion, so low.

`chalk next` guidance for a review block says 'fix the findings, then `chalk review <id>`', but the task is in state=blocked; if `chalk review` refuses to run on a blocked task the agent must first `chalk unblock`, which the message omits. Verify the re-review path actually works from the blocked state end-to-end (the locked test asserts the message, not the unblock→re-review round trip).

lib/run.mjs blockTask gained an optional `needs` parameter defaulting to 'human-input'; all other call sites (verify-RED, no-criteria, executor failure) keep prior behavior and the verify-RED case is explicitly re-pinned in test 3 — regression risk here looks contained.

title: fix: untrackedLockedTests exempts every .chalk/ pinned path — an e2e spec locked under .chalk/tests/ escapes the tracking gate

acceptanceCriteria.text: Narrow the exemption to spine-state files that genuinely land out-of-band, so pinned e2e specs under `.chalk/tests/` are still tracking-gated.
Locked test asserts the carve-out in BOTH directions: a spine-state pin is exempt, and a `.chalk/tests/*.test.yaml` pin is required to be tracked in git.

untrackedLockedTests narrows the .chalk/ exemption: e2e specs pinned under .chalk/tests/ ARE tracking-gated (must be git-tracked), while genuine out-of-band spine-state paths under .chalk/ stay exempt.

chalk commit stages pinned .chalk/tests/ specs (in addition to code and .chalk/evidence/), so the pipeline tracks e2e contract specs — closing the gap where the narrowed gate would otherwise block on a spec the commit stage never staged.

Locked test asserts the carve-out in BOTH directions: an untracked .chalk/tests/*.test.yaml pin blocks chalk done (and passes once tracked), and an untracked non-tests .chalk/ spine-state pin is exempt.

issue.body:
lib/testgate.mjs:54 filters out every pinned test path starting with `.chalk/` before the git-tracking check, justified by spine state landing out-of-band. But `chalk` also locks e2e specs at `.chalk/tests/<slug>.test.yaml` — those are real contract tests that SHOULD be tracked, and they now get NO tracking gate at all, re-opening exactly the vacuous-green hole #107 closed. Criterion 1 of the tracking task says EVERY locked test path must be verified, and no test pins this carve-out in either direction.

- [ ] Narrow the exemption to spine-state files that genuinely land out-of-band, so pinned e2e specs under `.chalk/tests/` are still tracking-gated.
- [ ] Locked test asserts the carve-out in BOTH directions: a spine-state pin is exempt, and a `.chalk/tests/*.test.yaml` pin is required to be tracked in git.

_filed by `chalk retro` (self-healing)_

findings.note: Diff under review shows only pipeline bookkeeping (board/tasks.json/updates.jsonl), but the working tree contains the actual implementation: lib/testgate.mjs spineStateExempt='p.startsWith(".chalk/") && !p.startsWith(".chalk/tests/")' (crit 1,3) and untrackedLockedTests filters by it; bin/chalk.mjs commit stages .chalk/tests/ at line 370 (crit 4); done gate (line 1368) and pr gate (line 407) both invoke the narrowed gate.

Locked test covers the carve-out in both directions and would fail if the change were reverted: unit assertions on spineStateExempt (line 24-27), done blocks on untracked .chalk/tests/ spec then passes when tracked while the exempt .chalk/mystate.json is ignored (line 53-81), and chalk commit stages/commits the .chalk/tests/ spec while keeping tasks.json out (line 83-102). Coverage is non-vacuous.

title: fix: release --commit/--promote orphan recovery keys on an un-namespaced "Released vX" substring over decisions.md

acceptanceCriteria.text: Match the completion marker namespaced to the specific commit/version (a dedicated marker or structured decision field), not a bare substring over shared prose, so unrelated text can neither spoof nor suppress a resume.
Detect the orphan by version/tag rather than a fixed `log -50` depth, or document and test the bound so a deeper orphan can't silently double-bump.
Locked test: a manual decision note whose body contains "Released vX.Y.Z" does NOT block resuming a genuinely orphaned release commit.

The release completion marker is matched anchored to the '## Released vX' decision HEADING (multiline ^…$), not as a bare substring over decisions.md — so prose in any decision body mentioning 'Released vX' can neither spoof completion nor suppress a legitimate resume.
The orphaned release commit is detected via git's own --grep at ANY depth (not a fixed log -50 window), so a deeply-buried orphan can't silently revert to bump-from-bumped.
A genuine finished release (real ## Released heading + tag) still suppresses the resume — no false resume onto a completed release.
Locked test proves: a decision body mentioning 'Released vX' does not block resuming a genuine orphan, a real heading does, and an orphan buried beyond 50 commits is still found.

issue.body:
The interrupted-release recovery (bin/chalk.mjs ~L528-537) detects an orphaned `chore(release): vX.Y.Z` commit and treats it as already-finished when `new RegExp('Released vX.Y.Z')` matches anywhere in `.chalk/decisions.md`. This completion marker lives OUTSIDE the release commit (which carries only CHANGELOG.md + package.json) and is matched as a bare, un-namespaced substring over the whole log. Two failure modes flagged repeatedly across the #91/#98/#100 release reviews: (1) any manual decision note containing the text "Released vX.Y.Z" suppresses a legitimate resume, so the re-run bumps FROM the already-bumped version and stacks a second release commit (version skip); (2) the orphan scan is a fixed `log -50` window, so an orphan buried deeper silently reverts to bump-from-bumped.

- [ ] Match the completion marker namespaced to the specific commit/version (a dedicated marker or structured decision field), not a bare substring over shared prose, so unrelated text can neither spoof nor suppress a resume.
- [ ] Detect the orphan by version/tag rather than a fixed `log -50` depth, or document and test the bound so a deeper orphan can't silently double-bump.
- [ ] Locked test: a manual decision note whose body contains "Released vX.Y.Z" does NOT block resuming a genuinely orphaned release commit.

_filed by `chalk retro` (self-healing)_

findings.note: Scope creep: the task under review is solely the release orphan-recovery marker fix (#125), but the diff also ships an entirely unrelated feature — issue-intake auto-committing to the base branch via a new gitCommitPaths() in lib/git.mjs and a new behavior in `chalk issue pull` (#114), plus test/intake-commit-scope.test.mjs. This violates 'keep diffs small and scoped to the current task' and bundles unrelated behavior into a release-gated change, which the release-marker acceptance criteria do not cover and its locked test cannot validate.

The bundled #114 change alters `chalk issue pull` to run `git add`/`git commit` on the current (base) branch as a side effect of intake. This is a new, out-of-scope behavioral change to core CLI/git flow (committing on whatever branch the user is on, staging entire .chalk/boards & .chalk/plans dirs). Its only coverage is the author's own new (non-locked) test; it is unrelated to the release-marker criteria and introduces regression surface the release-marker task never contemplated.

The `^## Released vX.Y.Z$` heading match is exact-line-anchored; if appendDecision ever emits a trailing suffix (date, annotation) after the version on the heading line, `$` would fail to match and a genuinely completed release would be re-resumed. The locked test pins the current exact format but there is no tolerance for heading-format drift.

The completion marker is matched as `^## Released vX.Y.Z$` (exact-line anchor). If appendDecision ever appends a suffix to the heading (date, annotation), `$` would fail and a genuinely completed release would be falsely re-resumed. Currently store.mjs writes the heading as exactly `## <title>` so it holds, but there is zero tolerance for heading-format drift — already noted in the task's own review.

Criterion 1 asks for a 'dedicated marker or structured decision field'; the implementation still regex-matches over decisions.md text rather than a structured field. A manual `chalk decision "Released v0.1.0"` (exact title) would render `## Released v0.1.0` and still spoof completion. Criterion 4 explicitly sanctions the heading-anchored approach so this is acceptable, but it is a narrower vector than a truly namespaced marker.

Test 2 (real heading suppresses) is not fully isolating: after a normal `release --commit` the tag v0.1.0 exists, so the `!tagLocal` guard alone suppresses the resume even if the heading match were broken. The heading's unique role (suppressing a completed --no-tag release with no tag) is, however, covered by the existing release-recovery.test.mjs (--no-tag case), so the change is not vacuously passing overall.

reviews.note: locked test amended after review — re-review required

title: fix: passing `chalk review` never clears a needs:review block — the printed guidance omits `chalk unblock`, stranding the task

acceptanceCriteria.text: A passing `chalk review` on a task blocked with `needs:review` auto-unblocks it (restore `blockedFrom`, clear `t.block`), or the review-blocked guidance in next/status/backlog explicitly includes the `chalk unblock` step
Locked test drives the full round trip: run-loop review block → fix → `chalk review` pass → task is runnable again without manual state surgery
`chalk done` succeeds after that round trip (no residual blocked-state gate failure)
A passing chalk review (adversarial or manual) on a task blocked with needs:review auto-unblocks it: restores blockedFrom, clears t.block, and announces it — so runnableTasks stops skipping it.
A non-review block (needs: human-input/creds/decision/upstream) is a real dependency and is NEVER cleared by a passing review.
Locked test drives the full round trip: run-loop review block → fix → chalk review pass → task runnable again → chalk done succeeds, with no manual state surgery.

issue.body:
The run loop auto-blocks a refuted task with `needs:review` (lib/run.mjs:119), and `chalk next`/`chalk status` tell the agent to 'fix the findings, then `chalk review <id>`' (bin/chalk.mjs:180, 1075). But the `review` command (bin/chalk.mjs:1417-1471) never touches `t.state`/`t.block`, and nothing else unblocks on a pass — so a task whose re-review PASSES stays `state=blocked`, `runnableTasks` keeps skipping it, and an agent following the printed guidance exactly can end the sweep with a green-reviewed task still parked. Reviewer flagged the unverified unblock→re-review round trip on #116.

- [ ] A passing `chalk review` on a task blocked with `needs:review` auto-unblocks it (restore `blockedFrom`, clear `t.block`), or the review-blocked guidance in next/status/backlog explicitly includes the `chalk unblock` step
- [ ] Locked test drives the full round trip: run-loop review block → fix → `chalk review` pass → task is runnable again without manual state surgery
- [ ] `chalk done` succeeds after that round trip (no residual blocked-state gate failure)

_filed by `chalk retro` (self-healing)_

findings.note: The supplied diff contains only .chalk bookkeeping (PR metadata in board/tasks/updates); the actual behavior change lives in the working tree at bin/chalk.mjs (clearReviewBlockOnPass, lines 73-80, wired into both the adversarial path line 1479 and the manual --note path line 1455). Inspected the tree per instructions — the implementation is present and correct, not missing.

All six criteria are satisfied: clearReviewBlockOnPass only fires when t.block?.needs==='review', restoring t.state from t.blockedFrom (set by `block` at line 1201) and deleting block/blockedFrom; it is invoked only on verdict==='pass'. A non-review block (needs:human-input/creds/etc.) is correctly left intact. Both paths announce '✓ needs:review block cleared — task is runnable again' (lines 1460/1487), matching the test's /runnable again|unblock|cleared/i assertion.

The locked test drives the full round trip (run-loop review block → fix → review pass → runnable → done), the manual --note path, and the negative case (human-input block NOT cleared). Reverting clearReviewBlockOnPass would leave state=blocked and fail assertions at lines 51-53/74-75 — not a vacuous pass. Coverage is adequate for every criterion including the non-review guard.

title: fix: issue-intake spine writes leak into unrelated task branches — recurring scoped-diff review noise

acceptanceCriteria.text: Issue import commits its spine changes (tasks.json entries, board rows) to the base branch in a dedicated chore(spine) commit before any task branch is cut, or the task commit stage excludes spine entries not belonging to the current task
A task branch's committed diff contains no tasks.json/board entries for other tasks imported during the sweep
Test: fixture runs intake → branch → commit and asserts the task commit touches only the current task's spine entry

The adversarial reviewer's captured diff excludes spine STATE (tasks.json, chalk.json, updates.jsonl, questions.json, decisions.md, lessons.md, boards/, plans/, handoffs/, analysis/) via git pathspec exclusions, so intake's imported-task and board churn never reaches the reviewer.
Contract artifacts stay visible to the reviewer: the code change and pinned .chalk/tests/ e2e specs (and .chalk/evidence/) are NOT excluded.
The exclusion applies to every captureDiff fallback (git diff HEAD, base...HEAD, origin/base...HEAD, git diff) and to the --stat file list, in both manual and pipeline order.
Locked test proves the reviewer's prompt carries the code + a .chalk/tests/ spec but not tasks.json/board rows/other imported task titles.

issue.body:
Four reviews in this sweep (release --promote, release --commit recovery, review-stage fix, cost ledger) each flagged the same design-intent finding: the task's diff bundles unrelated queue metadata — imported issue task specs and board rows written during intake — violating chalk's own 'keep diffs small and scoped' hard rule and burning reviewer attention every run. Intake mutates .chalk/tasks.json/board while that state is later swept into whichever task branch commits next.

- [ ] Issue import commits its spine changes (tasks.json entries, board rows) to the base branch in a dedicated chore(spine) commit before any task branch is cut, or the task commit stage excludes spine entries not belonging to the current task
- [ ] A task branch's committed diff contains no tasks.json/board entries for other tasks imported during the sweep
- [ ] Test: fixture runs intake → branch → commit and asserts the task commit touches only the current task's spine entry

_filed by `chalk retro` (self-healing)_

findings.note: Criteria 1 & 2 are unmet. The task contract requires the ROOT-cause fix: issue import commits spine changes in a dedicated chore(spine) commit before task branches are cut, OR the task-commit stage excludes non-current-task spine entries — and 'A task branch's committed diff contains no tasks.json/board entries for other tasks.' The change touches only lib/review.mjs captureDiff; it masks spine churn from the REVIEWER's view but leaves the actual committed branch diff exactly as leaky as before. The committed history still bundles unrelated imported-task/board entries, so criterion 2 (committed diff) is not satisfied.

Criterion 3 mandates a test that 'runs intake → branch → commit and asserts the task commit touches only the current task's spine entry.' No such test exists — the only locked test (review-diff-scope.test.mjs) exercises the reviewer prompt, never intake/branch/commit. The commit-scoping behavior demanded by criteria 1-3 ships with zero test coverage (vacuous pass).

Criterion 6 requires the exclusion to hold 'in both manual and pipeline order.' The test only covers manual mode (uncommitted tasks.json via git diff HEAD). The pipeline path — change committed on-branch so git diff HEAD is empty and it falls through to `git diff <base>...HEAD` — is never asserted; that fallback would still pass if the pathspec were reverted for that branch.

The stated goal (issue #114) is that spine writes leak into unrelated task branches, violating 'keep diffs small and scoped.' Hiding the leak from the adversarial reviewer solves the symptom (review noise) while leaving the underlying scoped-diff violation in the committed branches intact — arguably solving the wrong problem relative to criteria 1-3.

The intake commit stages spine files with `gitAdd(spineFiles)` but then calls `gitCommit`, which runs a bare `git commit -m ...` (lib/git.mjs:77-79) with NO pathspec — it commits the ENTIRE staged index. If a user has ANY pre-staged changes when they run `chalk issue pull` (staged but not yet committed code), those changes are swept into the auto-generated `chore(spine)` commit on the base branch. This directly contradicts the code's own explicit safety claim ("Scoped: only the spine files intake touched, never `git add -A`, so a user's other uncommitted work is untouched"). The `diff --cached --name-only` guard only checks whether the index is non-empty, then commits all of it. This is a real workflow/data hazard: unrelated user work gets committed to base under a misleading message.

intake-commit-scope.test.mjs only exercises a clean index before `issue pull` (test 1 asserts the commit touches only `.chalk/` files, but the repo has nothing else staged). No test stages an unrelated file before intake to prove the scoping guarantee the comment makes. The 'touches ONLY spine files, never code' assertion would still pass in the tested scenario even though the implementation would sweep pre-staged code in a real one — the test does not actually exercise the scoping claim's failure mode.

Criterion 1 requires the intake commit before any task branch is cut; this holds in worktree-disabled mode (the tests force `worktree.enabled=false`), but with worktrees enabled by default the interaction of committing to base at pull time vs. later branch creation is not exercised by any locked test, leaving the default-mode path unverified.

Criterion 6 requires the pathspec exclusion to apply to every captureDiff fallback (git diff HEAD, base...HEAD, origin/base...HEAD, git diff) in both manual and pipeline order. review-diff-scope.test.mjs only exercises the manual 'git diff HEAD' path (uncommitted staged changes); the pipeline path (committed-on-branch base...HEAD / origin/base...HEAD) is not directly asserted. Coverage is not vacuous, however: exclusions are a single shared `diffPathspec` constant appended to all four fallbacks and the --stat, and the REVIEW_DIFF_EXCLUDES unit test plus the integration test both fail if the exclusion is reverted.

The intake commit's spineFiles list (.chalk/tasks.json, updates.jsonl, boards, plans) is a subset of the reviewer's exclude list (which also covers chalk.json, questions.json, decisions.md, lessons.md, handoffs, analysis). If a future intake path dirties one of those un-committed spine files, it would float in the working tree again. Currently benign — intake only writes tasks.json/updates.jsonl/boards, and the locked test asserts a clean tree — but the two lists diverging is a latent maintenance hazard.

`chalk issue pull` now auto-creates a chore(spine) commit on the current (base) branch where it previously left changes uncommitted. Behavior is intended per criterion 1 and best-effort guarded (rev-parse check + try/catch, empty-commit skip, partial `git commit -- <pathspec>` leaving user's pre-staged work intact, all covered by intake-commit-scope tests incl. the non-git and pre-staged cases), but callers/pipelines that assumed intake left the spine uncommitted now see a new base-branch commit.

title: fix: chalk spec --test from a linked worktree records a '../<worktree>/…' lock path — dead after cleanup

acceptanceCriteria.text: chalk spec --test <path> and chalk amend-spec --test <path> invoked from a linked git worktree record the lock 'path' relative to the worktree's copy of the project root (tree-relative, e.g. test/x.mjs) — never a '../<worktree>/…' path that points into the worktree and dies after chalk merge cleans it up

issue.body:
## What happened

Dogfooding on `chalkagents/chalk-protocol-site` (issue #6 there): the reviewer blocked with "the test is not registered as a locked test", so — per the finding — I ran the sanctioned path from the task's **worktree** (so the file exists at the cwd):

```
cd ../chalk-protocol-site-feat-6-…   # the task worktree
chalk spec task-13052f3 --test test/docs-pages.test.mjs
  locked ../chalk-protocol-site-feat-6-feat-build-time-docs-rendering/test/docs-pages.test.mjs @ 15892a308f4b
```

The lock recorded `path: "../chalk-protocol-site-feat-6-…/test/docs-pages.test.mjs"` — relative to the canonical spine root (the #52 single-canonical-spine resolution works), but pointing INTO the worktree. After `chalk merge` cleans the worktree up, the recorded path is dead: integrity/break-it checks against it will ENOENT even though `test/docs-pages.test.mjs` exists on main.

## Where

`bin/chalk.mjs` spec/amend-spec: `s.lockTest(resolve(process.cwd(), String(p)))` — the abs path is later relativized against `store.root` (main checkout), so a cwd inside a linked worktree produces a `../<worktree>/…` path.

## Expected

When cwd is a linked worktree of the canonical root, the lock path should be recorded relative to the **worktree root** (i.e. `test/docs-pages.test.mjs`), which is the tree-relative path valid in every checkout. `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` from cwd (or comparing against `workdir(store, task)`) gives the right base.

## Workaround used

Normalized the recorded path by hand (same sha) + `chalk decision` documenting it.

## Related

The same dogfood run also reproduced #102's stage-marker friction in a new spot: after a manual review-fix round (manual commit+push, review PASS), the resumed `chalk pipeline` re-ran `work` (executor no-op, attempts++) and then FAILED at `commit` with "nothing to commit — the executor made no file changes", auto-blocking a task whose PR was already pushed, recorded, and LGTM'd. A clean tree + an existing recorded PR should advance the stage, not block. Happy to split this into its own issue if it shouldn't ride on #102.

findings.note: Criterion 3's monorepo-subdir clause is only exercised for the trivial case where the project root equals the git top-level (test 2 uses no subdir). The new offset computation (`offset = relative(wt.mainRoot, this.root)` then `resolve(wt.toplevel, offset)`) only does non-trivial work when a chalk project lives in a monorepo subdir INSIDE a linked worktree, and no test covers that path. The logic reads correct (offset direction main→worktree yields tree-relative), but it ships unverified.

lockBase relies on `this.root` already being the canonical MAIN-checkout project root (via findRoot's worktree→main redirect). In a monorepo worktree without a committed .chalk, findRoot may fail to redirect and this.root would be the worktree's own root, making `offset` degenerate; the redirect+lockBase interaction is not jointly tested. Non-blocking as the tested non-monorepo flow works end-to-end.

The core changed behavior (worktree cwd → tree-relative lock path, no '../<worktree>/…') is asserted by test 1 with assertions that fail on revert (path=='test/foo.test.mjs', !startsWith('..'), !includes(worktree basename)) plus brokenLocks==[] under the canonical root, so criteria 1 and 2 are non-vacuously covered.

title: feat: parallel task execution — scope P6 integrity per worktree, lock spine writes, fan out the driver

acceptanceCriteria.text: verify() checks each in-progress task's locked tests against THAT task's own worktree (task.worktree, falling back to store.root) instead of one shared cwd — so a second in-progress task on its own branch no longer trips a false P6 integrity break in the first task's checkout
Single in-progress task behavior is unchanged: when the task's worktree equals the verify cwd (the common case), the integrity result is byte-identical to today

The opt-in all-locks DONE-task integrity check still runs against the verify cwd (the current worktree), preserving the #80 anti-cheat that catches the current task weakening an already-done task's locked test

issue.body:
**From the 2026-07-06 dogfood sweeps.** Chalk's one-in-progress-task-at-a-time is a soft convention with one hard tooth, and it forces whole-repo sequential sweeps even when tasks are independent.

## What actually enforces sequential today

- `chalk start` does NOT refuse a second in-progress task; `chalk next` only warns (`protocol prefers ONE at a time`).
- The hard tooth is **P6**: `verify()` (lib/verify.mjs:39) checks EVERY in-progress task's locked tests against a SINGLE cwd. Two tasks in-progress on different branches → each checkout is missing the other task's locked test (or has a stale sha) → `brokenLocks` fires → verify RED for both. Worktrees isolate the *edits* but not the *integrity check*.
- The `chalk verify` CLI picks the FIRST in-progress task (`tasks().find(...)`, bin/chalk.mjs) to choose the worktree — wrong cwd for any second task.
- The Store writes the spine with plain `writeFileSync` — two concurrent chalk processes in the same repo race on tasks.json/updates.jsonl (last writer wins, events can interleave mid-line).
- `runDriver`/`runPipeline` are sequential for-loops over the queue.

(Parallel across DIFFERENT repos already works fine — each spine is independent.)

## Sketch

1. **Scope P6 per task**: check each in-progress task's locked tests in *its own* worktree (task.worktree, falling back to root). A task without a worktree in multi-mode is the error case.
2. **Spine write safety**: a lockfile (or O_APPEND-only event log + per-task json) so concurrent `chalk work`/`verify`/`done` don't clobber tasks.json.
3. **Driver fan-out**: `chalk pipeline --parallel N` — spawn per-task stage chains (branch→work→…→merge) in their own worktrees; merges still serialize through the gate (they contend on the base branch anyway).
4. Make the one-at-a-time preference explicit: `chalk start` refuses a second wip task unless `protocol.parallel.enabled` (or `--parallel`), instead of today's silent allow + downstream RED.

Until then the documented answer stays: one task in flight per repo, queue the rest (`chalk next` order).

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

findings.note: workdir() falls back to store.root, so an in-progress task with NO worktree field verified under an explicit non-root cwd would now hash at store.root instead of cwd — a behavior change vs. today. But this only diverges outside criterion 2's stated condition (worktree==cwd) and the pipeline always sets task.worktree when running in a worktree, so it's benign; not a violation of the contract.

Criterion 2 (single in-progress task, worktree==cwd → byte-identical) is not asserted by a dedicated test; it is only implied by the workdir fallback. However tests 1-3 each map to and discriminate criteria 1, genuine-break, and 3, and test 1 would fail if the change were reverted, so the core behavior change is covered.
Change is minimal, scoped, and directly implements per-worktree P6 scoping while keeping the #80 done-task all-locks anti-cheat at cwd (line 57). Matches the stated goal.

title: fix: chalk commit silently no-ops after the first commit, so review-fix changes never get committed

acceptanceCriteria.text: chalk commit commits new working-tree code changes even past the 'committed' stage (labeled follow-up), so review-fix changes land in git.
It no-ops idempotently when there is nothing new; the first commit still errors when the executor produced no changes.
After a follow-up commit no uncommitted CODE lingers — reviewer's view equals what merge takes.
Locked test proves first commit, follow-up landing, idempotent re-run, and empty-first-commit failure.

issue.body:
**Discovered while landing #114/#125.** `chalk commit` guards on `stageDone(t, 'committed')` and returns `ok('commit (already done)')` if the task's pipeline stage is at/after `committed`. But the review→fix loop routinely makes MORE code changes AFTER the first commit (to address a review BLOCK). On the next `chalk commit`, it no-ops — the fix changes stay uncommitted in the working tree.

**Real failure:** #114's review-round-2 fix (gitCommitPaths + intake commit + scoping test) was made after the first commit. `chalk commit` no-op'd; I committed only the spine manually; the code fix never reached the fix/114 branch and was squash-merged away. #114 shipped with only its round-1 half. The adversarial review PASSED because captureDiff shows uncommitted working-tree changes (`git diff HEAD`), so the reviewer saw the fix — but the MERGE only took committed changes. Required a manual split (#133 + rescoped #132) to recover.

**Fix options:**
- `chalk commit` should re-commit new working-tree changes when the branch has uncommitted code (amend or a follow-up commit), not silently no-op; OR
- loudly WARN when `chalk commit` is a no-op but the working tree has uncommitted code changes ('N files changed since the last commit — git add + commit them, or they won't land').

The mismatch between what the reviewer sees (working tree) and what merge takes (committed) is the deeper hazard — a green review can certify code that never lands.

title: refactor: unify the intake-commit spine paths and the reviewer diff-exclude list into one shared constant

acceptanceCriteria.text: Define the spine-state path list once in a shared module imported by both bin/chalk.mjs (intake commit) and lib/review.mjs (diff excludes)
Ensure the intake commit covers every spine path the reviewer excludes (contract artifacts like `.chalk/tests/` and `.chalk/evidence/` remain visible/committed as today)
Add a test asserting the intake-commit path set and the reviewer-exclude set stay consistent, so a future divergence trips the suite

issue.body:
`chalk issue pull` commits a hardcoded `spineFiles` list (`.chalk/tasks.json`, `.chalk/updates.jsonl`, `.chalk/boards`, `.chalk/plans`) in bin/chalk.mjs:337, while the reviewer excludes a *superset* of spine paths via `REVIEW_DIFF_EXCLUDES` in lib/review.mjs:66 (also `.chalk/chalk.json`, `.chalk/questions.json`, `.chalk/decisions.md`, `.chalk/lessons.md`, `.chalk/handoffs`, `.chalk/analysis`).

Because the intake list is a subset, any future intake path that dirties a spine file NOT in `spineFiles` (e.g. `chalk.json` or `questions.json`) is left uncommitted by intake yet excluded from the review diff — so it floats in the working tree and bundles into the next task branch, re-introducing exactly the scoped-diff leak #114 fixed. The two lists silently diverging is a latent maintenance hazard the #130 review flagged.

- [ ] Define the spine-state path list once in a shared module imported by both bin/chalk.mjs (intake commit) and lib/review.mjs (diff excludes)
- [ ] Ensure the intake commit covers every spine path the reviewer excludes (contract artifacts like `.chalk/tests/` and `.chalk/evidence/` remain visible/committed as today)
- [ ] Add a test asserting the intake-commit path set and the reviewer-exclude set stay consistent, so a future divergence trips the suite

_filed by `chalk retro` (self-healing)_

findings.note: Intake now commits additional spine paths not previously committed (chalk.json, questions.json, decisions.md, lessons.md, handoffs, analysis). If a user has manually-edited uncommitted `.chalk/chalk.json` at `chalk issue pull` time, those config edits would now be swept into the chore(spine) commit via `git commit -- <paths>`. This is consistent with the stated 'chalk owns spine state' intent, but is a behavior change not directly exercised by a runtime test (only tasks.json/boards/updates are actually written during pull in the fixtures).

The consistency test (test/spine-paths-consistency.test.mjs) pins REVIEW_DIFF_EXCLUDES == SPINE_STATE_PATHS wrapped, which is somewhat tautological given review.mjs literally maps the constant — its real value is the source-scan guard forbidding a re-hardcoded `.chalk/` list on the spineFiles line. No test functionally asserts that intake commits e.g. questions.json/chalk.json specifically; coverage rests on the structural constant-sharing plus the pre-existing 'working tree clean after intake' check. Adequate but indirect for criterion 2.

title: fix: untrackedLockedTests compares pinned paths verbatim against git ls-files — a './'-prefixed, backslashed, or case-differing pin false-blocks done/pr

acceptanceCriteria.text: Normalize both the pinned path and each `ls-files` entry before comparison (strip a leading `./`, unify path separators) so equivalent forms match
Handle case-insensitive filesystems so a case-only difference does not false-block (or document the platform boundary)
Add a locked test: a tracked file pinned as `./<path>` (and a backslash/case variant) is NOT reported untracked and `chalk done` proceeds
Keep the genuinely-untracked case still blocking (no regression to the #107 vacuous-green guard)

issue.body:
`untrackedLockedTests` (lib/testgate.mjs:65) does `pinned.filter(p => !tracked.has(p))` where `tracked` is the raw `git ls-files -z` output. Because it is exact string equality with no normalization, a locked test whose pinned path is written as `./contract.test.mjs`, uses backslashes on Windows, or differs only in case on a case-insensitive filesystem is reported as untracked even though git tracks it — a false block on `chalk done`/`chalk pr` that strands an otherwise-shippable task. The tracking gate should only ever fire on a genuinely untracked file.

- [ ] Normalize both the pinned path and each `ls-files` entry before comparison (strip a leading `./`, unify path separators) so equivalent forms match
- [ ] Handle case-insensitive filesystems so a case-only difference does not false-block (or document the platform boundary)
- [ ] Add a locked test: a tracked file pinned as `./<path>` (and a backslash/case variant) is NOT reported untracked and `chalk done` proceeds
- [ ] Keep the genuinely-untracked case still blocking (no regression to the #107 vacuous-green guard)

_filed by `chalk retro` (self-healing)_

findings.note: Criterion 3 names a backslash variant; the end-to-end `chalk done` proceeds path is only asserted for `./`-prefix and case variants. Backslash is covered only via the normTrackPath unit assertion (normTrackPath('./a\\b.mjs')===normTrackPath('a/b.mjs')). Acceptable since untrackedLockedTests normalizes both sides through that same shared helper, but no full-loop backslash assertion exists (a POSIX git tree can't track a backslash-separated file, so this is inherently unit-level).

Backslash→'/' unification is unconditional even on POSIX, where a literal backslash is a valid filename character; a pinned `a\b` could then spuriously match a tracked `a/b`, weakening the #107 guard in that pathological case. Extremely unlikely in practice for pinned test paths, so non-blocking.

case-insensitivity keys solely off `git config core.ignorecase`. If a user's repo has it unset/false on an ignorecase FS, a case-only pin would still false-block; the change documents this as the platform boundary (criterion 2 permits documentation), so acceptable. Revert-sensitivity confirmed: the `./`-pin and case tests both fail if the normalization is reverted, so the change is genuinely covered.

title: feat: spine write safety — atomic tasks.json writes + append-only event log so concurrent chalk processes don't clobber the spine (#110 slice 2)

acceptanceCriteria.text: Concurrent chalk processes mutating tasks.json via upsertTask do not lose updates: the read-modify-write runs under a cross-process advisory lock and RE-READS inside it, so N concurrent adds of distinct tasks all survive (no last-writer-wins clobber)
Spine JSON writes are atomic (temp file + rename): a concurrent reader always sees a complete valid file, and no .tmp residue is left after a successful write

The lock self-heals and stays out of the repo: a crashed holder's stale lock (older than the threshold) is stolen so a dead process cannot wedge the spine; the .lock and atomic-write temp files are gitignored

findings.note: Criterion 3 (lock self-heals: a stale lock older than LOCK_STALE_MS is stolen) has NO test in the locked suite. The entire stale-steal branch in withLock (statSync mtime > LOCK_STALE_MS → unlinkSync → continue) could be deleted and both locked tests would still pass. A crashed-holder scenario is never simulated. Feature shipped with no covering assertion — vacuous pass per the hard rule.

Criterion 3 also requires the .lock and atomic-write temp files be gitignored. No test asserts .gitignore ignores .chalk/.lock or the tasks.json.<pid>.tmp temp pattern. The gitignore change is untested behavior.

Stale-lock steal has a TOCTOU race: process A stats an old mtime and decides stale, but between stat and unlinkSync another process B may have already stolen and recreated a FRESH lock; A then unlinks B's live lock, allowing a third process to acquire concurrently — two holders, the exact clobber the lock is meant to prevent. Only fires near the 30s threshold and is untested, but it defeats the self-heal guarantee under contention.

The lock only guards upsertTask. lib/archive.mjs:82 does a read-modify-write via store.saveTasks(store.tasks().filter(...)) OUTSIDE the lock. A concurrent `chalk archive` and `upsertTask` still race with last-writer-wins on tasks.json — the criterion's spine-safety goal is not fully met for all mutators, and no test covers archive concurrency.

Test 2 ('no .tmp residue / valid JSON') does not actually exercise the torn-read window: because upsertTask serializes writes under the lock, temp collisions can't occur regardless, and the test never reads tasks.json mid-write. It is a weak proxy for the atomicity claim in criterion 2 (concurrent reader always sees a complete file).

gitignore adds redundant `.chalk/*.tmp.*` but the actual temp name is `tasks.json.<pid>.tmp` (ends in .tmp); the extra pattern is dead. Harmless, but signals the ignore rules weren't verified against the real temp filename.

Criterion 2 (atomic temp+rename writes) is not actually pinned by any locked test. Reverting writeJSON to a plain writeFileSync would leave the entire suite green: test 'atomic writes leave no .tmp residue' asserts stray===[] and valid JSON, but with a plain writeFileSync NO temp file is ever created, so the residue check passes trivially, and after all serialized writes complete the file is valid JSON either way. Because the lock (test 1) serializes writes, a torn-read window never occurs regardless of atomicity, so no assertion distinguishes atomic-write from non-atomic-write. The core behavior of criterion 2 ships without a failing-on-revert test.

Criterion 2 claims 'a concurrent reader always sees a complete valid file', but no test ever spawns a reader that reads tasks.json DURING a write. The atomicity guarantee is asserted only by proxy (post-hoc validity + no residue), neither of which exercises the truncate-then-write window a plain write would expose.

withLock is best-effort: after LOCK_WAIT_MS (15s) it proceeds UNLOCKED (fd===null) and then its finally block does not unlink the lock. Under sustained real contention a process could write outside the lock and still clobber a concurrent upsert — the exact last-writer-wins failure criterion 1 aims to eliminate. Unlikely in the 16-process test (each holds the lock for ms), so untested, but it means criterion 1's guarantee is conditional, not absolute.

writeJSON is now atomic for ALL callers (chalk.json, questions.json, spine.hashes.json, initSpine), broadening the change beyond the stated tasks.json scope. Benign/likely-improving, but it is behavior change to unrelated write paths with no dedicated coverage.

Criterion 3 (lock artifacts stay out of the repo): the stale-steal path renames the lock to `.chalk/.lock.stale.<pid>.<ts>` then unlinks it. That intermediate name matches neither the gitignore entry `.chalk/.lock` (exact) nor `.chalk/*.tmp` (needs .tmp suffix). In the normal path it is unlinked immediately, but a crash between renameSync and unlinkSync would leave an un-gitignored artifact in the repo. Narrow window, not covered by any test.

withLock is best-effort: after LOCK_WAIT_MS (15s) it proceeds UNLOCKED, which under pathological contention could reintroduce the last-writer-wins clobber criterion 1 forbids. This is a deliberate anti-deadlock backstop and is not reachable by the fast operations the tests exercise, so no test covers the unlocked fallback path.

writeJSON is now temp+rename for ALL spine writes (saveMeta, saveQuestions, initSpine, archive files), not just tasks.json. rename(2) requires same-filesystem sibling temp (satisfied here). No behavioral regression observed; sleepSync degrades to a busy-spin only if SharedArrayBuffer is unavailable (documented, functionally harmless).

Tests genuinely exercise the change and are non-vacuous (reverting the lock/atomic-write would fail the concurrent-adds and torn-read tests; reverting the archive routing would leave the stale lock, failing the archive test). All three criteria have direct assertions. Adequate.

title: feat: chalk start refuses a second in-progress task unless protocol.parallel.enabled — make the one-at-a-time convention a hard gate (#110 slice 4)

acceptanceCriteria.text: chalk start <id> refuses with a non-zero exit when another task is already in-progress and parallel mode is off; the task is NOT moved to in-progress, and the error names the blocking task and how to opt in
With protocol.parallel.enabled=true (or the --parallel flag) chalk start allows a second concurrent in-progress task
The gate does not fire when there is no other in-progress task (starting the first task) nor when re-running start on the already-in-progress task itself

findings.note: Tests cover all three criteria (refuse+no-move+names blocker+parallel word, config opt-in, --parallel flag, first-task and same-task no-fire). title: feat: chalk pipeline --parallel N — fan out per-task stage chains in worktrees, serialize merges at the gate (#110 slice 3)

acceptanceCriteria.text: chalk pipeline --parallel N runs up to N per-task chains (branch..evidence) concurrently, each in its own worktree, and never exceeds N in flight; every queued issue-backed task is chained (none dropped by the pool)

Merges are SERIALIZED — never concurrent — because they squash onto the shared base branch and contend; a chain that reaches the merge point cleanly is merged, and the git/gh stage runners are injectable so these invariants are testable without a live repo
A chain that blocks (non-zero) is NOT merged and is reported blocked; a merge that fails blocks that task; the sequential chalk pipeline (no --parallel) path is unchanged

findings.note: Every locked test injects both runChain and runMerge, so the entire DEFAULT production path is untested: defaultRunChain (spawn `pipeline --only <id> --stop-before merge`), defaultRunMerge (`chalk merge`), and the new `stopBefore` truncation in runPipeline. The invariant that chains actually stop before merge and that merges are serialized via a separate `chalk merge` step hinges on stopBefore — yet reverting the stopBefore logic (or having merge run inside the chain) would leave the suite fully green. The real mechanism satisfying criterion 2 has no coverage.

runPipeline's `--only` filter was widened from exact `t.id === only` to `t.id === only || t.id.startsWith(only)`. defaultRunChain passes the FULL id, but with prefix ids like `task-1`/`task-12`, `'task-12'.startsWith('task-1')` is true — so a single chain subprocess would run a sibling task's full chain too. That both double-runs a task and executes work outside the pool, violating criterion 1's 'never exceeds N in flight' and 'each in its own chain/worktree'. Untested.

The same `--only` startsWith broadening changes existing sequential `chalk pipeline --only <id>` behavior (previously exact match) with no test guarding it; any prefix-colliding task ids now get swept into a run that was expected to touch a single task.

Criterion 1 requires each chain run 'in its own worktree,' but defaultRunChain spawns every chain with `cwd: store.root` — a shared checkout — with no worktree creation in this diff. The comment asserts safety 'because of earlier slices,' but nothing here demonstrates per-task worktree isolation; concurrent chains in the same cwd could clobber each other's working tree. This is neither implemented in-diff nor tested.

The CLI wiring in bin/chalk.mjs (--parallel default of 4, `=== true ? 4 : Number()||4` parsing, exit-code 2 on blocked, summary output, and the new top-level `await Promise.resolve(fn())`) is entirely unexercised by tests.

The CLI glue in bin/chalk.mjs (the `--parallel N` flag parsing incl. `--parallel` bare→4 and `Number(flags.parallel)||4` defaulting, the parallel summary line, syncBrowser call, and `process.exit(2)` on blocked) is new behavior with no locked test — the suite exercises runPipelineParallel/runPipeline directly. Core invariants are covered, but the flag-to-function wiring and exit-code contract are unverified.

bin/chalk.mjs now wraps every command dispatch in `await Promise.resolve(fn(parsed))`, converting the whole CLI entrypoint to top-level await. Reviewed as safe (sync throws still propagate inside the try; sync returns unaffected), but it is a broad change touching all commands, not just the pipeline, and no test asserts sync-command error handling is unchanged.

The parallel queue filter (issue && !done && !blocked) ignores inter-task dependency ordering, so `--parallel` can fan out and merge a dependent task before its prerequisite. This mirrors the existing sequential runPipeline behavior (not a regression introduced here) and the slice-3 criteria don't require dep-ordering, but #110's stated dep-honoring semantics are not preserved by the parallel driver.

Per-worktree isolation of concurrent chains and cross-process tasks.json safety are asserted only by comments and depend on prior slices (branch-stage worktreeAdd + spine lock); the locked tests inject runners and thus never exercise real concurrent worktree/spine contention. Verified branch/commit/work stages do target workdir(store,t), so the design holds, but the concurrency-safety of the default production path is untested.

title: fix: vacuous verify trap — empty protocol.verify auto-passes P4; tighten chalk doctor to a blocker (#152)

acceptanceCriteria.text: chalk doctor reports a blocking 'fail' when protocol.verify has NO configured gate AND there is a runnable task — even if that task HAS a locked test (an empty verify never runs it, so P4 passes vacuously). Softened to 'warn' when an adversarial reviewer gate is configured (the backstop)
The empty-verify blocker makes chalk doctor exit non-zero and autopilot (which gates on doctor 'fail' findings) refuse — so an unattended run cannot silently complete tasks against a vacuous verify
A project WITH a configured protocol.verify gate produces no such finding (no false positive); the check is independent of the existing per-task testless check

findings.note: The new 'gates' blocker fires for ANY project with a runnable task and an empty protocol.verify (default `chalk init` without a preset). This is the intended behavior per #152, and the one affected editable test (pipeline.test.mjs) was updated to add a verify command, but the change now makes doctor exit non-zero for any bare-init repo with a runnable task — worth confirming no other suites depend on the old permissive doctor. verify is the gate for that.

verifyConfigured uses normGate(v).cmd across Object.values(proto.verify); an entry with an empty command string ({test:''}) is correctly treated as vacuous, and a configured {test:'...'} correctly suppresses the finding. Locked tests cover fail (no reviewer), warn (reviewer backstop), no-false-positive (configured verify), independence from the testless check, and real-CLI non-zero exit — all three criteria are asserted and autopilot gates on level:'fail'. Adequate.

title: fix: review diff-capture silently passes on no diff — abort loudly instead of a vacuous verdict (#151)

A review WITH a real (non-empty) diff is unaffected — the normal pass/block flow and recorded verdict are unchanged

findings.note: The EMPTY_TREE (git diff <empty-tree> HEAD) fallback means no-diff is only reachable when HEAD is unborn/no commits; any repo with committed content will render the whole tree as additions rather than aborting. This is intentional and is in fact locked by test 2 (a committed change with no base delta MUST be reviewed, not aborted), so it aligns with the contract — but it does narrow the abort to the unborn-HEAD case, so a misconfigured base on a populated branch reviews the whole repo instead of aborting. Acceptable given the locked spec, noting the boundary.

Criterion 1's no-diff abort is exercised only via the unborn-HEAD path (nothing committed).
