title: fix: merge ff-pull failure strands a stale base — chalk branch cuts from the fresh remote base (#150)

acceptanceCriteria.text: chalk branch cuts the new worktree from the FRESH remote base (origin/<base>, after a best-effort fetch), so a stale local base (behind the remote — e.g. after a failed merge pull --ff-only) does not strand the next task on old code: the worktree contains the remote's latest commits

When origin/<base> cannot be resolved (no remote / offline), branch falls back to the local base and warns if a remote exists — never SILENTLY stale; the merge itself still completes (remote is source of truth), unchanged
The normal case (local base already current) is unaffected — the worktree is cut from the base tip as before

findings.note: Criterion 2's second clause — 'when origin/<base> cannot be resolved but a remote EXISTS, fall back to local base AND warn (never silently stale)' — is entirely untested. Test 2 covers only the NO-remote case (currentRepo null, no warning). The 'remote exists but unresolvable/offline' branch (the console.warn on line 376) has no assertion; reverting that line/branch leaves both locked tests green. That is a vacuous pass for the warning contract.

The warning is gated on currentRepo(s.root), which only detects a parseable origin remote URL. A remote under a non-'origin' name, or an origin URL that fails the owner/repo regex, yields currentRepo()===null → no warning → SILENTLY stale, contradicting criterion 2's 'warns if a remote exists'. A `git remote` presence check would match the criterion more faithfully.

`fetch origin ${base}` is best-effort (swallowed by gitTry) but no test forces the fetch-fails-yet-origin-ref-exists path; if a prior stale origin/<base> ref exists and fetch fails, branch would cut from a stale remote-tracking ref while reporting success — a plausible edge not exercised.

branch now always cuts from origin/<base> when it resolves. If the local base were ever AHEAD of the remote (unpushed local commits on main), the new worktree would silently drop them. Chalk's workflow never commits to main locally (all work goes through PR worktrees), so this is out of scope of the criteria, but it is an unguarded edge the tests don't cover.

`git fetch origin ${base}` and `rev-parse origin/${base}` interpolate the configured base unquoted (worktreeAdd itself quotes via q()). Harmless for the canonical 'main' base and consistent with the spec's origin/<base> wording, but a base value with shell-special chars would be mishandled.

Test 3 (no remote) would still pass if the change were reverted (fileA is present with or without the patch). The load-bearing coverage comes from Test 1 (fileB recovery fails on revert) and Test 2 (warning fails on revert), which do pin the added behavior — so the suite is not vacuous, but the no-remote path is only weakly asserted (no explicit assertion that NO warning/fetch-crash occurs).

title: feat: spine/protocol migration — stamp writer version, detect skew on open, gated chalk migrate (#159)

acceptanceCriteria.text: Opening a spine stamped with a NEWER chalk-protocol version than the running binary is REFUSED (non-zero exit, a clear upgrade message) rather than silently misread — enforced in Store.open via spineSkew

chalk migrate carries an old-schema spine (pre-writerVersion, version 1.0) forward to the current schema, is IDEMPOTENT on re-run (no-op when already current), backs the spine up before mutating, and --dry-run mutates NOTHING
A same-version (compatible) spine opens with NO migration prompt and NO mutation of chalk.json; chalk doctor surfaces skew (fail for newer, warn for needs-migrate)

findings.note: doctor.mjs adds a `fail`-for-newer branch, but it is effectively unreachable via the CLI: Store.open throws on a newer spine before runDoctor executes. The locked test even acknowledges this ('the refusal IS the surfaced skew'). Reverting just that doctor line would leave all tests green — it is untested defensive code. Criterion 3's literal 'chalk doctor surfaces skew (fail for newer)' is satisfied only by the open-time refusal, not by doctor itself.

saveMeta now stamps writerVersion (and continues to bump updatedAt) on EVERY spine write, and initSpine bumps version 1.0→1.1. Any existing test or consumer doing an exact-snapshot deepEqual of chalk.json could break; the visible suite does not appear to, but the held-out set cannot be inspected. Low risk given the field is additive.

Store.open is now invoked twice per command (warnSpineTamper swallows the newer-skew throw, then the command handler re-throws it). Behavior is correct — the refusal still surfaces with exit 1 and the writer version — but the swallow in warnSpineTamper means the skew guard relies on the command handler also calling Store.open; a command that skips Store.open would bypass the refusal. All tested commands (status/doctor/migrate) do call it.

title: feat: chalk stats --public — PII-free shareable gate-efficacy artifact (markdown + shields badge) (#156)

acceptanceCriteria.text: chalk stats --public emits a PII-FREE markdown summary carrying the efficacy headline (gate catches, tasks reviewed, block/pass verdicts, self-report↔gate disagreement rate, verify-RED blocks, gated-landing fraction, held-out audit) and NO task titles, file paths, or task ids (the churn 'worst' list is excluded)

The public summary is derived purely from computeStats (deterministic for a fixed spine fixture, no new tracking) and README documents it as the social-proof block

findings.note: disagreementRate is defined as caught/reviewed (blocked-then-passed), which understates true self-report↔gate disagreement: a task blocked but not yet re-passed is a disagreement yet is excluded. Matches the locked test's 50% expectation, so acceptable, but the label 'disagreement' is a slight approximation.

The 'held-out audit', 'verify-RED blocks', and 'gated-landing fraction' rows of the markdown headline (criterion 1) are rendered but not directly asserted by any test; they would still render if their values were wrong. Core headline fields (catches, reviewed, verdicts, disagreement) and PII-absence are well covered.
An undocumented --md flag path was added alongside --public/--badge; harmless but not part of the stated contract and untested.

title: feat: chalk feedback --submit — upstream feedback via prefilled GitHub issue URL (#157)

acceptanceCriteria.text: buildUpstreamFeedbackUrl is a pure function that percent-encodes the message into a GitHub new-issue URL for the configured upstream repo, including the chalk version in the body and a user-feedback label

chalk feedback --submit "<msg>" prints that URL, works with NO .chalk spine (runs before Store.open), and never creates .chalk/feedback or calls the analysis agent; CHALK_UPSTREAM_REPO overrides the repo
The existing chalk feedback signal-analysis path is unchanged; an empty --submit message is a clear usage error

findings.note: Criterion 3's 'existing signal-analysis path unchanged' is not directly asserted in feedback-submit.test.mjs, but the new behavior is fully guarded by an early return on `flags.submit !== undefined` so the legacy path is structurally untouched; low regression risk.

Empty-message path relies on `_.slice(1).join(' ')` where `_` includes the 'feedback' command token; verified the arg parser (line 58) returns the full positional array and the dispatch passes it through, so slice(1) correctly drops the command name and yields '' → clean die(). Behaves as tested.

title: feat: package-update handling — fix --version, opt-out update notifier, chalk upgrade (#158)

acceptanceCriteria.text: chalk --version and -v print the installed PACKAGE version (semver) and exit 0; chalk version still prints only the protocol tag (chalk/0) for scripts that parse it

The update notifier is skip-FIRST and inert in every non-interactive/opted-out context (non-TTY, --json, CI, CHALK_NO_UPDATE_CHECK, protocol.updateCheck:false), prefers a fresh once-per-day cache over the network, and a registry failure never throws or changes a command's exit code / --json output
chalk upgrade [--dry-run] prints (or runs) the correct global-npm update command

findings.note: Criterion 3 (`chalk upgrade [--dry-run]`) is entirely untested. The locked suite (test/update-notifier.test.mjs) covers only --version/-v and the update notifier; nothing spawns `chalk upgrade` or `chalk upgrade --dry-run` to assert it prints/runs `npm i -g chalk-protocol@latest`. The whole `upgrade` command could be deleted and the suite would still pass — a vacuous pass for an entire acceptance criterion. Per the hard rule, this alone requires block. A trivial `run('upgrade','--dry-run')` assertion on the printed command is missing.

The notifier's INTERACTIVE path (isTTY true, no opt-out) is never exercised end-to-end through bin/chalk.mjs. Every spawned test runs non-TTY, so the actual wiring in bin (the `process.stdout.isTTY && parsed.flags.json !== true` guard, config read via Store, console.error emission) is never asserted to emit a notice; only the pure lib functions are unit-tested. A regression that broke the bin-level invocation would go undetected.

`chalk upgrade` runs `npm i -g chalk-protocol@latest` unconditionally with no confirmation and inherits stdio; combined with being untested, a broken/incorrect command string would ship silently. Also the notifier reads protocol().updateCheck but the env-vs-config precedence (e.g., CHALK_NO_UPDATE_CHECK vs updateCheck:true) is only validated in isolation, not as composed in bin.

The interactive bin display path (process.stdout.isTTY branch that actually console.error's the notice) is never exercised end-to-end — TTY can't easily be faked in spawnSync tests. The risky guarantees (inertness under non-TTY/--json, no exit-code/JSON pollution) ARE covered via bin, and checkForUpdate's notice production is unit-tested, so this is thin untested glue rather than an uncovered feature. Reverting the bin diff would fail the --version/upgrade/inertness tests, so the suite is not vacuous.
chalk upgrade non-dry-run (execSync 'npm i -g chalk-protocol@latest') is unavoidably untested; acceptable since criterion 3 is satisfied via the dry-run path and the command string is asserted.

Interactive notifier awaits checkForUpdate (up to a 1.5s network timeout) before running the actual command, adding latency to every interactive invocation; bounded and TTY-only, so within stated design but worth noting.

title: docs: document the promote CI-poll knobs (ciPollIntervalMs/ciPollAttempts) in CONFIG + a runtime hint (#153)

acceptanceCriteria.text: docs/CONFIG.md's github section DESCRIBES ciPollIntervalMs and ciPollAttempts — what they control (remote-CI polling cadence during merge/promote) and the ciPollAttempts:0 never-wait escape — not merely lists them; the docs/CONFIG.md ↔ initSpine drift gate stays green
The release --promote CI-poll timeout (still-pending) message points the user at github.ciPollAttempts / ciPollIntervalMs

findings.note: docs/CONFIG.md's new text claims `ciPollAttempts: 0` means "never wait (fall straight through to local verify)". This misdescribes the actual behavior. In lib/brokecheck.mjs, when the PR HAS pending checks, maxAttempts=0 skips the poll loop and returns ci==='pending' → {ok:false, 'remote CI still running — merge when checks complete'}, i.e. a hard block, NOT a fall-through to local verify. Local verify only runs when ci==='none' (no checks at all), which is independent of ciPollAttempts. Worse, in the promote path (bin/chalk.mjs:730) 0 with pending CI dies with 'still pending after 0 check(s)' — never local verify. A user setting 0 to bypass slow CI would instead get an immediate block, the opposite of what the docs promise. This defeats criterion 1's requirement to accurately DESCRIBE the never-wait escape.

The locked test only asserts the literal presence of /ciPollAttempts: ?0|never wait/ in the github section; it never validates that the described 0-behavior matches the code. The inaccurate '(fall straight through to local verify)' parenthetical therefore passes unchecked — the test would stay green even with a wrong description.

Criterion 1: docs/CONFIG.md github section now describes ciPollIntervalMs/ciPollAttempts (polling cadence, defaults 5000/24≈2min, applies to merge and release --promote) and the ciPollAttempts:0 never-wait escape. The 0-behavior claim ('blocks a still-pending check, does NOT fall back to local verify') is accurate against brokeCheck (loop skipped with maxAttempts=0 → ci stays 'pending' → returns ok:false source:'ci' without calling verifyFn). Fallback-to-local only for 'none'. Verified correct.

Criterion 2: the release --promote still-pending die() message now names github.ciPollAttempts / ciPollIntervalMs, and locked test 4 asserts /still pending[\s\S]{0,120}ciPollAttempts/ against bin/chalk.mjs — reverting the message change would fail this test. The doc drift gate, description, and 0-escape accuracy are each pinned by their own locked assertions. Change is non-vacuously covered.

title: feat: post-run feedback nudge — after a productive `chalk run`, point the user at `chalk feedback --submit` (opt-out via CHALK_NO_NUDGE) (#155)

acceptanceCriteria.text: feedbackNudge() returns a string pointing at 'chalk feedback --submit' after a productive run (merged>0 or blocked>0), and null on a no-op sweep (0/0) or when CHALK_NO_NUDGE is set
chalk run wires feedbackNudge into its end-of-run summary (imported + called with the loop's merged/blocked totals)

findings.note: The wiring test only greps bin/chalk.mjs source for an import + a call matching feedbackNudge({merged:...blocked:...}); it does not execute `chalk run` end-to-end, so it cannot verify the nudge is actually printed (or gated behind `if (nudge)`) at runtime. But the pure-helper branches (merged>0, blocked>0, 0/0, CHALK_NO_NUDGE, opt-out text) are all asserted, and the call site is verified present and correctly fed r.totalMerged/r.totalBlocked in the run summary — adequate for the stated criteria.
CHALK_NO_NUDGE is truthy-checked, so any non-empty value (incl. '0' or 'false') silences the nudge; this matches the documented 'any non-empty value' contract and criterion wording, so acceptable.

title: fix: decouple the issue-pull count from the loop parser — one shared literal so a CLI reword can't silently zero the standing loop's steady-state detection

acceptanceCriteria.text: The 'pulled N new issue(s)' phrasing and its parser live in one shared module (lib/pull-count.mjs); bin/chalk.mjs emits via pulledIssuesLine and lib/loop.mjs reads via parsePulledIssues — no divergent inline literal
parsePulledIssues round-trips pulledIssuesLine, reads the count through bold-ANSI wrapping + the '(N already tracked)' suffix, and returns 0 when the line is absent

findings.note: The change under review satisfies both criteria cleanly: lib/pull-count.mjs holds the single 'pulled N new issue(s)' literal + PULLED_ISSUES_RE; bin/chalk.mjs emits via pulledIssuesLine(C.b(...)) and lib/loop.mjs reads via parsePulledIssues (old inline regex removed). Criterion 2 is fully exercised by test/pull-count.test.mjs — round-trip over multiple counts, bold-ANSI + '(N already tracked)' suffix, absent/empty/null→0, anti-spoof anchoring, and a static assertion that both files route through the shared module. Behavior is covered, not vacuous.

Scope bloat: the diff bundles ~1830 lines across 35 files (migrate, upgrade, stats --public/--badge, parallel pipeline, feedback --submit, review no-diff, fresh-base worktree, per-worktree P6, concurrent spine writes) far beyond the stated pull-count decoupling task. Each carries its own risk surface and violates the 'keep diffs small and scoped' rule; the extraneous changes are not part of this task's contract and dilute reviewability. The pull-count contract itself is correct and adequately tested, so this does not block the task's criteria, but the bundling should be split for auditability.

title: fix: reviewer diffs against the LOCAL base first — a stale/divergent local dev balloons the review diff to the whole branch history; prefer origin/<base>

acceptanceCriteria.text: captureDiff's strategy order prefers origin/<base>...HEAD over <base>...HEAD, so a stale/divergent local base branch can't balloon the review diff to the whole base-vs-trunk history
The strategy list is exposed as a pure function (diffStrategies) and preserves working-tree-first + the branchless last-commit/empty-tree fallbacks after the base-relative diffs

findings.note: Tests assert only the command-string ordering of diffStrategies (a pure function), not captureDiff's runtime behavior — i.e. that when origin/<base> resolves, execSync uses it and short-circuits before the local <base>. The behavioral payoff (remote base actually winning at review time) is not exercised. But since captureDiff's first-non-empty-wins loop is unchanged and the ordering is the whole contract, the string-order tests do faithfully lock both criteria and would fail if the change were reverted (original had local before remote). Acceptable.

Edge case not covered by tests but not required by criteria: if origin/<base> is itself stale relative to the real PR base, or in offline CI where origin/<base> is absent, behavior silently falls through to local <base> — the pre-existing balloon risk remains. This is inherent to the stated design and within acceptance criteria scope.

title: ci: add concurrency groups — cancel superseded test runs; serialize releases without cancelling an in-flight publish

acceptanceCriteria.text: test.yml declares a top-level concurrency group with cancel-in-progress: true so a newer push supersedes an in-flight test run
release.yml declares a top-level concurrency group with cancel-in-progress: false — a publish is never cancelled mid-flight

findings.note: The change satisfies both criteria exactly: test.yml has top-level concurrency group 'test-${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}' with cancel-in-progress: true; release.yml has group 'release' with cancel-in-progress: false. Both are locked by ci-concurrency.test.mjs (including the doesNotMatch guard against release being flipped to true).

Scope creep: the diff labeled 'ci: add concurrency groups' bundles ~1793 lines across 35 files of unrelated behavior (migrate, parallel pipeline, stats --public, feedback --submit, worktree fresh-base, review no-diff, single-WIP gate). Each carries its own tests, but this violates the 'keep diffs small and scoped' rule and inflates regression surface far beyond the CI task. It does not affect the two CI criteria, which are met and tested.

title: chore: enable GitHub Discussions + add issue/feedback templates and a post-run feedback nudge

issue.body:
## Why
We have distribution but no low-friction feedback channel. The warmest audience — people who just finished a chalk loop — is never invited to say anything.

## What
- **Enable GitHub Discussions** on chalkagents/chalk-protocol (Q&A + Ideas + Show-and-tell categories).
- **Issue templates** (`.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/`): a "share your setup + biggest friction" form and a bug form that auto-collects `chalk --version` + `chalk doctor` summary.
- **Post-run nudge**: after a successful `chalk done` / end of a `chalk run`, print a single dim line inviting a ⭐ or feedback with the `chalk feedback --submit` command (see the in-CLI feedback feature) — shown at most once per day, suppressible via config/env.

## Acceptance
- Discussions enabled; templates present and render on GitHub.
- The nudge is rate-limited (≤1/day), suppressible (`CHALK_NO_NUDGE=1`), and never interleaves with machine-readable `--json` output.
- A locked test asserts the nudge is suppressed under `--json` and when disabled.

block.reason: Duplicate of #155 — post-run nudge shipped by task-f2c154c; issue/feedback templates (.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/{bug_report,feature_request,friction_report}.yml) already present. Only remaining piece is enabling GitHub Discussions, a repo-admin action outside this session.

title: docs: document the promote CI-poll knobs (ciPollIntervalMs / ciPollAttempts) in help and CONFIG

issue.body:
## Gap
`chalk release --promote` polls the promotion PR’s CI in a loop up to `ciPollAttempts` times (default ~24) every `ciPollIntervalMs` (default ~5s) — up to ~2 hours — but neither the CLI help (`bin/chalk.mjs:~1809`) nor `docs/CONFIG.md` mentions the knobs or the wait. A developer running promote is surprised by the long wait and has no documented way to tune it.

## Suggested direction
- Add `ciPollIntervalMs` / `ciPollAttempts` to `docs/CONFIG.md` with defaults and effect.
- Mention the CI-poll behavior in the `release --promote` help text.
- Consider logging the effective timeout when polling begins (“waiting up to N min for CI…”).

## Acceptance
- CONFIG.md documents both knobs; help text references CI polling. (Doc-only; no gate test required, but a help-text assertion is welcome.)

Grounded in: `bin/chalk.mjs:688-692`.

block.reason: Duplicate of #153 — shipped by task-6039444 (merged, commit 766be82). CI-poll knobs documented in CONFIG + runtime hint. No code work remains; parked pending issue close.

title: docs(skills): add a chalk-autopilot-setup skill for readying an unattended run

acceptanceCriteria.text: .claude/skills/chalk-autopilot-setup/SKILL.md exists with YAML frontmatter whose description triggers on 'set up autopilot'/'ready for unattended'/'chalk doctor fails'/'resume after churn'

issue.body:
## Why
Before `chalk run`/`chalk pipeline`, `chalk doctor` must pass, but doctor is read-only — the fixes (executor, reviewer, test-locks, held-out isolation) are all manual, and churn/handoff resume is undocumented.

## What it should encode
- Run `chalk doctor`; map each FAIL/WARN to its fix: set `executor.command`, configure a reviewer (avoid same-model as executor — self-preference bias, `lib/config.mjs`), lock tests on runnable tasks, set `worktree.setup`.
- **Held-out isolation** (P7): worktree+gitignored in-repo, OR manual-mode outside the repo root (#82) — `heldOutBase()` resolution.
- **Vacuous-verify guard**: an empty `protocol.verify` prints GREEN checking nothing — ensure real checks before queuing tasks.
- **Churn/handoff resume**: when a task exceeds `handoff.maxAttempts` (default 3) a handoff is written to `.chalk/handoffs/<id>-N.md`; resume in a FRESH session with `chalk context <id>`.

## Acceptance
- `.claude/skills/chalk-autopilot-setup/SKILL.md` with frontmatter + trigger ("set up autopilot", "ready for unattended", "chalk doctor fails", "resume after churn").
- Doctor-failure → fix table + isolation guidance + handoff-resume steps.

Grounded in: `lib/doctor.mjs`, `lib/regression.mjs`, `lib/handoff.mjs`, `lib/run.mjs:71-78`. Related: #82.

findings.note: Skill lists the lock command as `chalk spec <id> --test <path>`; the canonical/help form is `chalk spec <id> --criterion "..." --test <path>`. The abbreviated form is valid but slightly under-specified vs the CLI help text.

No locked acceptance test exists for the skill (criteria are content requirements). Acceptable here because the change is pure documentation with no executable behavior to assert; all four criteria are verifiable by inspection and are present and factually consistent with doctor.mjs/handoff.mjs/regression.mjs.

acceptanceCriteria.text: .claude/skills/chalk-dogfood/SKILL.md exists with YAML frontmatter whose description triggers on 'contribute to chalk'/'dogfood'/'run the loop on chalk itself'

Encodes the ordering gotchas: commit issue-intake spine metadata in its OWN chore(spine) commit BEFORE feature work, commit review-fix changes MANUALLY (chalk commit no-ops #134) verifying git status clean + git show --stat HEAD before chalk merge, commit sha256-pinned locked tests in the same change, and reconcile with chore(spine) after out-of-band merges
Links chalk-commit (#141) and chalk-ship (#142)

issue.body:
## Why
The self-hosting loop is the intended contribution path but its ordering rules are scattered across `CONTRIBUTING.md` + 5 lessons, and getting them wrong creates review noise or lost work.

## Why

## What it should encode
- **Author-fail-first**: write a test that FAILS without the change, passes with it.
- **Pin it**: `chalk spec --test <path>` sha256-locks the file.
- **Commit the lock in the SAME change that creates it** — an untracked locked test ships a vacuous green (tracking gate #107/#113).

acceptanceCriteria.text: .claude/skills/chalk-branch-cleanup/SKILL.md exists with YAML frontmatter (name, description) whose description triggers on 'clean up branches'

Prominently documents that git branch --merged is UNRELIABLE here (squash merges are not ancestors) and PR state must be verified via gh pr list --head <branch> --state all --json state (delete only when MERGED)

issue.body:
## Why
Branch cleanup was just done ad-hoc this session. The key subtlety — **squash-merged branches do NOT show as merged by ancestry**, so `git branch --merged` misses them and you must verify PR state via `gh` — is easy to get wrong (and risky: deleting an unmerged branch loses work). A `chalk-branch-cleanup` skill makes it repeatable and safe.

## What it should encode
- `git fetch --prune` first — clears local tracking refs for branches already deleted on the remote.
- **Do NOT trust `git branch --merged origin/main`** for this repo: it squash-merges, so merged feature branches are not ancestors of main. Instead verify each branch's PR: `gh pr list --head <branch> --state all --json state` → only delete when `MERGED`.
- Delete remote merged branches: `git push origin --delete <branches...>`.
- Delete stale local branches whose upstream is `gone` (`git branch -vv`), force-delete (`-D`) since squash merges are not ancestors — but only after confirming the PR is `MERGED`.
- Resync `main` to `origin/main` when it has drifted behind.
- **Safety rule**: never delete a branch with an OPEN or no PR without checking `git log origin/main..<branch>` for unmerged commits first.

## Acceptance
- `.claude/skills/chalk-branch-cleanup/SKILL.md` exists with frontmatter and a trigger description covering "clean up branches".
- Content includes the exact commands and the squash-merge/gh-verification caveat prominently.
- Includes the "check unmerged commits before deleting a non-MERGED branch" safety step.

findings.note: Criterion 2 specifies '--json state' but the skill uses '--json number,state'. This is a superset that still includes the required state field and correctly instructs 'delete ONLY when state == MERGED', so the intent (verify PR state via gh, delete only when MERGED) is fully satisfied.

acceptanceCriteria.text: .claude/skills/chalk-ship/SKILL.md exists with YAML frontmatter (name: chalk-ship, description) whose description triggers on 'push'/'open PR'/'land'

issue.body:
## Why
Landing PRs in this repo has a sharp, expensive trap that has already bitten us (stacked PRs auto-closed by `--delete-branch`). The safe procedure lives only in a memory note. A `chalk-ship` skill would make push/PR-landing uniform and trap-free.

## What it should encode
- **Branch naming**: `<type>/<issue>-<slug>`.
- **The stacked-PR `--delete-branch` trap**: never `gh pr merge --delete-branch` a PR whose head is the BASE of another open PR — it auto-CLOSES the child, and a closed PR whose base branch is gone cannot be reopened or rebased. You must recreate it.
- **Landing a stack A←B←C bottom-up**:
  1. Merge A **without** `--delete-branch` (use `--merge`, not `--squash`, to preserve shared ancestry so children stay mergeable).
  2. `gh pr edit B --base main`, confirm `mergeable: MERGEABLE`, merge B (no delete). Repeat for C.
  3. Delete all merged branches **at the end**, once nothing targets them.
  - GitHub does NOT reliably auto-retarget children — retarget each child explicitly before merging it.
- **Single-PR path**: normal squash-merge is fine when nothing stacks on it.
- **Pre-merge check**: confirm the fix is actually committed (ties into the chalk-commit no-op hazard, #134) before merge.

## Acceptance
- `.claude/skills/chalk-ship/SKILL.md` exists with frontmatter and a trigger description covering "push"/"open PR"/"land".
- Content covers the single-PR path AND the stacked-PR procedure with the exact `gh` commands.
- Cross-references `chalk-commit`.

Related: #134

title: feat: spine/protocol migration — version-stamp the spine, detect skew on open, add gated chalk migrate

issue.body:
## Why
chalk is a STATEFUL CLI: a project’s `.chalk/` spine is written by whatever package version the user had. When they `npm i -g chalk-protocol@latest`, a newer binary may read a spine written by an older one (or vice-versa). Today the spine stamps `chalk.json.version: "1.0"` (schema) and `protocol.version: "chalk/0"` (`lib/store.mjs:439,443`) but:
- **No package-version stamp** — nothing records which chalk-protocol version last wrote the spine.
- **No skew detection** — `Store.open()` reads a spine of any age with no compatibility check.
- **No migration path** — if the tasks.json schema or `PROTOCOL` ever changes (`chalk/0 → chalk/1`), an existing project silently misreads or breaks; there’s no sanctioned upgrade.

This is the real data-safety risk when updating a stateful tool. Sibling to the package-update work (#158), which covers the binary; this covers the DATA.

## What
1. **Stamp the writer version**: record the chalk-protocol package version (and keep `chalk.json.version` schema + `protocol.version`) on `initSpine` and on every spine write, so a spine self-describes what wrote it.
2. **Detect skew on `Store.open()`**: compare the spine’s stamped versions against the running binary.
   - Newer spine + older binary → refuse with a clear message ("this project was written by chalk 0.4.0; you’re on 0.2.0 — upgrade").
   - Older spine needing a schema/protocol bump → prompt to run `chalk migrate` (don’t silently mutate).
   - Compatible → proceed untouched (no nag for same-major).
3. **`chalk migrate` (gated)**: apply ordered, per-version migration steps to bring a spine to the current schema/protocol; `--dry-run` shows the plan; writes a backup (e.g. `.chalk/backups/`) before mutating; records a decision. Idempotent; a no-op when already current.
4. **`chalk doctor` surfaces skew** as a WARN/FAIL with the remediation.

## Acceptance
- Locked test: opening a spine stamped with a NEWER binary version refuses (non-zero, clear message) rather than misreading.
- Locked test: `chalk migrate` on an old-schema fixture upgrades it to current, is idempotent on re-run, and `--dry-run` mutates nothing.
- Locked test: a same-version (compatible) spine opens with no migration prompt and no mutation.

#158 (package update — the binary half). Cross-ref `lib/store.mjs` initSpine/Store.open, `PROTOCOL` in `lib/store.mjs`.

title: feat: proper package-update handling — fix --version, add an opt-out update notifier + chalk upgrade

issue.body:
## Why
chalk-protocol is a globally-installed npm CLI (`npm i -g chalk-protocol`) but has no update story, and the version basics are broken:
- **`chalk --version` / `-v` errors** with `unknown command: --version` (`bin/chalk.mjs` arg dispatch). The `version` command prints `chalk/0` — the PROTOCOL tag (`lib/store.mjs` `PROTOCOL`), NOT the package version (`0.2.0`). A user cannot easily tell what they are running.
- **No update check** — nothing surfaces that a newer version exists; users silently run stale copies and hit already-fixed bugs.

## What
1. **Fix version reporting**: `chalk --version` / `-v` print the package version (read chalk's own `package.json`, resolved module-relative — see `chalkVersion()` pattern used elsewhere). Keep `chalk version` for the protocol tag, or print both (`chalk-protocol 0.2.0 · protocol chalk/0`).
2. **Opt-out update notifier**: on run, best-effort check the npm registry for a newer `latest` and print a one-line, dim, non-blocking notice ("update available: 0.2.0 → 0.3.0 · run `npm i -g chalk-protocol@latest`").
   - **Zero-dependency**: a tiny homegrown check (registry JSON), not `update-notifier`.
   - **Throttled + cached** (e.g. once/day in a state file); **never blocks or fails a command**; suppressed under `--json`, on CI, when offline, and via `CHALK_NO_UPDATE_CHECK=1` / config. Same network-etiquette + opt-out posture as the telemetry issue (#154).
3. **`chalk upgrade` (convenience)**: prints/runs the correct update command for the install method (global npm), with `--dry-run` to just show it.

## Acceptance
- Locked test: `--version`/`-v` emit the package version (semver), exit 0; `chalk version` still emits the protocol tag.
- Locked test: the update check is skipped under `--json` / when disabled / when the cache is fresh, and a registry failure never changes exit code or `--json` output.

## Related / NOT in scope here
Spine + protocol **migration** (upgrading an existing `.chalk/` when `PROTOCOL` bumps `chalk/0 → chalk/1`, or the tasks.json schema changes across package versions) is a distinct concern — the real data-safety risk when a user updates a stateful tool. Filing separately (a `chalk migrate` / doctor-guided upgrade). Cross-ref #154 (network/opt-out posture).

title: feat: opt-in anonymous activation telemetry (init → first green verify → done funnel)

acceptanceCriteria.text: Telemetry is OFF by default: with no opt-in config and no env, no network call, no install-id write, and no payload is emitted on init/verify/done
When enabled, the emitted payload contains ONLY whitelisted fields (event name, chalk version, random anonymous install id, timestamp) — never code, paths, prompts, diffs, or repo identity
Emission is fire-and-forget and non-blocking: a network/DNS failure (or unreachable endpoint) never changes a command's exit code or throws
chalk telemetry --show prints the resolved enabled state and EXACTLY the payload that would be sent; CHALK_TELEMETRY=0 and a config flag hard-disable, and CI (process.env.CI) disables by default
Opt-in is prompted once at chalk init (default N); README + docs/CONFIG.md document the telemetry config, the env kill-switch, and the whitelisted fields

issue.body:
## Why
`chalk-protocol` has ~200 npm downloads/week but we are blind on real usage — registry mirrors inflate download counts and we cannot tell how many installs ever ran `chalk init`, let alone reached a green verify. Without an activation signal, all traction work is pouring water into a bucket with no gauge.

## What
Opt-in, anonymous, minimal telemetry that reports funnel milestones only:
- `init`, first `verify` GREEN, first `done`, and CLI version.
- **No code, paths, prompts, diffs, or repo identity.** Random anonymous install id.
- **Opt-IN**: prompt once at `chalk init` ("help improve chalk? anonymous usage stats [y/N]"); default off; `CHALK_TELEMETRY=0` and a config flag hard-disable; documented in README + docs/CONFIG.md.
- Fire-and-forget, non-blocking, never fails a command; strip on CI by default.

## Why opt-in matters
The agentic-dev-tool audience is telemetry-allergic. A surprise phone-home costs more trust than the data is worth. Make consent loud and the payload inspectable (`chalk telemetry --show`).

## Acceptance
- Locked test: telemetry is OFF unless explicitly enabled; when enabled, payload contains ONLY the whitelisted fields; a network failure never affects exit code.
- Docs updated; `chalk telemetry --show` prints exactly what would be sent.

Context: 196 downloads last week, zero activation visibility.

findings.note: The integration wiring added to bin/chalk.mjs — firing the 'verify' milestone on first green verify, the 'done' milestone on chalk done, and the interactive opt-in at chalk init (flip config + emit 'init') — has NO test. The locked suite only unit-tests lib/telemetry.mjs functions and spawns `chalk init --bare` + `chalk telemetry --show`. If every `emitMilestone` call site in bin/chalk.mjs were deleted, the entire suite would still pass. That is a vacuous pass for the core funnel behavior (criteria 1/5).

Criterion 5 (opt-in prompted once at init, default N; opting in enables config and fires the init milestone) is unverified for the affirmative path. promptTelemetryOptIn + the config write + init emit are never exercised by a test; only the non-TTY decline path is implicitly hit. Consent-flipping behavior shipping with zero assertion is exactly the gap adversarial review must catch.

In `verify`, `void emitMilestone(...)` is immediately followed by `process.exit(v.green?0:2)`. emitMilestone synchronously writes state marking the 'verify' milestone as sent BEFORE the `await send`, then process.exit terminates the process before the fetch completes — so the first-green-verify event is recorded as sent but the POST is aborted and never delivered, and because it's marked sent it will never be retried. The verify funnel step is structurally undeliverable, defeating the stated design intent.

Criterion 3 non-blocking: `chalk done` does NOT call process.exit, so the un-awaited emitMilestone leaves a pending fetch/1500ms-timeout on the event loop, delaying process exit by up to ~1.5s when enabled and endpoint is unreachable. No test asserts done stays prompt/non-blocking under a hanging endpoint.

`telemetry --show` claims to print 'EXACTLY the payload that would be sent' (criterion 4) but samplePayload hardcodes event:'init' regardless of which milestones remain unsent, so the displayed event can differ from the next actually-sent event.

Criterion 5's core behavior — the one-time interactive opt-in prompt at `chalk init` (default N, 'y'/'yes' to accept, EOF/empty declines) — has NO test. All locked tests use the --telemetry/--no-telemetry flags or the non-TTY silent-decline path; removing promptTelemetryOptIn entirely would leave the suite fully green. The prompt text, affirmative-consent path, and default-N semantics are unverified (vacuous pass for the prompt feature).

The ENABLED-state view of `chalk telemetry --show` (optedIn=yes, killSwitch display, endpoint, sample payload with a real installId) is never exercised via CLI or telemetryStatus; only the OFF path is asserted. Criterion 4 requires --show to print the resolved enabled state exactly, but the enabled rendering path is untested.

Criterion 3 says emission is 'non-blocking', yet emitMilestone is awaited inline in init/verify/done and can stall the command up to the 700ms sender timeout when opted in. Exit code is preserved (tested), but 'non-blocking' is only satisfied in the loose sense; a truly fire-and-forget design would not block the command's completion on the POST.
The `--no-telemetry` flag branch and the CHALK_TELEMETRY='off' kill-switch value are handled in code but never asserted by any test (only '0' and 'false' are covered for the env switch).

Fire-and-forget emit rides the event loop via `void emitMilestone` + `process.exitCode=0` (replacing `process.exit(0)` in verify). For an opted-in user hitting a slow/unreachable collector, process exit is delayed up to the 700ms AbortController timeout on every init/verify/done. Exit code and throwing are unaffected (criterion 3's literal requirement is met and e2e-tested), but 'non-blocking' is slightly overstated — exit is stalled until the pending fetch resolves/aborts.

The interactive opt-in prompt wiring (askTelemetryOptIn → readStdinLine via readSync on a real TTY) is never exercised end-to-end; init opt-in is only tested via --telemetry/--no-telemetry flags. promptTelemetryOptIn's logic is unit-tested with injected I/O, so the consent semantics are covered, but the actual init-time TTY prompt path (criterion 5, 'prompted once at chalk init, default N') has no test asserting the prompt appears and enabled flips on 'y'.

Criterion 5's documentation requirement (README + docs/CONFIG.md documenting the config, env kill-switch, and whitelisted fields) has no assertion; content is present in the diff but nothing guards against future doc drift. Acceptable for docs but worth noting.

verify now returns via process.exitCode=0 instead of process.exit(0), relying on the event loop draining. If any other command path leaves an open handle/unref'd timer, verify could hang rather than force-exit as before. Default-OFF telemetry adds no fetch so the common path is clean and e2e tests exit 0, but the guarantee is now weaker than an explicit process.exit.

telemetry --show prints installId placeholder '(assigned on first enabled emit)' when enabled but no id minted yet, so the 'sample payload' is not byte-exact to what would actually be sent (real UUID). This is a deliberate/justified tradeoff to honor the OFF/no-write invariant (locked test asserts --show writes no state), and all other payload fields match — acceptable, not a contract violation.

The fire-and-forget guarantee is exercised only against connection-REFUSED (instant reject); a hung-but-connected endpoint (relying on the 700ms AbortController) is not directly tested. Mechanism is present and init lacks the 900ms safety timer verify has, but the abort bounds it, so exit codes stay unchanged.

The real interactive-TTY wiring (readStdinLine/askTelemetryOptIn via readSync(fd 0)) is not integration-tested; only the pure promptTelemetryOptIn consent semantics are covered. Hard to PTY-test and the decision logic is fully unit-tested, so coverage of the actual behavior is adequate.

verify() switched from process.exit(0) to process.exitCode=0 + unref'd 900ms force-exit timer. When telemetry is OFF (default/CI) emitMilestone returns synchronously with no pending handle, so the unref'd timer does not delay exit and the exit codes (0 green / 2 non-green) are preserved; e2e OFF + unreachable tests confirm 0. Low residual risk if runVerify ever leaves a ref'd handle.

issue.body:
## The white space chalk should own

Every AI coding tool gates the **plan** and the **PR**. **Nobody owns the mid-task "empty middle"** — the judgment calls an agent hits *while* building and silently one-shots past (HiL-Bench 2026). #160 is exactly this failure mode observed in the wild.

The defensible mechanism — win on the mechanism, not the slogan — is **risk-based decision triage**.

## The mechanism: score choices, escalate the risky ones

Before `chalk done`, the agent runs a **risk pass over its own choices** and scores each on:

- **Reversibility** — how hard is this to undo later?
- **Blast radius** — how much of the system / product surface does it touch?
- **Ambiguity** — how underspecified was the intent here?

Choices above a threshold **do not get one-shotted** — they auto-convert to `chalk question --for us` / `chalk block --needs decision`, so the agent **escalates instead of assuming**. Low-risk choices flow through untouched (this must not turn every task into a wall of questions — the threshold and a cap matter).

## The surface: a director inbox

Mirror `chalk next` (the agent's entrypoint) with the **human's** entrypoint: a **risk-ranked queue of decisions awaiting judgment** — e.g. `chalk pending`, or reuse the existing `lib/boards.mjs` / `lib/portal.mjs` surfaces. This is what makes chalk *feel* like a director's harness rather than a linter.

## Sequencing note

This is **Tier 2** — heavier than the reviewer decision-digest (sibling issue). Recommend gating it on the digest slice landing + the demo post drawing signal, per the content-first validation plan. Filed now so the mechanism is on record and scoped.

## Acceptance sketch (to be locked during spec)

- The agent produces a per-choice risk score (reversibility × blast-radius × ambiguity) over its diff before `done`.
- Choices above a configurable threshold auto-escalate to a decision/question rather than passing silently; below-threshold choices are unaffected; a cap prevents question-flooding.
- A director inbox surface lists pending decisions ranked by risk.
- Covered by a locked test.

Milestone: director-harness. Relates to #160.

findings.note: Criterion 2 ('chalk review ranks the decision digest highest-risk-first with a per-decision risk badge') is not exercised by any test. The new review-command behavior lives in bin/chalk.mjs (the ranked/badged loop over formatDecisionLine+decisionRisk+RISK_RANK sort), but director-triage.test.mjs never invokes `chalk review`, and the locked #192 test (review-digest.test.mjs) only asserts the 'Decision digest' header and choice-text presence — not ordering and not the risk badge. Reverting the entire review-display change back to plain formatDecisionDigest would leave both #192 and the new triage tests green. That is a behavior change shipped with no asserting test (vacuous pass).

The inbox ref uses taskId.slice(0,12), while real ids are `task-`+8 hex = 13 chars, so the displayed ref is a 12-char prefix that drops the last hex char. accept/redirect resolve it via s.task() (startsWith prefix match), which works only while the 12-char prefix stays unique across tasks; a collision would silently resolve the wrong task. Consistent with the repo's resolveRef convention, but the test only uses a non-standard 12-char id (task-abc1234), so the truncation-of-real-ids path is never exercised.

Accept/redirect resolutions are stored on the decision object inside a task's latest review. When a task is re-reviewed, runReview regenerates decisions fresh (no accepted/redirected flags carried over), so previously-accepted/redirected calls resurface in the inbox after any subsequent review. No test covers resolution persistence across re-review; may undercut the 'drops it from the inbox' guarantee over a task's life.

issue.body:
## The reframe

Chalk's adversarial reviewer is framed as a *referee refuting a cheat* — its output is essentially pass/block against acceptance criteria. That's the commoditizing "catch a cheating agent" frame.

Under the director's harness, the same engine should also produce **the accept button**: a **decision digest** the human reviews and acts on.

## The mechanism: reviewer emits a decision digest

Extend the reviewer output (same run, same diff) to surface, alongside the pass/block verdict:

- The **N judgment calls the agent made** while implementing the task (the choices it *silently* resolved),
- Each with its **rationale** and a **blast-radius / reversibility** note,
- Framed for **accept / redirect**, not just "is this a violation."

So the human reads a short "here's what I decided on your behalf — confirm or redirect each" list instead of re-reading a diff.

## Why now

- It's a **small, high-leverage change** — reuses `lib/review.mjs` and the existing reviewer agent; mostly an output-shape + prompt change.
- It produces the exact artifact the **content-demo** needs (agent surfaces a judgment call → director redirects it → screen recording), so it's product + marketing in one slice.
- It reframes the gate from *cop* → *accept button* without demoting it: the gates stay, they just speak the director's language.

## Acceptance sketch (to be locked during spec)

title: feat(director): alignment checkpoint before build — human accepts the criteria/outcome, not just the plan

acceptanceCriteria.text: protocol.director.required defaults off; when off, chalk work behaves exactly as today (no regression)
With director.required on and criteria not accepted, chalk work AND the autonomous driver (chalk run) refuse before build, pointing the human at chalk align
chalk align records task.criteriaAccepted = { at, by }; after alignment chalk work proceeds past the gate
chalk align surfaces the task's acceptance criteria for the human to read before accepting (not blind), and refuses when there are no criteria yet

issue.body:
## The gap

Reported empirically in #160: in autonomous mode (`chalk run` / `chalk pipeline`) the agent scoped criteria, looped, and built everything — **but ended up misaligned with what the human actually wanted.** There was no point at which a human confirmed *"yes, this is what done means"* before the build committed.

Today chalk gates the **plan** (`chalk approve-plan`) and the **outcome** (`verify`/`review`/`done`). It does **not** gate the *framing of done* — the acceptance criteria themselves. In director terms: the human never gets to press accept on the spec before the agent one-shots past it.

> "needs alignment on what is done… needs alignment on outcome… approval / go-ahead on acceptance criteria / prototype before build." — #160

## The mechanism: an alignment checkpoint before build

Introduce a **criteria/outcome accept gate** that, in director mode, blocks `chalk work` until the human has signed off on the acceptance criteria (and optionally a prototype/plan). Concretely:

- After `chalk discover` / criteria authoring, the agent emits a **plain-language "here's what I think *done* means"** restatement — outcome, criteria, and the judgment calls it's assuming — not the raw criteria list.
- A new gate (e.g. `chalk align <id>` / an approve-criteria step, mirroring the existing `approve-plan`) requires explicit human go-ahead. Without it, `chalk work` refuses in director mode.
- In autonomous mode this is opt-in via config (`protocol.director.alignBeforeBuild`), so unattended runs can still fan out — but the default for a director-mode project is **align first**.

## Why this is the pivot's keystone

This is the direct fix for #160 and the mechanism behind *"you can't direct what you can't verify"* — the criteria **are** the spec of done, and the human must accept them before build, not discover the mismatch at review. It reuses the `approve-plan` checkpoint pattern already in the codebase.

## Acceptance sketch (to be locked during spec)

- A director-mode project cannot reach `chalk work`/build on a task whose criteria have not been human-accepted.
- The accept step surfaces a plain-language outcome restatement, not just the raw criteria.
- Autonomous runs honor an opt-in/opt-out config knob; the behavior is covered by a locked test.

Anchor: #160. Milestone: director-harness.

findings.note: `chalk align` only refuses when BOTH acceptanceCriteria and tests are empty; a task with locked tests but no acceptanceCriteria aligns while surfacing only test paths, which is a defensible reading of 'criteria as spec' but slightly loosens criterion 4's literal 'no criteria yet' refusal. Not a functional gap.

No test asserts the ordering that the align gate is checked BEFORE the state flip in `chalk work` (i.e. a refusal leaves no side effect / task not moved to in-progress). Behavior is correct in the code but this 'no side effect on refusal' property is unverified.
Gate sits after the stageDone('verified') early-return, so an already-verified task never requires alignment; acceptable but untested for the director-on case.

reviews.note: locked test amended after review — re-review required

findings.note: chalk align refuses only when BOTH acceptanceCriteria and tests are empty (`!criteria.length && !(t.tests||[]).length`). A task with locked tests but zero textual criteria can be aligned while surfacing no criteria text — a slightly looser reading of criterion 4 ('surfaces the criteria... refuses when there are no criteria yet'), though defensible since the human still sees the locked test paths.

The default attribution `by: 'human'` is never asserted (only the explicit --by 'jerel' path is), and the chalk run block reason's 'points the human at chalk align' wording is not asserted in the run test (only needs=human-input + handoff). Both are exercised indirectly; behavior itself (predicate, work refusal, run block, align record) is covered such that reverting any code path fails a test.

Backward compatibility for pre-existing spines relies on optional chaining (`director?.required`) rather than a migration adding the key; verified safe (undefined→false), so old spines stay opt-out. No regression, noted for completeness.

title: fix: vacuous verify trap for tasks queued after init — empty protocol.verify prints GREEN checking nothing

issue.body:
## Bug
An empty `protocol.verify` config makes every `chalk verify` print GREEN while checking nothing. This is warned at `chalk init` (`bin/chalk.mjs:129-138`) and in verify output (line 1392-1393), but it is not enforced by the gates. A developer who queues tasks into a project whose verify was never configured gets tasks that auto-pass P4 without any real testing; `chalk run` will happily “complete” them.

## Why it matters
The whole product value is the verify gate. A vacuous verify silently defeats it for anyone who didn’t configure verify at init time.

## Suggested direction
Have `chalk start`/`chalk work`/`chalk done` (or `chalk next`) refuse or loudly warn when `protocol.verify` is empty on a runnable task — not only at init. `chalk doctor` warns only when a reviewer backstop is absent; tighten this.

## Acceptance
- A locked test asserts a runnable task with empty `protocol.verify` cannot silently reach `done` via a vacuous green.

Grounded in: `bin/chalk.mjs:129-138`, `1392-1393`; `lib/doctor.mjs:89`.

block.reason: Duplicate of #152 — already shipped to dev as task-3c3ede1 (vacuous-verify doctor blocker). Re-imported by an unfiltered issue pull; no code work remains. Closes when dev→main lands #152.

title: fix: review diff-capture silently falls back to "(no diff captured)", letting a reviewer verdict on no diff

issue.body:
## Bug
`captureDiff` (`lib/review.mjs:78-93`) tries `git diff HEAD` → `base...HEAD` → `origin/base...HEAD` → `git diff`, and if all fail emits `"(no diff captured — read the source files in the current directory)"`. A reviewer running in isolation (remote LLM without the working tree) then produces a PASS or BLOCK verdict on **no diff** — and the fallback message isn’t alarming enough to catch it.

## Why it matters
Same class of hazard as #134: a gate can certify against incomplete input. A vacuous diff → a vacuous review.

## Suggested direction
When no diff is captured, either fail the review stage loudly (config/env problem, like a reviewer ERROR rather than a BLOCK), or require the reviewer to explicitly acknowledge tree-inspection mode. Surface it in `chalk review` output and diagnostics, not just the prompt.

## Acceptance
- A locked test where all diff strategies fail asserts the review does NOT silently pass — it errors or is clearly flagged as diffless.

Grounded in: `lib/review.mjs:78-93`. Related: #134.

block.reason: Duplicate of #151 — already shipped to dev as task-daa4516 (diffless-review guard). Re-imported by an unfiltered issue pull; no code work remains. Closes when dev→main lands #151.

title: fix: merge cleanup fast-forward failure still marks the task done, leaving a stale local base

issue.body:
## Bug
After a squash-merge, `chalk merge` best-effort fast-forwards the primary base branch locally (`bin/chalk.mjs:825-829`). If that ff-pull fails (e.g. local `main` has commits), the failure is printed as a warning but does **not** fail the merge gate — the task is marked `done` anyway (`bin/chalk.mjs:830-834`).

## Why it matters
The developer’s primary checkout is left dirty/stale. The next `chalk branch` for the following task may branch off a stale base or fail. The warning is printed mid-merge-output and easily missed.

## Suggested direction
Either (a) surface the ff failure more loudly and record it on the task, or (b) make the next `chalk branch` fetch/validate the base tip before branching rather than trusting local. Remote is source of truth, so don’t block `done` — but don’t silently strand a stale base either.

## Acceptance
- A locked test drives a merge where the local base ff-pull fails, asserting the task still completes AND the stale-base condition is either recovered or clearly flagged before the next branch.

Grounded in: `bin/chalk.mjs:825-834`.

title: feat(director-loop): B2 · inject prior director decisions into new-task context (the moat)

No director decisions → no block (no regression to existing context)

issue.body:
Part of the **director-loop** milestone — EPIC B (judgment compounds). **This is the defensible moat** — seam-03: "judgment as a compounding asset."

## Problem

Past director calls never inform future work, so the same fork recurs task after task. The director's-harness thesis is that "the agent gets more *you* over time" — that only happens if accepted/redirected decisions (with their *why*) fold back into future context.

## Acceptance sketch (to be locked at spec time)

- `buildContext` injects a **bounded** `## Director's calls so far (apply this taste)` block, built from the durable record (#201), most-recent-first.
- Bounded by a budget knob (like `lessons` / `contextBudget`), with an elision note when trimmed — the essentials (criteria/tests/handoff/directives) are never displaced.
- **Empty/off** when there are no director decisions yet (no regression to existing context for projects that don't use it).
- Covered by a locked test: a prior decision appears in a *new* task's context, and the block respects the budget.

## Touchpoints
- `lib/store.mjs` — `buildContext` (a new bounded block, sibling to the elastic lessons block), plus a budget/cap knob.

## Dependencies
Depends on **#201** (the durable record). Turns on the compounding loop.

findings.note: The director block is injected unconditionally, not gated to 'NEW tasks' — it renders whenever buildContext runs, including when `task` is null (no current task) and on the very task whose accept/redirect it may have just produced, so a decision logged against the current task can echo back into its own context. Harmless but broader than the 'on NEW tasks' scope the criterion states; no test pins the null-task or same-task case.

Tests assert the director block renders and is budget-priority in isolation, but none asserts the intended ordering/coexistence with lessons (director block first, lessons still present) or that directorBytes correctly reserves budget so both blocks fit. The 'higher-signal than lessons' priority tradeoff is implemented but unverified — a regression that dropped lessons entirely when director decisions exist would pass the suite.

The rendered heading ('## Director's calls so far (apply this taste — the human accepted/redirected these)') is longer than the criterion's quoted string ('## Director's calls so far (apply this taste)'); tests only match the loose substring /Director's calls so far/i, so the exact wording is unpinned and could drift.

decisions.rationale: Director's explicit accept/redirect calls are treated as higher-signal taste than auto-collected lessons

decisions.choice: Inject the block on every buildContext call rather than filtering to unresolved/other-task decisions or a 'new' task state
decisions.rationale: Simplicity; the whole durable record is the compounding taste feed

decisions.choice: Fallback strings for missing fields ('a choice', '(see record)') instead of skipping malformed records
decisions.rationale: Render gracefully rather than drop a director call

decisions.choice: Elision note wording and most-recent-first ordering mirror the lessons block convention
decisions.rationale: Consistency with existing bounded-context behavior

findings.note: Criterion 1 scopes the block to 'NEW tasks', but fitDirectorBlock is injected for ANY task passed to buildContext regardless of state (in-progress, re-opened, etc.). No test asserts suppression on non-new tasks. Consequence: a re-opened/in-progress task's OWN just-recorded director decision can surface in the compounding block AND simultaneously in the essential 'Director corrections' block (task.directives) — duplicate signal. Not a criterion failure (tests treat in-progress as 'new'), but it's an unconfirmed scope call worth a human's eye.

directorLines renders anything that is not verdict==='redirected' as 'accepted:'. Any future/other verdict value (e.g. a logged non-accept/redirect) would be silently mislabeled as accepted. Safe today since B1's schema is accept/redirect only, but the else-branch is not defensive and no test pins non-accepted/non-redirected input.

When directorBlock consumes nearly all leftover budget, lessons get remaining ≤ 0 and fitLessonsBlock still emits a heading-plus-elision-note block with zero lessons. Pre-existing behavior, but the new director-first budget split makes it easier to trigger; no test covers the director+lessons-both-under-pressure interaction (only director-alone elision and coexist-when-roomy are tested).

Criterion 2 asks for 'elided with a note'; in the total-starvation case there is no note at all. Minor and essentials are still protected, but it's an inconsistency with the sibling behavior it claims to mirror.

Criterion 1 scopes the block to 'NEW tasks', but the implementation injects it for ANY task passed to buildContext (the test task is state 'in-progress', not new). Only the current task's own decisions are filtered out. Injecting broadly is arguably beneficial, but no test pins the 'new-task' semantics, so a future narrowing/broadening would go uncaught.

No test covers the redirected-with-missing-instruction fallback ('(see record)') or the accepted-with-missing-rationale path, nor the interaction where the current task's own decision co-exists with a #199 directives block in the same render. Core paths are well covered, but these branches ship untested.

decisions.rationale: Encodes the B1 schema split (rationale for accepted, instruction for redirected) as distinct human-readable lines

title: feat(director-loop): B1 · a durable, structured director-decision record

acceptanceCriteria.text: chalk pending accept/redirect write through to a durable append-only record (.chalk/director.jsonl) with structured fields: at, verdict (accepted|redirected), choice, why, risk, taskId, by

The durable record survives a re-review that regenerates t.reviews[].decisions — accept/redirect history persists for the task's life, independent of the volatile per-review flags (fixes the #193 persistence finding)
A directorDecisions() store accessor reads the record back; chalk decisions surfaces the director's accepted/redirected calls
.chalk/director.jsonl is spine state — in SPINE_STATE_PATHS so it is excluded from review diffs and committed by intake (no bookkeeping churn in feature diffs)

issue.body:
Part of the **director-loop** milestone — EPIC B (judgment compounds). This is the foundation for the moat (seam-03).

## Problem

Accept/redirect resolutions live on `t.reviews[].decisions` — per-task, tied to the **latest** review, and **regenerated on re-review** (the #193 adversarial reviewer explicitly flagged this: a re-review drops prior accepted/redirected flags, so resolutions don't persist over a task's life). For judgment to **compound**, decisions need a durable, queryable record independent of the volatile review array.

## Acceptance sketch (to be locked at spec time)

- Accept/redirect (`chalk pending`) write through to a **durable** record — `{ choice, why, risk, taskId, verdict: accepted|redirected, at, by }` — e.g. structured entries in `decisions.md` or a new `.chalk/director.jsonl`.
- The record **survives re-review** (unlike `t.reviews[].decisions`).
- A read accessor (e.g. `directorDecisions(store)`) returns them for query/injection.
- Surfaced to the human via `chalk decisions` (or a new view).
- Covered by a locked test (including the survives-re-review property).

## Touchpoints
- `lib/store.mjs` (the record + accessor), `bin/chalk.mjs` (`pending` accept/redirect write-through).

## Dependencies
None. Also **resolves the #193 persistence finding**. Enables #202.

findings.note: Criterion 2's 'survives a re-review' test never invokes the real runReview path — it hand-rewrites tasks.json to simulate regeneration. The durability holds trivially because director.jsonl is a separate file, but no test proves runReview actually leaves the record intact end-to-end. Adequate given the separate-file design, but the assertion is weaker than the criterion's wording implies.

No de-duplication: because the per-review accepted/redirected flag is regenerated away on re-review, re-accepting the same decision after a re-review appends a second director.jsonl entry (the die('already resolved') guard only sees the volatile flag). The compounding record can accrue duplicate calls for one underlying decision. Likely acceptable for an append-only log, but unbounded and untested.

The 'why' field is semantically overloaded: for an accepted call it stores the decision's original rationale (d.rationale), for a redirected call it stores the human's course-correction. A downstream consumer (#202 context feed) reading 'why' gets two different meanings depending on verdict; no field distinguishes 'author's reason' from 'director's instruction'.

decisions.choice: Store the durable director record as append-only JSONL at .chalk/director.jsonl, git-tracked as spine state
decisions.rationale: Append-only survives re-review regeneration and is the substrate for the #202 compounding-context moat; spine-state classification keeps it out of feature review diffs

decisions.choice: Reuse the existing emitUpdate type 'decision-logged' for director accept/redirect events
decisions.rationale: Avoids introducing a new event type; but conflates director calls with the prose decision log for any consumer filtering on that type

decisions.choice: Default the 'by' provenance field to 'human' when --by is absent
decisions.rationale: Accept/redirect are director actions, so 'human' is the sensible default; but an agent-driven `chalk run` accept would be mislabeled as human

decisions.choice: Map accepted decision's 'why' to the decision's original rationale and redirected's 'why' to the course-correction
decisions.rationale: Reuses one field for both verdicts to keep the schema flat

reviews.note: locked test amended after review — re-review required

findings.note: Criterion 1 literally enumerates the field `why`, but the record ships no `why` field — the implementer split it into `rationale` (agent's reason) and `instruction` (director's course-correction, redirect-only). This is a defensible, better-normalized design that #202 downstream depends on, and the locked test pins it — but it is a deviation from the written contract's field list that a director should knowingly ratify rather than have silently substituted.

director.jsonl is append-only with no dedup. Because the resolve-guard (`d.accepted||d.redirected`) lives on the volatile t.reviews[].decisions flag, a re-review that regenerates decisions clears that guard — so re-accepting/re-redirecting the same decision after re-review appends a second (possibly conflicting) durable entry for the same choice/taskId. No test covers this re-resolve path.

The 'survives re-review' test hand-rewrites tasks.json rather than driving runReview, so it proves only that a separate file isn't touched (nearly tautological) — it does not exercise the real regeneration path or that accept still functions correctly after a genuine re-review. directorDecisions() is also only tested indirectly via `chalk decisions`, never for its own return shape.

decisions.choice: Model the durable record with distinct `rationale` (agent) and `instruction` (director) fields instead of the single `why` field named in the acceptance criteria
decisions.rationale: Keeping the agent's original reason separate from the director's course-correction is needed for the compounding-context feed (#202) to say 'apply this rationale' vs 'do this instead'

decisions.choice: Snapshot the computed risk via decisionRisk(d) into the record at write time rather than recomputing on read
decisions.rationale: Freezes the risk classification as-of the director's call so later logic changes don't retroactively alter history

decisions.choice: Append-only JSONL with no dedup/supersede semantics for re-resolved decisions
decisions.rationale: Simplest durable substrate; treats every director call as an immutable event

decisions.choice: Default `by` to 'human' when --by is absent
decisions.rationale: Most accept/redirect calls come from a human director at the CLI

decisions.choice: Surface the durable record as a new 'Director's calls' section appended to `chalk decisions` rather than a dedicated command
decisions.rationale: Co-locates director judgment history with the existing prose decision log
