issue.body:
Part of the **director-loop** milestone — EPIC A (redirect actually re-directs).

## Problem

A re-opened task carrying a director correction (#198) with the correction in its context (#199) must actually flow back through work → verify → done, and the directive be **marked resolved** on completion — otherwise the loop never closes and the inbox/task state drifts.

## Acceptance sketch (to be locked at spec time)

- `chalk work` / `chalk run` treat a redirected (re-opened) task as **runnable** and re-execute it.
- On successful completion (verify green → `done`), the task's outstanding director directives are marked **resolved**.
- A task with unresolved directives is **surfaced** — e.g. `chalk next` / `chalk status` notes "N director correction(s) pending rework" so it isn't silently stranded.
- Covered by a locked test: redirect → work → directive resolved end-to-end.

## Touchpoints
- `lib/run.mjs` (driver), `bin/chalk.mjs` (`work`/`done`, `next`/`status`), `runnableTasks` in `lib/store.mjs`.

## Dependencies
Depends on **#198** and **#199**. Closes EPIC A — the visible loop.

findings.note: Criterion 2 explicitly requires that BOTH `chalk done` AND the pipeline merge resolve pending directives. Only the `chalk done` path (bin/chalk.mjs:1601) is tested. The pipeline-merge resolution added at bin/chalk.mjs:947 has NO test — reverting that single line leaves the entire locked suite green. That production auto-merge path (used by `chalk run`) ships directive-resolution behavior unverified, so a regression there would be silent. Per the coverage rule this is a vacuous pass for half of criterion 2.

runnableTasks now re-admits any in-progress task carrying an unresolved directive. A redirect on an already in-progress task (NOT a done→reopen) also attaches an unresolved directive (chalk.mjs:1940 pushes resolved:false regardless of reopen), so such a task becomes 'runnable' and could be re-fanned-out by `chalk run --parallel` while it is actively being worked. The tests only exercise the clean re-opened case; concurrent-pick / double-execution against an in-flight worktree is unverified.

`chalk done` resolves pending directives independent of `reopenedAt`, but `chalk next`'s '(re-opened for rework)' banner keys off `reopenedAt` while the pending-corrections block keys off pendingDirectives. A directive added to a task that was never done (no reopenedAt) will surface the '↻ pending rework' block without the 're-opened' banner — an inconsistent surfacing state the tests don't cover.

decisions.choice: Model a re-opened task by overloading state='in-progress' + an unresolved directive rather than introducing a dedicated 'reopened'/'redirected' state
decisions.rationale: Reuses existing state machine and the done-gate's `state==='in-progress'` guard so no new transitions are needed; runnableTasks distinguishes via pendingDirectives

decisions.choice: `chalk done` and pipeline merge resolve ALL pending directives on the task, not only those a re-open was triggered for
decisions.rationale: Completing the task is treated as satisfying every outstanding correction; keeps resolution logic a single filter with no per-directive targeting

decisions.choice: Surface pending corrections in `chalk next` inline under the in-progress list with the literal 'instead' instruction, rather than as a separate section or gate
decisions.rationale: Keeps the redirect visible in the normal next-action flow so it isn't stranded, minimal output change

findings.note: Criterion 2's pipeline-merge resolution path is only verified by grepping bin/chalk.mjs for `resolveDirectives(t)` occurrences (>=2). This catches a straight revert of the call site but does NOT behaviorally exercise the merge path — it can't detect the call being placed on a dead branch, resolving the wrong task, or firing before the merge actually lands. The `chalk done` path, by contrast, is properly integration-tested.

reopenedAt is set on done→redirect but never cleared (resolveDirectives only stamps directives). A task that was once re-opened, reworked, and returned to in-progress will still have reopenedAt set; a subsequent redirect while it is ACTIVE (never going back through done) would satisfy needsRework and re-admit it — the very 'active-redirect double-execution' case the design claims to exclude. Narrow corner, but the exclusion invariant relies on reopenedAt only ever coexisting with a done→reopen, which isn't guaranteed over a task's lifetime.

needsRework gates purely on reopenedAt + unresolved directive and ignores task.state, while runnableTasks separately ORs it with state==='specd'. A done task that gets a fresh directive without state flipping (e.g., an external mutation) would be judged needsRework=true by the helper in isolation; the surfacing in `chalk next` only shows it because it iterates the wip list, so behavior is coupled to callers filtering by state rather than the helper itself.

decisions.choice: Gate re-admission on a dedicated reopenedAt marker (set only on done→redirect) rather than 'in-progress + any unresolved directive'
decisions.rationale: Prevents a redirect issued against an already-active task from re-admitting it to the driver and double-executing in-flight work

decisions.choice: Do not clear reopenedAt when directives are resolved; rely on state transitions (done) to drop the task out of runnableTasks
decisions.rationale: Simpler completion path via the shared resolveDirectives helper; treats reopenedAt as a durable historical stamp

decisions.choice: Verify the second (pipeline-merge) completion path with a source-text grep assertion instead of a behavioral integration test
decisions.rationale: Spinning up a full PR-merge pipeline in-test is heavy; the grep guards against silent removal of the call site

decisions.choice: Surface re-opened rework inline within the existing `chalk next` in-progress loop (banner + pending corrections) rather than as a distinct triage section
decisions.rationale: Reuses the wip rendering so a re-opened task isn't stranded as plain in-progress, with minimal new output surface

reviews.note: locked test amended after review — re-review required

findings.note: The pipeline-merge completion path (criterion 2's 'and the pipeline merge') is only covered by a brittle SOURCE-GREP assertion counting `resolveDirectives(t)` occurrences >= 2. No behavioral test drives a re-opened task through the merge path to assert directives actually resolve there. A refactor that renames the arg (e.g. resolveDirectives(task)) breaks the test without a real regression, and a call that is present-but-broken would still pass. The done path is genuinely integration-tested; the merge path is not.

Criterion 2 says both completion paths resolve corrections 'and reports it'. The `chalk done` path appends '· N director correction(s) resolved' to its output, but the pipeline-merge path calls resolveDirectives silently — its emitUpdate only says 'Merged + cleaned', with no mention of resolved corrections. The merge path partially misses the 'reports it' half of the criterion.

runnableTasks now returns some in-progress tasks (re-opened ones). doctor.mjs feeds runnableTasks into the testless/backlog-quality check and chalk.mjs line 340 uses it for empty-queue detection; a re-opened task with no test would now be flagged runnable-but-testless. Behaviorally reasonable but a subtly widened surface not directly asserted by the new tests.

needsRework ignores task.state (gates purely on reopenedAt + pending directives); it is runnableTasks that ORs with state==='specd'. A done task carrying a stale reopenedAt + fresh unresolved directive from an external mutation would be judged needsRework=true by the helper in isolation. Safe only because callers filter by state — coupling correctness to caller discipline rather than the helper.

decisions.choice: Gate re-admission on a dedicated `reopenedAt` marker (set only on done→redirect) rather than the criterion's literal 'in-progress + any unresolved directive'
decisions.rationale: Prevents a directive added to an ALREADY-active task from re-admitting it to the driver and double-executing in-flight work under chalk run --parallel

decisions.choice: resolveDirectives CLEARS reopenedAt when the rework lands, treating it as a transient re-open flag rather than a durable historical stamp
decisions.rationale: So a stale re-open marker can never coexist with a later active-redirect and re-admit an in-flight task; keeps the 'reopenedAt ⇒ awaiting rework' invariant true for the task's whole lifetime — at the cost of losing the audit trail of when a task was re-opened

decisions.choice: Assert the pipeline-merge resolution via a source-code regex test instead of a behavioral end-to-end merge test
decisions.rationale: Cheap way to guard against silently reverting one of the two call sites without standing up a full PR/merge fixture

decisions.choice: Merge path resolves directives silently (no user-facing 'corrections resolved' report) while done reports it
decisions.rationale: Merge output already emits a work-item-accepted update; implementer chose not to add directive-count reporting there

findings.note: Criterion 2 explicitly covers 'the pipeline merge' path, but no test exercises that code path end-to-end — it is only asserted by a source-grep counting `resolveDirectives(t)` call sites (>=2). The grep would still pass if the merge-path call were placed but dead/unreached, or if resolveDirectives were subtly wrong for the merge context. The `chalk done` path is genuinely integration-tested; the pipeline merge is not. Non-vacuous overall (resolveDirectives is unit-tested + done path is real), so not blocking, but the merge branch's actual behavior is unverified.

runnableTasks now returns some in-progress (re-opened) tasks, widening a helper long assumed to return only specd tasks. doctor.mjs:100-104 feeds it into the testless-backlog check: a re-opened task whose tests array is empty would now be flagged runnable-but-testless (fail w/o reviewer gate). Also run.mjs:77 comment ('runnableTasks only returns specd tasks') is now stale/misleading. Behaviorally the driver re-start (t.state='in-progress' again) is idempotent so re-execution works, but the widened surface is not directly asserted by the new tests.

needsRework gates purely on reopenedAt + pending directive and ignores task.state; correctness of the 'no double-run of active work' guarantee depends entirely on reopenedAt being set ONLY on a done→redirect and cleared on resolve. That invariant lives in A1 (#198) code not in this diff — if any other path ever sets reopenedAt on an active task, an in-flight task gets re-admitted and double-executed. Coupling correctness to caller discipline rather than the helper itself.

decisions.choice: Key re-admission on a dedicated reopenedAt marker rather than the literal criterion wording 'in-progress + unresolved directive'
decisions.rationale: A directive added to an ALREADY-active task would otherwise re-admit and double-execute in-flight work under chalk run --parallel; reopenedAt distinguishes a done→reopen from a live redirect

decisions.choice: Clear reopenedAt inside resolveDirectives (delete the marker on rework completion) instead of relying on the done-state transition to drop it from runnableTasks
decisions.rationale: Prevents a stale reopenedAt from coexisting with a future fresh directive and re-admitting a task later; keeps the reopenedAt⇒awaiting-rework invariant lifetime-true

decisions.choice: Make re-opened tasks report as in-progress-but-runnable (widen runnableTasks to return non-specd tasks)
decisions.rationale: Reuses the existing state machine and the done-gate's state==='in-progress' guard so no new transition is needed

decisions.choice: Surface pending corrections only via chalk next's existing wip iteration (behavior coupled to callers filtering by state) rather than centralizing in the helper
decisions.rationale: Minimal diff reusing the wip loop; but means a done task with a stale reopenedAt+fresh directive would read needsRework=true in isolation

title: feat(director-loop): A2 · inject pending director corrections into buildContext

acceptanceCriteria.text: buildContext surfaces a task's unresolved directives as a '### Director corrections (REBUILD to these)' block naming the corrected choice + what to do instead
Only UNRESOLVED directives are injected — a resolved directive is not re-surfaced
No directives → no block (no regression to existing context)
The corrections block is ESSENTIAL — never dropped for the context budget (only the elastic lessons block is trimmed), like the review-findings block it mirrors

issue.body:
Part of the **director-loop** milestone — EPIC A (redirect actually re-directs).

## Problem

Even once a task is re-opened with a directive (#198), the executor's next `chalk work` run can't *see* the correction. `buildContext` already surfaces prior **review** findings (lib/store.mjs, the `### Address these review findings` block) but nothing for director redirects.

## Acceptance sketch (to be locked at spec time)

- `buildContext` includes a `### Director corrections (rebuild to these)` block listing the current task's **unresolved** directives (the choice that was rejected → what to do instead + why).
- The block is an **essential** section (never dropped for the context budget), exactly like the review-findings block it mirrors.
- The block is **absent** when the task has no unresolved directives (no empty header, no regression to existing context).
- Covered by a locked test asserting the directive text appears in `buildContext` output.

## Touchpoints
- `lib/store.mjs` — `buildContext` (mirror the existing review-findings block at ~lines 564–568).

## Dependencies
Depends on **#198** (the directive must exist on the task). Feeds #200.

findings.note: `dir.instead` has no fallback (unlike `dir.choice` which defaults to 'your earlier choice'). A directive with a missing/empty `instead` renders '...: undefined' or a dangling colon. A1 (#198) presumably guarantees `instead` is populated, but buildContext doesn't defend against it; no test covers a directive lacking `instead`.

Multiple-directive rendering (a task with two unresolved directives) is never exercised — only single-directive cases. The loop is trivial so risk is low, but ordering/formatting of stacked corrections is unverified.

The 'ESSENTIAL' test infers essentialness only indirectly: it asserts the correction survives while 'elided' appears for lessons. It does not construct a case where the correction would compete with lessons for the SAME bytes (essentials are computed before lessons regardless), so it proves the block is in `post` but not that it was a deliberate budget priority over a borderline lessons trim. Adequate for the criterion as written.

decisions.choice: Placed the Director corrections block immediately after the review-findings block, inside the `if (task)` branch and within `post` (the always-kept essentials array)
decisions.rationale: Mirrors the review-findings block so corrections are never budget-dropped; keeps human redirections adjacent to prior-review fixes in the executor's reading order

decisions.choice: Consumes a `task.directives` array with shape {choice, instead, resolved, at, by} and filters on truthy `!x.resolved`
decisions.rationale: Assumes A1 (#198) writes this durable schema; unresolved = pending correction

decisions.choice: Fallback text 'your earlier choice' for a missing `choice`, but no fallback for a missing `instead`
decisions.rationale: Treats `instead` as the always-present payload of a directive

decisions.choice: Rendered as free-text markdown prose in context rather than a structured/actionable field the executor can programmatically ack or resolve
decisions.rationale: Consistency with the existing review-findings presentation; keeps A2 scoped to context injection, leaving resolution to a later slice

title: feat(director-loop): A1 · redirect re-opens the task as an actionable directive

acceptanceCriteria.text: chalk pending redirect records a durable directive on the task (t.directives[] = { choice, instead, at, by, resolved:false }) — the correction becomes actionable work, not just a log line
Redirecting a DONE task re-opens it to in-progress (reopenedAt stamped) so it can be reworked to the director's call
Redirecting a non-done (already active) task keeps its state and only attaches the directive (no spurious re-open)
accept does NOT create a directive or re-open the task — only redirect re-directs

issue.body:
Part of the **director-loop** milestone — EPIC A (redirect actually re-directs). Follows #191–193.

## Problem

`chalk pending redirect <task>#<n> "why"` (shipped in #193) only sets `d.redirected` on the review decision, appends a line to `decisions.md`, and drops the item from the inbox. **The correction never becomes work** — the task stays `done`, the agent never rebuilds. A redirect has to make the call *actionable*.

## Acceptance sketch (to be locked at spec time)

- A redirect records a durable **directive** on the task — `{ choice, instead (the "why"/what-to-do), at, by, resolved:false }` — not just a `decisions.md` line.
- Redirecting a `done`/reviewed task transitions it back to a **runnable** state (e.g. `in-progress` or `specd`), flagged as needing rework per the director's correction.
- Redirecting an `in-progress` task keeps its state but attaches the directive.
- The redirected decision leaves the inbox (as today via `d.redirected`); the task now carries an **unresolved directive** until rework completes (resolved in #200).
- Covered by a locked test.

## Touchpoints
- `bin/chalk.mjs` — the `pending` command's `redirect` branch.
- The task state machine (`TASK_STATES`) + spine.

## Dependencies
None — builds directly on the shipped `chalk pending` (#193). Enables #199 (context injection) and #200 (re-run + resolve).

findings.note: Re-opening a DONE task only flips state→in-progress and stamps reopenedAt; it leaves any stale done-artifacts intact (e.g. t.pr/mergedAt, prior verify/review state). A previously-merged/released task now appearing as in-progress with those artifacts could confuse downstream (`chalk next`, audit, release, done-gate). No test asserts what happens to those fields, but this is outside the stated criteria.

The redirect emitUpdate ('progress-update') message string and the '— task re-opened for rework' output, plus the appendDirectorDecision/appendDecision durable records, are unasserted cosmetics — harmless, and the four core behaviors (directive shape, done→reopen, non-done no-reopen, accept-no-directive) are each covered and would fail if the change were reverted.

emitUpdate uses generic type 'progress-update' for a redirect, while accept uses 'work-item-accepted'. A stored prior decision in tasks.json says to reuse 'decision-logged' for director accept/redirect events; the chosen type is inconsistent with both that note and the accept path. Cosmetic but worth confirming.

decisions.choice: Re-open a redirected DONE task to 'in-progress' (rather than a dedicated 'redirected'/'reopened' state or back to 'todo')
decisions.rationale: Reuses the existing active state so the executor's next `chalk work` picks it up; minimal new vocabulary

decisions.choice: On re-open, only flip state + stamp reopenedAt; do not clear done-artifacts (pr, mergedAt, verify/review results)
decisions.rationale: Keeps the diff small and scoped to the criteria; the directive drives rework

decisions.choice: Directive schema fixed to { choice, instead, at, by, resolved:false } with choice defaulting to '' when the decision has none
decisions.rationale: Matches criterion 1's shape and keeps directives self-describing for the #199/#200 executor read

decisions.choice: Redirect emits a generic 'progress-update' event type
decisions.rationale: Reuses an existing event type rather than introducing a director-specific one

title: feat(director-mid-flight): C3 · raised forks pause the task + route to the inbox

acceptanceCriteria.text: After a chalk work run, a task with OPEN raises does not proceed: chalk work exits 2 and the driver blocks it needs:decision — a guessed choice never ships past a raised fork
chalk pending surfaces open raised forks (fork + options + why) across tasks, each with an answer ref

chalk pending answer <raiseId> "<decision>" marks the raise answered, feeds the answer back as a directive (#199 channel so the next work rebuilds to it), compounds it to the durable director record (#201/#202), and unblocks a task parked on the raise
Once the raise is answered, chalk work proceeds (no open raises left) — the mid-flight loop is closed

issue.body:
Part of the **director-mid-flight** milestone — EPIC C. Wire raises into the closed loop.

## Problem
A raised fork (#209) must actually PAUSE the work and reach the director — then the answer must travel back so the agent proceeds with it. This reuses the director-loop machinery (inbox #193, context injection #199, compounding #201/#202).

## Acceptance sketch (to be locked at spec time)
- After a `chalk work` run, a task with OPEN raises blocks (needs `decision`) instead of proceeding (exit 2 → pipeline/driver auto-block), so a guessed choice never ships.
- `chalk pending` surfaces open raised forks (with their options/why) alongside review-derived calls, each with a ref.
- Answering a raise (e.g. `chalk pending answer <ref> "<decision>"`, or reuse accept/redirect) records the answer, **injects it into the task's context** (reuse the #199 directive/corrections channel) and **unblocks** the task so the next `chalk work` proceeds with the director's call — and it **compounds** into future context (#202).
- Locked test: work-with-open-raise blocks; pending shows it; answering unblocks + lands in context.

## Touchpoints
`bin/chalk.mjs` (`work` gate, `pending` surface + answer), `lib/run.mjs` (driver block), `lib/store.mjs` (context feed).

## Dependencies
Depends on **#209** and **#210**. Closes EPIC C — mid-flight raising wired into the loop.

findings.note: Criterion 1 requires the driver to block a raise-parked task with needs:decision, but lib/run.mjs calls blockTask(...) with no needs arg, so it defaults to 'human-input' (blockTask signature: needs='human-input'). The block is therefore mislabeled versus the contract.

End-to-end break: the answer/unblock logic in `pending answer` only unblocks when `t.block?.needs === 'decision'`. Since the driver actually parks the task with needs:'human-input', answering a raise will NOT unblock a task the driver blocked — directly defeating criteria 3 ('unblocks a task parked on the raise') and 4 for the real driver path.

The locked test masks the above: repo() for the unblock case hardcodes `block:{needs:'decision'}` instead of producing the block via the driver. No test drives runDriver's raise-block path or asserts the needs value it sets, so the mismatch between code ('human-input') and the compensating unblock check ('decision') is never exercised. Reverting the run.mjs needs behavior (or the criterion's decision label) would still pass the suite — a vacuous pass on the driver path.

Criterion 4's test answers a raise on a task that is in-progress (not blocked), so the unblock-then-proceed transition is never verified as a single flow; 'work proceeds' is only checked in isolation from the block/unblock it depends on in practice.

pending now prints 'Raised forks' before the Director inbox and returns undefined (not ok()) when only raises exist and no judgment calls remain; the empty-inbox exit path was reworked. No test asserts exit code / ok-line behavior for the mixed (raises + judgment calls) case, so the inbox-ranking output contract is only partially covered.

decisions.choice: Pause on a raised fork by exiting 2 from `chalk work` and letting the pipeline/driver auto-block, mirroring the plan-approval/criteria gates
decisions.rationale: Reuses the existing exit-2 → auto-block convention rather than inventing a new pause mechanism

decisions.choice: Unblock is gated on block.needs==='decision' specifically
decisions.rationale: Intends to only revive tasks parked by a raise, not other blocks

decisions.choice: Answered raises are recorded as a new director-record verdict 'answered' (distinct from accepted/redirected), and rendered as its own line in the compounding taste feed
decisions.rationale: Keeps mid-flight fork answers semantically separate from post-hoc review calls

decisions.choice: Raised forks are surfaced ABOVE the med/high-risk judgment-call inbox in `chalk pending`
decisions.rationale: Agent-initiated forks are treated as higher urgency than review-surfaced calls

decisions.choice: Answer resolution matches raiseId by exact-or-prefix and picks the first match across all tasks
decisions.rationale: Convenience for short ids typed from the pending list

findings.note: The `why` field display in `chalk pending` (criterion 2 says fork+options+why) is never asserted — the test raise has no `why`, so a regression that dropped `why` rendering would go uncaught.

The new `directorLines` 'answered' branch in store.mjs (labels an answered raise distinctly in the #202 compounding taste feed injected into future agents) has no test. Reverting just that hunk fails nothing — an answered decision would silently render as 'accepted'. The durable *record* write is tested; its rendering back into agent context is not.

`chalk pending` empty-state message text changed and the return path now yields `undefined` when raises exist but no review decisions do; no test pins the empty message, so low risk, but the behavior of `pending` with-raises-only prints no closing 'inbox empty' line by design.

driver e2e re-run after answering: the executor stub literally re-runs `chalk raise`, which would re-raise the same fork and re-block. Harmless in the product (answer feeds back as a directive so a real agent stops re-raising), and openRaises correctly filters to status:'open' so answered raises don't re-trigger — loop closes as specified.

decisions.choice: Block a raised-fork task with needs:'decision' (not the driver's default 'human-input')
decisions.rationale: `chalk pending answer` keys its auto-unblock on block.needs==='decision', so the value is load-bearing coupling between the block reason and the answer path

decisions.choice: Merge raised forks into the existing `chalk pending` command (shown above the review inbox) rather than a dedicated `chalk raises`/inbox surface
decisions.rationale: One director inbox for both mid-flight forks and post-review judgment calls keeps the director's attention in a single place

decisions.choice: Answer feeds back through the same `t.directives` (#199) 'Instead of X: Y' channel used by redirects, with resolved:false
decisions.rationale: Reuses the proven buildContext injection so the next work rebuilds to the decision without a new mechanism

decisions.choice: Auto-unblock only when state==='blocked' && needs==='decision' && no open raises remain; multiple open raises on one task each need answering before resume
decisions.rationale: Avoids resuming a task that still has unanswered forks and avoids touching tasks blocked for other reasons

decisions.choice: Run the executor first, then check for raises and discard the run — the work/driver still executes the agent before pausing
decisions.rationale: The raise is written to the spine during the run, so the check must come after; but a task pre-carrying an open raise still pays a wasted executor run

reviews.note: locked test amended after review — re-review required

findings.note: The open-raise gate is enforced only in `chalk work` (bin) and `runDriver` (run.mjs), not in `chalk done`. A raise generally can't reach done because work exits 2 before verify, but there's no direct guard on done — if a task were otherwise green/reviewed it could in principle be marked done with an open raise. Not covered by criteria or tests.

`answer` resolves the raise id via prefix match (`x.id.startsWith(rid)`) and takes the FIRST match across all tasks. Ambiguous short prefixes could answer the wrong fork silently; no disambiguation or collision guard. Tests only use full ids.

The `chalk pending` empty-state message text changed ('no med/high-risk judgment calls awaiting you.' → 'no raised forks or judgment calls awaiting you.'). Confirmed no existing test asserts the old string, so safe, but it is a user-facing copy change bundled in.

Criterion 3's '#199 feed-back' is asserted only by presence of the directive object on the task, not by verifying buildContext actually renders it into the next work prompt. Verified manually (store.mjs line 655 consumes dir.choice/dir.instead, matching the pushed shape) so the feed-back is real, but the locked test doesn't exercise that render path; the `--options`/why rendering in pending also lacks a 'why' case.

decisions.choice: Block a raised task as needs:'decision' rather than the default 'human-input'
decisions.rationale: `chalk pending answer` only unblocks tasks whose block.needs==='decision', so this coupling is what lets answering resume the parked task; distinguishes an intentional director fork from an executor-can't-make-green stall

decisions.choice: `chalk work` exits code 2 on an open raise (mirrors the driver auto-block-needs-decision convention)
decisions.rationale: Signals the pipeline/driver to auto-block rather than treating it as a hard failure or silent proceed

decisions.choice: An answered raise is dual-written: a transient task directive (resolved:false, feeds next work) AND a durable director.jsonl record with a new verdict:'answered'
decisions.rationale: Directive drives the immediate rebuild (#199); the durable record makes it compound as taste (#201/#202) and stop recurring

decisions.choice: New 'answered' verdict rendered as its own line in directorLines ('answered: fork → decision'), distinct from accepted/redirected
decisions.rationale: Keeps a mid-flight fork semantically separate from a post-hoc accept so future context reads truthfully

decisions.choice: Surface raised forks ABOVE the review judgment-call inbox in `chalk pending` output
decisions.rationale: A raise is an explicit blocking ask, so it's prioritized over accept/redirect triage

decisions.choice: Task is only unblocked when NO open raises remain (guarded), leaving it parked if other forks are still open
decisions.rationale: Prevents resuming work while an unanswered fork would still force another guess

title: feat(director-mid-flight): C2 · executor contract — raise a fork instead of guessing

acceptanceCriteria.text: buildContext injects a mid-flight raise instruction telling the executor to run chalk raise for a fork the criteria don't answer, and to raise only the few that need taste (not flood)

The raise instruction is a LOW-priority elastic context block — present at any realistic budget but first to yield under extreme pressure, so the essential/director/lessons budget the locked context-budget tests pin stays unchanged
Both chalk-executor definitions (shipped share/agents + dogfood .claude/agents) document the raise convention and stay in sync (agents-sync drift gate green)

issue.body:
Part of the **director-mid-flight** milestone — EPIC C. The executor contract.

## Problem
`chalk raise` (#209) exists, but the agent won't use it unless its contract tells it to — and tells it WHEN (a genuine fork needing the director's taste, not every micro-choice).

## Acceptance sketch (to be locked at spec time)
- `buildContext` includes a raise instruction: when you hit a fork that needs the director's judgment (architecture, a real tradeoff, an ambiguous requirement), run `chalk raise "<fork>"` instead of silently picking — it pauses for the director. Emphasise: raise the FEW that need taste, not everything (no raise-flooding).
- The shipped + dogfood `chalk-executor` agent definitions describe the raise convention (kept in sync — the agents-sync drift gate stays green).
- Locked test (context carries the instruction; both agent defs describe it).

## Touchpoints
`lib/store.mjs` (buildContext), `share/agents/chalk-executor.md` + `.claude/agents/chalk-executor.md`.

## Dependencies
Depends on **#209**. Feeds #211.

findings.note: Criterion 2 claims the raise block is elastic — 'first to yield under extreme pressure' — but the new locked test only asserts the instruction is PRESENT at default budget. No test drives buildContext under a tiny contextBudget to prove the raise block actually drops while essentials/director/lessons survive. If the raiseFits budget guard were deleted (block always emitted), the new test would still pass, so the 'yields first' behavior is effectively unverified except indirectly via the pre-existing locked context-budget tests.

RAISE_INSTRUCTION's copy is duplicated/independent from the full convention in the two chalk-executor.md files; there is no gate keeping the terse in-context wording aligned with the executor-def wording, so they can drift silently (the agents-sync gate only checks the two .md files against each other, not against store.mjs).

raiseBlock adds bytes to every task context at realistic budgets; verify is assumed green, but any budget test asserting total-output size rather than just essential-survival would be sensitive to this addition. Worth confirming the locked context-budget tests pass unchanged.

decisions.choice: Emit the raise block as the lowest-priority elastic section, computed after and subtracting essential+director+lessons bytes, placed just before the task 'post' section
decisions.rationale: Keeps the pinned essential/director/lessons budgets untouched so locked context-budget tests stay green while still surfacing the instruction at any realistic budget

decisions.choice: Duplicate the raise guidance: a terse one-liner injected into context (store.mjs) plus the full convention in both executor definitions
decisions.rationale: Context stays compact under budget pressure while the authoritative long-form lives in the agent contract

decisions.choice: Gate the raise block on `task` being present (no raise instruction in task-less context)
decisions.rationale: The instruction is only meaningful mid-task, so skip it when there is no current task

decisions.choice: For shell-less executors, instruct surfacing the fork in the one-line summary instead of failing
decisions.rationale: Graceful degradation so executors without a shell tool can still escalate a fork to a human

reviews.note: locked test amended after review — re-review required

findings.note: The elasticity test only checks the two extremes (default budget vs budget=1). It never asserts the ordering claim in criterion 2 that the raise block yields *before* lessons/director under moderate pressure — a bug swapping raise ahead of lessons in the budget calc would still pass all three tests as long as essentials survive at budget=1.

The terse RAISE_INSTRUCTION string in lib/store.mjs and the full 'Raise a fork instead of guessing' section in the two .md files are independent copies of the same convention. The agents-sync drift gate only compares the two .md files to each other; nothing pins the in-code injected wording to the executor-def wording, so they can drift silently (e.g. flag names like --options/--why change in one but not the other).

buildContext now emits raiseBlock between lessons and the essential 'post' section at any budget with leftover headroom. Locked context-budget tests are claimed green, but any downstream consumer that asserted exact full-context output or 'lessons is the last elastic block' would see new bytes; the guard protects essential/director/lessons byte-budgets but not exact-output snapshots.

decisions.choice: Injected raise guidance as a NEW lowest-priority elastic block appended after director+lessons, gated by a leftover-budget check (raiseFits), rather than folding it into the always-present essential contract text.
decisions.rationale: Keeps the locked essential/director/lessons budget math untouched so pinned context-budget tests stay green, while still surfacing the instruction at realistic budgets.

decisions.choice: Gated the raise block on `task` being present (no task ⇒ no raise instruction).
decisions.rationale: The raise convention is only meaningful mid-task, so it's suppressed for taskless context calls.

decisions.choice: Duplicated the convention: a terse one-liner in code + a full prose section in both executor defs, instead of a single sourced string.
decisions.rationale: Context budget favors terseness in-band while the agent definition can afford the full explanation; accepted the copy-drift risk.

decisions.choice: Fallback instruction for shell-less executors: 'surface the fork in your one-line summary' so a human can chalk raise it.
decisions.rationale: chalk raise needs shell access; without a graceful fallback, non-shell executors would be told to run an unavailable command.

title: feat(director-mid-flight): C1 · chalk raise — the mid-flight raise primitive

acceptanceCriteria.text: chalk raise "<fork>" [--options a|b|c] [--why ...] [--task <id>] records a raise on the target task's t.raised[]: {id, fork, options?, why?, at, by:'agent', status:'open'}
Defaults to the current in-progress task; refuses cleanly when there is none and no --task
options parse from a pipe-delimited list; chalk raise with no fork text lists the open raised forks; openRaises(task) accessor returns only open raises

issue.body:
Part of the **director-mid-flight** milestone — EPIC C (the agent works "out loud"). The raise primitive.

## Problem
All decision surfacing today is POST-HOC: the reviewer digests a *finished* diff (#192). The aimed pivot has the agent stop at a fork *during* work and raise it *before* guessing. The executor is BYO, so this is a convention it opts into — starting with a command it can call.

## Acceptance sketch (to be locked at spec time)
- `chalk raise "<the fork>" [--options "a|b|c"] [--why "..."] [--task <id>]` appends a raised fork to the task's `t.raised[]`: `{ id, fork, options?, why?, at, by:'agent', status:'open' }`.
- Defaults to the current in-progress task; refuses cleanly if none and no `--task`.
- A read accessor (e.g. `openRaises(task)` / `raisedTasks(tasks)`) returns unanswered raises; surfaced to the human.
- `.chalk` spine state stays consistent (the raise rides `t.raised`, so it's already inside tasks.json / SPINE_STATE_PATHS).
- Locked test.

## Touchpoints
`bin/chalk.mjs` (new `raise` command + help), `lib/store.mjs` (accessor).

## Dependencies
None. Enables #210 (the contract) and #211 (route into the inbox/loop).

findings.note: The command emits a `progress-update` event (s.emitUpdate) and calls syncBrowser as side effects, but no test asserts either. Not part of the acceptance criteria, so non-blocking, but the update-log integration is unverified.

An undocumented `--by` override (flags.by) can spoof provenance away from 'agent'; criterion says raises are by:'agent'. Harmless for now but no test locks that the CLI default path can't be overridden, and the help text omits --by.
The no-fork listing test only exercises a single task/single raise. Cross-task aggregation (flatMap over s.tasks()) and the 'no open raised forks' empty-state branch are not directly asserted.

decisions.choice: Pipe '|' as the sole --options delimiter, split/trim/filter-empty
decisions.rationale: Matches the criterion's 'pipe-delimited list' and avoids comma collisions with prose options

decisions.choice: raise only RECORDS the fork (status:'open') and does not pause/route the task
decisions.rationale: Pausing + director routing + answer feedback explicitly scoped to #211; C1 is the storage+listing primitive

decisions.choice: Defaults target to the first task with state==='in-progress' via Array.find
decisions.rationale: Mirrors the 'current in-progress task' criterion; single-active-task assumption

decisions.choice: Provenance field `by` defaults to 'agent' but is overridable via flags.by
decisions.rationale: Anticipates future director/human raises while defaulting to agent

decisions.choice: Status vocabulary 'open' vs (test hints) 'answered'
decisions.rationale: openRaises filters status==='open'; downstream states named implicitly by the resolver (#211)

title: feat(director-kit): D3 · reframe the gates as one optional 'Checks' part

acceptanceCriteria.text: chalk harness frames the Checks section as OPTIONAL, the accept button, one part of the kit (not the whole product)
A checks-OFF project (no verify/review/held-out, require-test off) renders a coherent harness with an 'all optional — runs without gates' note — reinforcing checks are not mandatory
chalk harness closes by naming the CORE — the director's taste/judgment (align · digest · pending · raise) — with the gates as one part
docs/harness.md documents the kit and frames the gates as one optional Checks part, with the director's taste/judgment as the defensible core

issue.body:
Part of the **director-kit** milestone — EPIC D. Reframe the gates as one optional "Checks" part.

## Problem
The gates (P1–P7 + verify/regression/review) read today as chalk's WHOLE product. The pivot demotes them to **one part** of the kit — "Checks" — powerful but optional, alongside agents/flows/skills. This is positioning made concrete in the harness view + docs.

## Acceptance sketch (to be locked at spec time)
- `chalk harness` (#216) groups the gates + verify/regression/review under a **"Checks"** section, presented as ONE (optional) part of the kit — with a clear on/off/how-many signal.
- A project with checks minimal/off still renders a coherent harness (Checks just shows "none/optional"), reinforcing they're not mandatory.
- A short docs/help framing: the gates are **Checks** — one composable part, not the whole story (the defensible core is the director's taste/judgment, built in #191–211).
- Locked test.

## Touchpoints
`bin/chalk.mjs` (the harness Checks section), `docs/` (a framing note).

## Dependencies
Depends on **#216** (the view it groups into). Closes EPIC D.

findings.note: The checks-OFF coherence test (criterion 2) only asserts the presence of the 'all optional — runs without gates' note and exit code 0. It does not verify the rest of the harness still renders coherently (Agents/Skills/Flows/core lines) in the everything-off configuration, so a partial breakage of the surrounding output could slip through. Low risk since the existing #216 harness test covers structure on default config.

anyCheck treats review as active only via p.review.command, and regression via p.regression.required — consistent with the dots rendered, but a project that has requiredAt set yet an empty command (or regression.tests without required) would still show the 'all optional' note. Edge, not contradicting the criteria as written.

decisions.choice: Placed the framing entirely in cosmetic output/docs (harness command header text + closing lines + new docs/harness.md) rather than changing any gate behavior or config semantics
decisions.rationale: D3 is a positioning/reframe task; the accept-button demotion is messaging, not a functional change to gating

decisions.choice: Derived the 'all optional — runs without gates' note from a single anyCheck expression (verify||review.command||regression.required||requireTest) shown only when ALL are off
decisions.rationale: Simplest signal that no gate is engaged; reinforces optionality without per-row noise

decisions.choice: Fixed the core mechanisms to the string 'align · digest · pending · raise' as THE director core
decisions.rationale: Names concrete commands as the defensible center; ties messaging to shippable features

decisions.choice: Authored docs/harness.md asserting the gates 'were once framed as the whole product… that framing is commoditizing' — an opinionated product-strategy claim baked into user-facing docs
decisions.rationale: Advances the director-pivot narrative; but it editorializes about market positioning in reference docs

findings.note: Criterion 1 requires the Checks section be framed as 'the accept button, one part of the kit (not the whole product)'. Tests assert the substrings 'OPTIONAL', 'accept button', and 'one part of the kit' appear anywhere in output — they don't assert these are attached to the Checks header specifically. A future edit could satisfy the regex while degrading the framing, but current output is correct.

anyCheck treats a project that has held-out regression tests configured but regression.required=false (or review command empty) as 'no gates', printing the 'runs without gates' note. This matches criterion 2's definition (require-test off, held-out off) but the note keys on 'required'/'command' truthiness rather than presence of config — acceptable for a framing message, worth confirming intent.

director-harness.test.mjs only asserts the literal word 'Checks' is present, which the reframed header still contains; no existing test pins the old 'the gates (P1–P7)' string, so the header text change is safe.

decisions.choice: Defined a checks-OFF project via anyCheck = verify keys || review.command || regression.required || requireTest, printing the 'all optional — runs without gates' note only when all four are falsy
decisions.rationale: Gives criterion 2 a concrete trigger; ties the note to the same signals the dots render

decisions.choice: Named the director-core as exactly 'align · digest · pending · raise' both in the closing harness line and docs, and made docs/harness.md a brand-new standalone file rather than folding into README
decisions.rationale: Pins a canonical four-verb vocabulary for the director-taste 'core' pivot and keeps the manifesto separate from operational README

decisions.choice: Delivered the reframe as pure output/copy changes (no behavior/config change to gate enforcement)
decisions.rationale: Scope is framing/positioning per the D3 pivot; avoids touching enforcement logic

decisions.choice: Baked marketing/positioning language ('not a tool that catches cheating agents', 'the core is not the kit — it's you') into shipped CLI output and docs
decisions.rationale: Advances the director-harness narrative pivot

title: feat(director-kit): D1 · chalk harness — the kit made visible

acceptanceCriteria.text: chalk harness shows the four parts of the kit — Agents, Skills, Checks, Flows — in one read-only view
It reflects actual config: wired agents show their command / unwired show '(not wired)'; configured verify + wired review show as on; project skills (#215) are surfaced
A bare project still renders coherently (none/off states, no crash) — reinforcing the parts are composable, not mandatory
chalk harness is READ-ONLY — it mutates no spine state

issue.body:
Part of the **director-kit** milestone — EPIC D. The kit made visible — "the spine becomes the star."

## Problem
Chalk already HAS the parts — agents (`protocol.executor/planner/reviewer/retro`), checks (the gates + verify/regression/review), flows (run/pipeline/loop/autopilot), and now skills (#215) — but nothing shows them as one assembled **kit**. The composition is invisible, so the "harness" framing isn't legible.

## Acceptance sketch (to be locked at spec time)
- `chalk harness` prints the project's assembled parts, read-only, reflecting actual config:
  - **Agents** — which BYO commands are wired (executor/planner/reviewer/retro) vs. empty.
  - **Checks** — which gates/verify/regression/review are ON (see #217 for the framing).
  - **Flows** — the available drivers (run / pipeline / loop / autopilot).
  - **Skills** — the project skills (#215) count/names.
- Purely informational (no mutation); a bare project and a fully-wired one both render coherently.
- Locked test.

## Touchpoints
`bin/chalk.mjs` (new `harness` command + help), reads `protocol()` + skills.

## Dependencies
Best after **#215** (so it can surface skills). Hosts the #217 Checks framing.

findings.note: Several new output rows ship with no assertion: the 'retro' agent row, the 'held-out' check row, and the 'require-test' check row are all rendered by harness() but no locked test asserts them. If any of these regressed (wrong config key, crash on undefined), the suite would still pass. The core criteria (executor/planner/reviewer, verify, review, skills, flows names) ARE asserted, so this is a coverage gap on secondary rows, not a vacuous pass.

Criterion 2 says the view 'reflects actual config,' but the Flows section is a hardcoded static string ('run · pipeline · loop · autopilot') that does not reflect any config — it's the same in a bare and a fully-wired project. Consistent with the other three parts being config-reflective, Flows silently is not; acceptable since flows aren't config-gated, but worth noting the asymmetry.

harness() calls Store.open() with no guard; outside a spine it will throw and die() rather than render. Tests only run inside an initialized project, so this path is untested. Matches sibling commands' behavior, so likely intended, but the 'no crash' criterion is only proven for a bare *initialized* project.

decisions.choice: Exposed the kit as a new top-level command `chalk harness` rather than a `--kit` flag on `chalk status` or `chalk doctor`.
decisions.rationale: A dedicated read-only 'director's-eye' view keeps status/doctor focused on operational state; harness is purely explanatory.

decisions.choice: Rendered a 'retro' agent row and 'held-out'/'require-test' check rows beyond the four parts named in the criteria, and labeled an empty verify '(none configured — vacuous green)'.
decisions.rationale: Gives a fuller picture of the assembled kit and reuses chalk's existing vacuous-green framing.

decisions.choice: Flows are a fixed informational string, not derived from config.
decisions.rationale: Flows (run/pipeline/loop/autopilot) are always-available commands, not per-project toggles, so there is nothing to reflect.

decisions.choice: Truthiness of command strings drives the on/off dot (e.g. executor?.command), treating empty-string config as 'not wired'.
decisions.rationale: Bare init writes empty-string commands; empty must read as unwired.

reviews.note: locked test amended after review — re-review required

findings.note: Harness reports require-test via plain truthiness (p.requireTest ? 'on' : 'off'), but the actual gate (lib/testgate.mjs) treats it as ON unless === false. For a spine where requireTest is undefined/absent (e.g. an older or hand-edited config), the gate enforces require-test while harness would display 'off' — a misleading divergence. Tests only cover the fresh-init default (true), so this inconsistency is unasserted.

The Flows section is entirely hardcoded static text ('run · pipeline · loop · autopilot') and does not reflect any actual config, unlike Agents/Skills/Checks. This satisfies the letter of criterion #1 (show the four parts) but the row is purely decorative — it can never surface a project-specific or misconfigured flow state.

The READ-ONLY test only diffs tasks.json + chalk.json. It would not catch incidental writes to other spine artifacts (.chalk/local, skills dir, boards). Adequate for the current no-op implementation but a shallow guarantee of the 'mutates no spine state' criterion.

decisions.choice: Named the command `chalk harness` (vs e.g. `kit`, `overview`, `parts`) and slotted it under the setup/status help group
decisions.rationale: 'Harness' matches the product framing ('the kit made visible', the director's harness); placing it near status frames it as an informational read

decisions.choice: Render Flows as fixed prose rather than deriving from configured/available flow commands
decisions.rationale: Flows aren't individually toggled in config the way agents/checks are; a static list communicates the loop shape cheaply

decisions.choice: Model 'require-test on/off' on plain truthiness of protocol.requireTest instead of mirroring the gate's `=== false` default-on semantics
decisions.rationale: Simpler display logic; relies on init writing requireTest:true by default

decisions.choice: Scoped Checks to verify/review/held-out/require-test and Agents to executor/planner/reviewer/retro, omitting other wired stages (discovery, planner-plan, feedback, prbody, handoff, e2e)
decisions.rationale: Keep the view to the core P1–P7 gates and the four primary agents rather than every optional protocol.* command

title: feat(director-kit): D2 · skills as a first-class part (.chalk/skills → context)

acceptanceCriteria.text: chalk skill add "<name>" [--file <path> | "<text>"] writes .chalk/skills/<slug>.md; chalk skill (no sub) lists them; an empty skill is refused
buildContext injects a '## Project skills (apply these)' block from .chalk/skills/*.md, each skill a titled section with its content — the affirmative playbook, distinct from lessons
The skills block is elastic — present at a realistic budget, dropped under extreme pressure while essentials survive (does not disturb the locked context-budget tests)
.chalk/skills is spine state (in SPINE_STATE_PATHS — committed by intake, excluded from review diffs), consistent with lessons.md

issue.body:
Part of the **director-kit** milestone — EPIC D (the kit reframe). Skills as a first-class part. Build FIRST (the harness view #216 shows it).

## Problem
The artifact promotes **skills** — reusable domain how-to — to first-class, but chalk has no project-skills concept (only auto-collected `lessons` and Claude-Code agent-def frontmatter). A project should be able to teach its agents "how we do X here" and have it applied on every task.

## Acceptance sketch (to be locked at spec time)
- `chalk skill add "<name>" [--file <path> | "<text>"]` writes `.chalk/skills/<name>.md`; `chalk skill list` lists them; `chalk skill` (no arg) lists.
- `buildContext` injects a bounded `## Project skills (apply these)` block from `.chalk/skills/*.md` — **elastic like lessons/director-calls**: present at realistic budgets, yields under extreme pressure, essentials never displaced (do NOT disturb the locked context-budget tests).
- `.chalk/skills/` is spine state (in SPINE_STATE_PATHS — committed by intake, excluded from review diffs), consistent with `lessons.md`.
- Locked test.

## Guardrail (avoid framework-creep)
A skill is just **injected reusable text** — NOT a plugin, hook, or executable. Keeps "taste, not framework."

## Touchpoints
`bin/chalk.mjs` (skill command + help), `lib/store.mjs` (skills accessor + buildContext block + path + SPINE_STATE_PATHS).

## Dependencies
None. Feeds #216 (the harness view surfaces skills).

findings.note: Criterion 4's 'committed by intake, excluded from review diffs' behavior is only asserted via SPINE_STATE_PATHS membership, not via actual intake-commit or review-diff exclusion behavior. It relies on that array being the sole mechanism (as with lessons.md), which holds, but the end-to-end behavior is untested.

Adding a skill whose name slugs to an existing file silently overwrites it (writeFileSync, no collision check/confirmation). Two different display names can collide to the same slug and clobber prior content with no warning. Not covered by any test.

Skills are budgeted at HIGHER priority than lessons (skills computed before lessons, taking budget first), so under moderate pressure auto-lessons drop before authored skills. The elastic test only exercises the extreme (budget=1) case where both drop, so the relative-priority intent is asserted nowhere; if the intended ordering were reversed the suite would still pass.

decisions.choice: Rank project skills above auto-lessons in the context budget (skills fit first, lessons get the remainder)
decisions.rationale: Author-curated affirmative playbook is treated as higher-signal than machine-accumulated lessons

decisions.choice: Skills are plain injected markdown, never executable ('just text, not code') — no run/exec surface
decisions.rationale: Guardrail against framework-creep while still promoting skills to first-class

decisions.choice: Slug scheme lowercases and collapses non-alphanumerics to hyphens, and same-slug add overwrites silently
decisions.rationale: Simple, predictable filenames; treat re-add as edit

decisions.choice: Skill heading text '## Project skills (apply these — how this project does things)' and per-skill '### <name>' sections
decisions.rationale: Distinguish the affirmative playbook from the lessons block in agent context

reviews.note: locked test amended after review — re-review required

findings.note: Slug collision is untested and silent: two distinct names that slug to the same file (e.g. 'API Conventions' vs 'api-conventions') overwrite each other with no warning. Not a criterion violation, but an unguarded data-loss edge.
No `skill remove`/`skill edit` path — skills can only be added or overwritten by re-adding the same slug. Acceptable for D2's scope, but lifecycle management is left entirely to manual file editing.

decisions.choice: Skills are budgeted and rendered ABOVE auto-lessons (skills win the leftover budget first; lessons fill the remainder).
decisions.rationale: Author-curated affirmative playbook is treated as higher-signal than machine-accumulated lessons, so under pressure lessons yield before skills.

decisions.choice: Skill body is plain injected markdown text, never executable — no code/hooks.
decisions.rationale: Explicit guardrail against framework-creep; a skill is context, not a plugin.

decisions.choice: Name is slugged (lowercase, non-alphanumeric→hyphen) into <slug>.md and re-adding the same slug silently overwrites.
decisions.rationale: Predictable filename mapping consistent with a single-file-per-skill model; treats add as upsert.

decisions.choice: `--file` takes precedence over inline text when both are supplied; empty/whitespace-only content is refused.
decisions.rationale: Deterministic source resolution and a minimum-content guard to keep the injected block meaningful.

decisions.choice: Elision note wording and per-skill '### <name>' section format chosen without a spec-fixed template; skills ordered by filename sort.
decisions.rationale: Mirrors the other elastic blocks' render style; alphabetical order is stable but not priority-aware.

title: design: specify Agent Adapter Protocol v1 and canonical role contracts

acceptanceCriteria.text: A normative protocol document uses MUST/SHOULD/MAY language and carries an explicit version.
Request and response examples cover text output, structured JSON output, failure, and usage reporting.
Every existing agent-backed Chalk stage maps to a named role and output contract.
Access requests distinguish at least `read-only` and `workspace-write`.
Identity includes an opaque reviewer-independence key; Chalk does not infer it from provider names.
Compatibility behavior for current command strings is specified.
A fake-adapter fixture demonstrates that the contract is implementable without importing Chalk internals.
The design explicitly identifies what remains inside Chalk core versus inside an adapter.

issue.body:
Parent roadmap: #226

## Problem

Chalk describes agents as BYO commands, but the actual contract is implicit and varies by call site. Provider-specific prompt transport, output recovery, permissions, usage capture, and identity cannot move behind adapters until the seam is specified.

## Deliverable

Write a versioned Agent Adapter Protocol v1 describing:

- the request envelope: protocol version, role, canonical instructions, task context, requested access, expected output contract, timeout, and working-directory semantics;
- the response envelope: status, text, optional structured payload, normalized usage, opaque identity metadata, and diagnostics;
- lifecycle and error behavior: exit codes, malformed output, timeouts, partial output, unknown fields, and forward compatibility;
- canonical role contracts for executor, planner, reviewer, discovery, feedback, retro, handoff, PR narrative, and regression authoring;
- the raw-command compatibility behavior for existing `protocol.*.command` users.

The contract should separate provider-neutral role semantics from provider-native prompt or agent-file formats.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A normative protocol document uses MUST/SHOULD/MAY language and carries an explicit version.
- [ ] Request and response examples cover text output, structured JSON output, failure, and usage reporting.
- [ ] Every existing agent-backed Chalk stage maps to a named role and output contract.
- [ ] Access requests distinguish at least `read-only` and `workspace-write`.
- [ ] Identity includes an opaque reviewer-independence key; Chalk does not infer it from provider names.
- [ ] Compatibility behavior for current command strings is specified.
- [ ] A fake-adapter fixture demonstrates that the contract is implementable without importing Chalk internals.
- [ ] The design explicitly identifies what remains inside Chalk core versus inside an adapter.

## Non-goals

- Implementing the Agent Runner.
- Implementing any real provider adapter.
- Choosing model names or provider-specific flags.

title: refactor: introduce the Agent Runner seam and migrate executor + planner

acceptanceCriteria.text: Executor and planner invoke one `runAgent(role, request)` interface instead of calling child-process helpers directly.
The runner returns normalized status, text, structured output, usage, identity, and diagnostics as applicable.
Existing command-string configuration produces the same observable executor and planner behavior.
Executor terminal output remains visible and planner output remains storable as plain text.
Timeouts, non-zero exits, missing binaries, malformed envelopes, and usage capture are covered by fake-adapter tests.
Project `protocol.runner` is no longer prepended to agent commands; it remains scoped to project toolchain commands.
No Chalk workflow module branches on a provider name.
Cost-ledger behavior from #99 remains compatible.

issue.body:
Parent roadmap: #226
Depends on: #227

## Problem

Executor and planner invocation currently use direct shell execution plus provider-aware output helpers. There is no single module responsible for role execution, normalization, diagnostics, and cost capture.

## Scope

Introduce one deep Agent Runner module following Agent Adapter Protocol v1. Start with the executor and planner paths, using a raw-command compatibility adapter so behavior remains unchanged for existing projects.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Executor and planner invoke one `runAgent(role, request)` interface instead of calling child-process helpers directly.
- [ ] The runner returns normalized status, text, structured output, usage, identity, and diagnostics as applicable.
- [ ] Existing command-string configuration produces the same observable executor and planner behavior.
- [ ] Executor terminal output remains visible and planner output remains storable as plain text.
- [ ] Timeouts, non-zero exits, missing binaries, malformed envelopes, and usage capture are covered by fake-adapter tests.
- [ ] Project `protocol.runner` is no longer prepended to agent commands; it remains scoped to project toolchain commands.
- [ ] No Chalk workflow module branches on a provider name.
- [ ] Cost-ledger behavior from #99 remains compatible.

## Non-goals

- Migrating reviewer or analysis roles.
- Introducing the new profile configuration.
- Adding a new provider.

title: refactor: route every remaining agent-backed stage through Agent Runner

acceptanceCriteria.text: Reviewer, discovery, feedback, retro, handoff, PR narrative, and regression authoring all call the Agent Runner.
Existing role-specific parsers receive normalized runner output and preserve their current success/error behavior.
Non-zero commands that still return a valid reviewer verdict remain parseable.
Best-effort narrative roles retain their fallback behavior and useful diagnostics.
Usage and wall-clock logging follow one runner-owned policy across every role.
Duplicate provider-aware execution and envelope-unwrapping code is removed.
Tests exercise each migrated role through the same fake-adapter seam.
The deletion test holds: removing Agent Runner would force execution complexity back into every caller.

issue.body:
Parent roadmap: #226
Depends on: #228

## Problem

A provider-neutral seam is not real while reviewer, discovery, feedback, retro, handoff, PR narrative, and regression authoring still execute commands independently.

## Scope

Migrate all remaining agent-backed stages to the Agent Runner and delete the superseded execution paths instead of layering wrappers over them.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Reviewer, discovery, feedback, retro, handoff, PR narrative, and regression authoring all call the Agent Runner.
- [ ] Existing role-specific parsers receive normalized runner output and preserve their current success/error behavior.
- [ ] Non-zero commands that still return a valid reviewer verdict remain parseable.
- [ ] Best-effort narrative roles retain their fallback behavior and useful diagnostics.
- [ ] Usage and wall-clock logging follow one runner-owned policy across every role.
- [ ] Duplicate provider-aware execution and envelope-unwrapping code is removed.
- [ ] Tests exercise each migrated role through the same fake-adapter seam.
- [ ] The deletion test holds: removing Agent Runner would force execution complexity back into every caller.

## Non-goals

- Changing role prompts or acceptance semantics.
- Adding provider profiles.
- Changing review cadence or gate policy.

Parent roadmap: #226
Depends on: #227, #228, #229

## Problem

Provider and model identity are inferred from shell command tokens and special environment variables. Role configuration is duplicated across `executor.command`, `planner.command`, `review.command`, and other stage keys.

## Scope

Add provider-neutral agent profiles and role bindings. A profile selects an adapter and carries optional opaque configuration such as model display text and reviewer-independence identity. Roles refer to profiles.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Configuration supports named profiles and a role-to-profile map.
- [ ] One profile can serve multiple roles without duplicating its connection details.
- [ ] Model values are opaque strings and never drive provider branches in Chalk core.

- [ ] Config drift tests and `docs/CONFIG.md` cover every new field.
- [ ] `chalk doctor --json` reports resolved role bindings and identity without exposing credentials.
- [ ] Tests cover shared profiles, distinct reviewer identity, unknown identity, and legacy configuration.

- Detecting installed CLIs.
- Removing legacy command support.

Provider permission flags are advisory and inconsistent. A reviewer or discovery agent can be configured through a command that mutates the worktree, and structured roles currently recover JSON differently at individual call sites.

## Scope

Make access and output requirements first-class Agent Runner contracts. Adapters report supported capabilities; Chalk requests the role policy and independently checks important invariants.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Every canonical role declares `read-only` or `workspace-write` access and text or structured output.
- [ ] Adapters report which requested capabilities they can enforce.
- [ ] Unsupported required capabilities fail readiness checks honestly rather than silently degrading.
- [ ] Chalk detects worktree changes made by a read-only role and refuses to accept that role result.
- [ ] The refusal identifies changed paths without automatically deleting user data.
- [ ] Structured roles validate their normalized payload against one role-specific contract after adapter decoding.
- [ ] Malformed, truncated, or schema-invalid output yields consistent diagnostics across providers.
- [ ] Tests use malicious and incapable fake adapters to cover mutation and capability failures.
- [ ] Executor write access remains unaffected.

## Non-goals

- Building a general OS sandbox.
- Automatically reverting unauthorized changes.
- Guaranteeing that a provider CLI permission mode is itself secure.

Parent roadmap: #226
Promotion review: #239
Depends on: #242

## Problem

The mutation fixture currently reports conformance PASS when an adapter returns `status: ok` after changing a read-only workspace. Its success condition proves that mutation happened, not that the result was refused.

## Scope

Make the conformance harness execute read-only fixtures through the same enforcement seam used in production, and require the normalized result to be failed/refused with a mutation diagnostic. Keep offline fixtures provider-inert while ensuring each adapter entrypoint actually satisfies the public Protocol v1 interface.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] An adapter returning `ok` after a read-only mutation cannot receive an overall passing conformance report.
- [ ] The mutation fixture passes only when the production enforcement seam returns a failed/refused normalized result with the changed path.
- [ ] Built-in and external adapter commands use the same assessment logic.
- [ ] Offline conformance makes no provider/network call; `--live` remains the only opt-in model call.
- [ ] Conformance still covers multiline transport, structured output, failures, usage, identity, diagnostics, timeouts, access, and unsupported capabilities.
- [ ] Tests include a malicious external adapter and prove a direct `ok`+mutation response fails conformance.

## Non-goals

- Certifying model quality.
- Contacting provider CLIs during offline CI.

reviews.note: Codex manual review: Agent Runner and conformance share one read-only refusal seam; the mutation fixture passes only on a normalized failed result naming changed paths; direct ok+mutation is retained as an adapter violation that fails the overall report; built-in/external commands share assessment; offline/network and all legacy fixtures remain covered; full Chalk verify passes.

issue.body:
Parent roadmap: #226
Promotion review: #239
Depends on: #241

## Problem

Read-only mutation detection snapshots dirty tracked files plus non-ignored untracked files. Existing ignored workspace files—such as local configuration—are invisible, so a read-only role can mutate them and still have its result accepted.

## Scope

Deepen the workspace-snapshot module so one interface detects net mutations across tracked, untracked, and ignored workspace files while continuing to exclude `.git`, dependency trees, and `.chalk/held-out/` by construction.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A read-only role that edits an existing ignored file is refused and the changed path is reported.
- [ ] Creating or deleting an ignored file is also detected.
- [ ] Clean tracked, dirty tracked, and ordinary untracked mutation detection remains green.
- [ ] `.git`, `node_modules`, and `.chalk/held-out/` are never traversed or reported.
- [ ] Symlinks are hashed without following targets outside the workspace.
- [ ] Workspace-write roles remain unaffected.
- [ ] Tests exercise the public workspace-snapshot/Agent Runner seam, including ignored files.

## Non-goals

- Restoring files mutated by an agent.
- Inspecting held-out test contents.

reviews.note: Codex manual review: Git inventories cover tracked, untracked, and ignored files; exclusion pathspecs and filters protect .git/node_modules/held-out; lstat hashes symlinks without following targets; the locked Agent Runner regression covers ignored edit/create/delete and workspace-write behavior; full Chalk verify passes.

title: fix(agents): keep reviewer independence unverified unless explicit

acceptanceCriteria.text: `chalk connect` does not synthesize `independenceKey` from adapter or model values.

Equal and different explicit keys still report `same` and `distinct` respectively.
Adapter-reported identity remains opaque to Chalk and may replace missing profile display metadata without being parsed for routing.
Doctor/connect remediation explains how to configure explicit identity or accept an unverified reviewer without falsely promising that changing providers proves independence.
Tests cover same, distinct, and unknown identity through the real `chalk connect` path.

issue.body:
Parent roadmap: #226
Promotion review: #239
Depends on: #240

## Problem

`chalk connect` manufactures `independenceKey` values from adapter ids and optional model strings. This can certify two profiles as independent without explicit identity evidence, contradicting Protocol v1's opaque-identity rule.

## Scope

Make unknown identity remain unknown. Chalk may compare an explicit configured or adapter-reported key, but core connection and readiness code must never derive one from provider, adapter, model, binary, flags, or environment conventions.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `chalk connect` does not synthesize `independenceKey` from adapter or model values.
- [ ] Distinct providers without explicit keys report reviewer independence as `unverified`, not `distinct`.
- [ ] Equal and different explicit keys still report `same` and `distinct` respectively.

issue.body:
Parent roadmap: #226
Promotion review: #239

## Problem

Agent Runner's raw-command compatibility path now prepends canonical role instructions whenever a production caller supplies `context`. Existing `protocol.*.command` integrations therefore receive different stdin bytes from the pre-runner behavior.

## Scope

Keep canonical instructions and context separate for Protocol v1 adapters while preserving the exact historical stage prompt for `raw-command` profiles. Put this compatibility decision behind the Agent Runner seam so workflow callers do not branch on transport.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Every legacy `protocol.*.command` role receives byte-for-byte the same stdin it received before Agent Runner.
- [ ] Protocol v1 profiles still receive separate canonical `instructions` and task `context` fields.
- [ ] Executor streaming, structured-role decoding, timeouts, and cost capture remain compatible.
- [ ] Tests call the same production `context` path used by executor, planner, reviewer, and analysis roles rather than bypassing it with test-only `input` calls.
- [ ] No workflow module branches on provider or adapter names.

## Non-goals

- Changing canonical role instructions.
- Removing the raw-command compatibility adapter.

reviews.note: Codex manual review: regression fails on the pre-change behavior; all nine raw-command roles preserve exact context bytes; Protocol v1 still transports instructions and context separately; focused tests and full Chalk verify pass; no unrelated product files changed.
