title: feat: persist verification runs with source-bound evidence

acceptanceCriteria.text: Every verify invocation, including done and automated callers, stores a unique local run with commands, complete stdout/stderr logs, timestamps, exit/signal/error status, source fingerprints, effective verification configuration and matching task criteria/test identity.

Source identity includes tracked and ordinary untracked inputs and excludes protocol bookkeeping, held-out content and ignored build output; unknown identity or inputs changing during a run are reported and cannot produce green verification.

Passing, failing, timed-out and interrupted subprocess results retain evidence without shell-buffer truncation; failures to persist evidence fail verification explicitly; existing integrity and toolchain behavior remains covered.

findings.note: lib/verification-record.mjs:107 compares only endpoint fingerprints. Reproduced a command modifying source.js, using its modified contents, then restoring it: verification returned green with freshness='fresh'. Criterion 2 prohibits inputs changing during the run. The existing mutation test covers only changes left behind.

lib/verification-record.mjs:51-57 silently excludes every .log file and conventional generated directories outside Git, regardless of whether they contain ordinary inputs. Reproduced mutation of an input fixture.log returning green/fresh with that file absent from the manifest. Git probe errors also select this permissive fallback instead of reporting unknown identity.

lib/verify.mjs delegates browser checks to lib/e2e.mjs:62, which still uses inherited stdout/stderr and discards subprocess status details. Reproduced browser output appearing on the terminal but absent from verification evidence; the recorded e2e entry lacks command, streams, timestamps and exit/signal/error details. Criteria 1 and 3 apply to these verification subprocesses too.

lib/verify.mjs:36-54 archives logs and finalizes status only after spawnSync returns. Sending SIGTERM to an active chalk verify left both receipt and gate permanently 'running', without completion or interruption status, referencing temporary logs; its detached command continued. The interruption test kills only the command itself and does not cover cancellation of the verifier.

lib/verification-record.mjs:102 records only in-progress tasks matching cwd, but performVerify checks other worktrees' active locks and, under all-locks, done-task locks. Their criteria/test identities are absent from otherwise successful receipts and freshness comparisons. Existing integrity tests assert verdicts, not this evidence completeness. All 33 focused tests passed, but they do not establish the full contract.

decisions.choice: Store UUID-addressed JSON receipts and separate logs under .chalk/local/verification.
decisions.rationale: Keeps complete evidence local and outside versioned bookkeeping, with atomic receipt replacement.

decisions.choice: Spool subprocess streams into temporary files and archive them after execution.
decisions.rationale: Avoids shell-buffer limits and prevents growing workspace logs from triggering read-only agent guards; requires reliable interruption recovery.

decisions.choice: Use Git manifests when available and heuristic filesystem exclusions otherwise.
decisions.rationale: Supports both Git and non-Git projects while suppressing generated output, but makes assumptions about which files can affect verification.

decisions.choice: Define freshness through before/after source, configuration and task digests.
decisions.rationale: Detects persistent changes without continuous monitoring or an immutable execution snapshot, but misses changes restored before completion.

decisions.choice: Scope recorded task contracts to active tasks in the execution worktree.
decisions.rationale: Associates evidence with the corresponding task checkout, but excludes additional contracts consumed by integrity verification.

findings.note: lib/verification-command.mjs:31–42 watches only directories containing initial manifest files. Reproduced creating, reading and deleting empty/transient.js inside a pre-existing empty directory: verify returned green=true, freshness='fresh', inputChanges=[]. This violates criterion 2. Watch eligible empty directories too and add a regression test.

lib/verification-command.mjs:99–112 finalizes when the shell exits, although descendants can still write inherited log descriptors. Reproduced 'node worker.cjs &' returning GREEN with empty archived stdout; the worker subsequently printed output and changed source.txt. The output remained absent from evidence. Retain supervision and log capture until descendants finish, or fail explicitly when they remain.

lib/verification-record.mjs:132–139 snapshots inputs before saving the initial receipt. A snapshot exception therefore leaves no run.json and no returned evidence reference. Reproduced with a symlinked locked test accepted by Store.lockTest: verify returned an integrity-input error and left an empty UUID directory. Persist an initial receipt before snapshotting and archive snapshot failures.

All 21 locked tests passed, but none covers transient inputs inside existing empty directories, surviving background descendants, or receipt retention after initial snapshot errors. The reproduced failures show that the current green suite does not establish criteria 1–3.

decisions.choice: Preserve synchronous verification callers through a separate asynchronous supervisor.
decisions.rationale: Avoids changing caller APIs while enabling filesystem monitoring, cancellation and interruption archival.

decisions.choice: Spool command streams outside the workspace, then copy them into local UUID run directories.
decisions.rationale: Avoids shell-buffer limits and prevents live output from triggering workspace mutation guards.

decisions.choice: Include timestamps, inode identity and executable bits alongside content hashes.
decisions.rationale: Detects restored-byte rewrites and permission changes, making fingerprints specific to local filesystem state.

decisions.choice: Use Git manifests when available and conservative filesystem enumeration otherwise; reject unresolved symlink targets.
decisions.rationale: Honors Git ignore rules without guessing which non-Git files are generated, and fails closed for uncertifiable inputs.

findings.note: lib/verify.mjs:54–56,76–84 and lib/verification-command.mjs:26–29: temporary contract changes bypass integrity verification. Reproduced a toolchain command removing a broken test's lock, followed by a browser command restoring it after integrity checking. Verification returned green=true, freshness='fresh', integrity=[], although the lock was broken before and after. Endpoint contract digests match and watchers exclude tasks.json. Bind execution to the captured contract and detect relevant changes throughout verification; add a regression test.

lib/verification-command.mjs:146–153 and lib/verify.mjs:61–64: archive failures erase recoverable command evidence. Reproduced a command printing both streams and exiting 7 while its archive destination was unavailable. Verification correctly returned RED, but the catch overwrote the supervisor's live receipt with an older record containing only skipped gates. The command, exit status and structured log references disappeared; output remained in an orphaned temporary spool. Preserve the latest command state and fallback log references when archival fails.

lib/e2e.mjs:68 changes verdict precedence so a runner's 'passed' report cannot override subprocess failure, but no test asserts conflicting verdicts. Existing tests either omit run.json or make its verdict agree with the exit code, so reverting this behavior still passes. Add a disagreement test plus coverage for the two reproduced failures. All 26 locked tests passed, and the supplied 625-test receipt matches current source/configuration/contract fingerprints; neither establishes these missing behaviors.

decisions.choice: Keep verification synchronous by launching a separate asynchronous supervisor for each command.
decisions.rationale: Preserves caller APIs while enabling streaming capture, filesystem monitoring and cancellation after controller termination. Adds process-management and platform-specific lifecycle complexity.

decisions.choice: Include timestamps, inode and executable bits alongside content in source fingerprints.
decisions.rationale: Detects rewrites that restore original bytes, but makes identity local to filesystem history rather than reproducible from identical content.

decisions.choice: Store UUID receipts locally and spool complete logs in temporary storage before copying them into each run.
decisions.rationale: Avoids shell-buffer truncation and interference with workspace mutation guards. Requires reliable archive-failure recovery and leaves retention unbounded.

decisions.choice: Make subprocess failure authoritative over a browser runner's passing report.
decisions.rationale: Prevents contradictory runner evidence from opening the verification gate, changing the previous report-precedence behavior.

findings.note: lib/verification-command.mjs:62–65 misclassifies deleted ignored directories. Reproduced with .gitignore containing build/ and a command that creates then removes build/output.log: exitCode=0 and identical source fingerprints, but green=false, freshness='stale', inputChanges=['build']. Once the directory disappears, check-ignore receives a basename without directory semantics. Preserve ignored-directory classification and add deletion coverage; the existing test only leaves generated output present.

lib/verification-command.mjs:153 writes recovery metadata outside the archival error handler. Reproduced by making the spool directory unwritable before a command exits 7: verification fails explicitly, but its persisted command remains 'running', without exitCode, signal, errorCode or finishedAt, despite complete readable logs and a writable main evidence directory. Handle this failure while preserving the completed outcome and attempting normal archival. Existing archive-failure coverage misses this path.

test/verification-record.test.mjs:52–58 is timing-sensitive: the locked suite passed 30/31 tests, failing because stdout lacked 'started' before the two-second timeout; the test passed in isolation. Establish subprocess readiness before testing timeout log retention so startup delays cannot masquerade as evidence loss.

decisions.choice: Keep verification synchronous through a separate asynchronous supervisor.
decisions.rationale: Preserves existing callers while streaming logs and supervising cancellation and descendants.

decisions.choice: Combine content hashes, filesystem metadata and directory watchers for source freshness.
decisions.rationale: Detects restored bytes and transient inputs, but makes identity machine-local and verification dependent on watcher availability.

decisions.choice: Freeze verification contracts and invalidate runs on authority-file metadata changes.
decisions.rationale: Prevents temporary configuration or lock changes from bypassing gates, while also invalidating unrelated writes to those files.

decisions.choice: Spool complete logs temporarily, then archive them under unique local run directories.
decisions.rationale: Avoids shell-buffer truncation and interference with mutation guards; introduces two storage failure boundaries.

decisions.choice: Prevent browser reports from overriding failed supervised subprocesses.
decisions.rationale: A runner-written passing verdict cannot conceal execution failure.

findings.note: lib/verification-command.mjs:74–78 treats vanished paths as directories without evidence. Reproduced with .gitignore containing build/: a command creates, reads and deletes an ordinary file named build, yet verify returns green=true, freshness='fresh', inputChanges=[]. This violates criterion 2. Preserve file/directory distinctions or fail closed when classification is unknown; add coverage alongside the ignored-directory deletion test.

lib/regression.mjs:102–104 ignores source-monitor failures and mutations from runToolchain. Reproduced an audit command rewriting source.js: inputChanges=['source.js'], but audit.green=true. Its evidence directory also lacks run.json and source/config/task bindings. Route phase verification through equivalent receipt and freshness enforcement, and test mutation/unknown-identity rejection; the audit-policy test only covers excluded inputs.

decisions.choice: Keep verification synchronous while delegating commands to an asynchronous supervisor with process-group cancellation.
decisions.rationale: Preserves existing callers while retaining streamed logs and handling controller interruption; adds platform-dependent supervision complexity.

decisions.choice: Combine content hashes, filesystem metadata and directory watchers for source identity.
decisions.rationale: Detects restored bytes and transient inputs, but makes verification depend on watcher availability and fingerprints sensitive to metadata-only changes.

decisions.choice: Use Git ignore rules for input boundaries and a conservative filesystem manifest outside Git.
decisions.rationale: Excludes ignored output without guessing generated-directory names; non-Git projects consequently fingerprint generated files too.

decisions.choice: Freeze configuration and task contracts before execution and detect authority-file rewrites.
decisions.rationale: Prevents commands from weakening later checks, while concurrent task/configuration updates invalidate verification.

decisions.choice: Store full logs locally under UUID run directories, with temporary recovery spools.
decisions.rationale: Avoids shell-buffer truncation and preserves recoverable evidence when archival fails; introduces local disk growth without a retention policy.

findings.note: lib/verification-command.mjs:62–65 violates criterion 2 by classifying earlier filesystem events using the path's current type. Reproduced three times with .gitignore containing build/: the command creates and reads an ordinary file named build, deletes it, then creates a directory named build. Verification returns green=true, freshness='fresh', inputChanges=[] because check-ignore sees the replacement directory. Fail closed when the event's original type cannot be established. Add a regression test for this transition; all 36 locked tests passed independently despite this false green.

lib/regression.mjs:102 changes audit from toolchain-only phase verification to full verify, adding visible locked-test integrity checks and active browser-spec execution. No audit test asserts these added behaviors: current coverage exercises toolchain freshness, exclusions and held-out gates. Add audit integration tests proving broken visible locks and failed browser commands block audit and retain evidence, or preserve the previous gate scope. These untested behavior changes trigger the required block rule.

decisions.choice: Preserve a synchronous verification API through a separate asynchronous subprocess supervisor.
decisions.rationale: Allows streamed logs, deadlines and cancellation recovery without converting existing callers to async; introduces process-tree supervision and platform-specific behavior.

decisions.choice: Combine source-content hashes, filesystem metadata and notifications, failing closed when monitoring is unavailable.
decisions.rationale: Detects restored bytes and transient inputs, but makes successful verification dependent on filesystem-watching permissions and conservative path classification.

decisions.choice: Freeze verification contracts and invalidate runs on any task/config authority-file rewrite.
decisions.rationale: Prevents temporary lock or configuration removal from bypassing gates, while also rejecting unrelated concurrent bookkeeping changes.

decisions.choice: Route phase audits through full verification.
decisions.rationale: Reuses receipt and freshness enforcement, but also expands audit to visible integrity and browser gates.

decisions.choice: Keep receipts and complete logs local; defer evidence reuse and broader environment identity.
decisions.rationale: Limits this slice to host execution evidence. Done reruns verification, and receipts do not fully identify external SDKs, installed dependencies or relevant environment inputs.

findings.note: lib/verification-command.mjs:137–143: live-log write errors escape asynchronously from the data handlers, bypassing cancellation and outcome archival. Injecting ENOSPC reproduced a failed verification whose command receipt remained 'running', without finish time or exit/signal status; the detached command survived and wrote a later marker. This violates criteria 1 and 3. Catch stream/write failures, terminate and await the command tree, and persist the failed outcome with recoverable logs. Add a regression test for this path.

lib/verification-command.mjs:149–157 adds supervision after descendants close their streams, but no test asserts that behavior. The background-descendant test inherits stdout/stderr, so Node's close event already waits for it; removing the process-group wait would leave that test passing. Add a descendant that closes its streams and assert verification waits or cancels it. All 38 locked tests passed independently, but this behavior lacks the required revert-detecting coverage.

decisions.choice: Preserve the synchronous verification API using a separate asynchronous supervisor and temporary log spool.
decisions.rationale: Avoids shell-output buffer limits and supports recovery when the controller exits, while introducing additional process and storage failure boundaries.

decisions.choice: Include filesystem metadata and mandatory notifications in source freshness checks.
decisions.rationale: Detects temporary rewrites and transient inputs; metadata-only changes and unavailable monitoring also close the gate.

decisions.choice: Expand phase audit from toolchain execution to full verification, including visible locks and active browser specifications.
decisions.rationale: Reuses source-bound recording and freshness enforcement, while adding audit failure conditions and execution cost.

decisions.choice: Defer external SDK, dependency-installation and environment identity, and independently validated Windows supervision.
decisions.rationale: Bounds this slice to local source evidence and development-host supervision; receipts consequently have narrower reproducibility and portability guarantees.

findings.note: lib/verification-record.mjs:48–53 omits ancestor .gitignore files when Chalk runs below the Git worktree root. Independently reproduced a command creating, reading and deleting ephemeral.js, temporarily changing ../.gitignore to conceal its events, then restoring that policy. Verification returned green=true, freshness='fresh', and inputChanges=[]; the ancestor policy was absent from the receipt. This violates criterion 2. Bind and monitor applicable ancestor ignore files through the Git root, and add a regression test.

lib/verification-record.mjs:44–50 discovers configuration files only from existing Git configuration entries, omitting initially absent configuration authorities. Independently reproduced this with GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL pointing to an absent temporary file: the command created configuration selecting an ignore file, created/read/deleted an ordinary input, then removed the configuration. Verification again returned fresh GREEN with no input changes. Track absent configuration candidates and their creation, including explicitly configured paths. All 43 locked tests and 12 existing regression tests passed, but neither reproduced policy gap is covered.

decisions.choice: Preserve the synchronous verification API using a separate asynchronous supervisor and temporary log spool.
decisions.rationale: Streams large outputs and handles cancellation while preserving existing callers; adds subprocess and recovery complexity.

decisions.choice: Combine content hashes, filesystem metadata and notifications to determine freshness.
decisions.rationale: Detects restored bytes and transient inputs, but makes successful verification dependent on monitoring availability and conservative event classification.

decisions.choice: Invalidate verification on any task/configuration authority-file rewrite.
decisions.rationale: Protects captured contracts against temporary changes, while also rejecting unrelated concurrent bookkeeping.

decisions.choice: Run full verification during phase audits, including integrity and active browser checks.
decisions.rationale: Applies the same evidence and freshness gates to audits, expanding their enforcement and execution cost.

decisions.choice: Conservatively include ordinary files outside Git without guessing generated directories.
decisions.rationale: Avoids silently excluding source inputs, but can hash dependencies and classify generated output as source changes in non-Git projects.

findings.note: Criterion 2 remains bypassable through transient Git index changes. lib/verification-command.mjs excludes .git events and classifies newly tracked paths using the initial manifest plus check-ignore --no-index; lib/verification-record.mjs does not monitor index membership. Independently reproduced: start with ignored candidate.js, run git add -f candidate.js, modify/read it while tracked, then git rm --cached -f candidate.js. Verification returned green=true, freshness='fresh', inputChanges=[] despite changing a tracked input during execution. Monitor changes to tracked-input membership and add a regression covering this sequence while preserving unchanged-staging behavior. All 46 locked tests and 22 existing regression tests passed, demonstrating that current coverage misses this case.

decisions.choice: Preserve the synchronous verification API using a separate asynchronous subprocess supervisor and temporary log storage.
decisions.rationale: Retains complete streams and interruption evidence without migrating existing callers to asynchronous APIs; introduces additional process and storage lifecycle management.

decisions.choice: Fail verification closed when filesystem monitoring or Git configuration-authority discovery is unavailable.
decisions.rationale: Prevents unsupported environments from claiming fresh evidence, at the cost of compatibility with older Git versions and restricted environments.

decisions.choice: Reject ambiguous directory-only ignore events.
decisions.rationale: A current directory cannot establish whether an earlier event involved an ordinary file; generated-output workflows must retain directories or declare type-independent exclusions.

decisions.choice: Route phase audits through full verification, including visible integrity and active browser checks.
decisions.rationale: Gives phase gates bound receipts and consistent enforcement, while expanding audit execution and failure conditions.

decisions.choice: Use filesystem metadata and whole task/config authority files for within-run freshness.
decisions.rationale: Detects restored-byte mutations and temporary contract changes, but unrelated concurrent bookkeeping can invalidate verification.

decisions.choice: Keep receipts local and defer verification reuse and comprehensive dependency/environment identity.
decisions.rationale: Scopes this change to execution evidence; done continues rerunning verification, and receipts cannot yet support comprehensive reproducibility or safe reuse.

findings.note: Criterion 2 remains bypassable through the .git gitdir pointer. lib/verification-record.mjs:75 binds HEAD and commondir but omits the .git file selecting their repository; lib/verification-command.mjs:28 excludes its events. Independently reproduced using git init --separate-git-dir: temporarily point .git at another repository whose ignore policy excludes ephemeral.js, create/read/delete ephemeral.js, then restore .git. Verification returned green=true, freshness='fresh', inputChanges=[], and identical before/after source fingerprints. Bind and monitor repository-discovery selectors, including .git files, and add a regression requiring this sequence to fail. All 50 locked acceptance tests and 12 existing integrity/browser regression tests passed, demonstrating that current coverage misses this false GREEN.

decisions.rationale: Bounds this implementation to recording current execution; done continues rerunning verification, and receipts do not establish reproducibility across hosts.

findings.note: Criterion 2 is bypassable in descendant directories. lib/verification-command.mjs:28 excludes every .git event, but :99 classifies new files using Git discovered from the event's directory. lib/verification-record.mjs:93 binds selectors only from the verification root upward and in recognized submodules. Verification returned green=true, freshness='fresh', inputChanges=[], and identical source fingerprints. Bind repository selection for every directory used for classification, or reject selector changes there, and add this regression.

Validate all retained streams before finalizing success and preserve recoverable evidence until then. Add coverage for later-gate deletion and truncation.

findings.note: Criteria 1 and 3 fail at lib/verification-command.mjs:193–226. Stream identities are calculated by reopening spool paths after execution, rather than hashing captured chunks. Independently reproduced: a command emits stdout, unlinks its live stdout spool, recreates an empty file there, and emits more stdout. Verification returns green=true, freshness='fresh', and a zero-byte stdout archive with no error. Bind byte counts and hashes to captured chunks, detect spool replacement/truncation, and preserve recoverable output before closing descriptors.

Initial archival can overwrite source at lib/verification-command.mjs:237. Independently reproduced: the command creates test.stdout.log as a symlink to source.txt; copyFileSync follows it and replaces the original source with command output. Final validation reports RED and repairs the archive, but leaves source corrupted. Apply safe atomic destination replacement to initial archival, including protection against redirected parent directories.

All 59 locked verification tests and 12 existing integrity/browser regression tests passed independently despite both reproduced failures. Retention coverage exercises later-gate archive damage, but misses live-spool replacement/truncation and redirection before initial archival. Add regressions asserting complete captured output or explicit failure, and preservation of source bytes.

Changing its contents leaves the digest unchanged with status='known'. Treat the configured directory literally and add tracked/untracked regression cases.

The parent directory never changed, and the output is unambiguously ignored. Distinguish ancestor matches from ambiguous changes to the ignored directory itself and test this case.

The isolated rerun passed, leaving an intermittent watcher-evidence failure unresolved. All 17 selected existing regressions passed. Neither reproduced boundary defect above has a regression assertion.

findings.note: Criterion 2: invalidated alignment and plan approvals do not prevent completion. lib/spec-revisions.mjs:59 deletes them, but lib/run.mjs:78–143 never rechecks after execution, and bin/chalk.mjs:1748's done handler does not enforce them. Independently reproduced with both approvals required: an executor amended the criteria and chalk run marked the task done without renewed approval. Direct amend-spec → done also succeeded. Recheck the current revision and required approvals before completion; add regression tests for both paths.

Criterion 2: merge ignores invalidated verification. lib/spec-revisions.mjs:68 sets verificationInvalidated, but lib/brokecheck.mjs:42 accepts existing green remote CI and lib/mergegate.mjs:9 never checks the marker or revision. An isolated CLI reproduction amended criteria, configured local verification to fail, supplied mock green CI, and successfully merged with verificationInvalidated still set. Require verification against the amended contract before merging. The 13 passing locked tests cover work's shortcut, but not this admission path.

findings.note: lib/archive.mjs:79–94 loses revision history after interrupted archival. Independently reproduced: interrupt after archive-file creation but before live-task removal; amend, revalidate and release the live task; retry archive. Deduplication keeps the archived revision 0 while deleting live revision 1 and its history. An audit approval for revision 0 then becomes current again. This violates both criteria. Reconcile archived and live revisions before removal, and add interruption/retry coverage.

findings.note: Criterion 2 is bypassable after archival. lib/store.mjs:462 inserts a stale task snapshot when its live record has disappeared, without checking archived revisions. Independently reproduced through chalk plan: while planning in a separate task workdir, amend, revalidate, release and archive the canonical task; the returning planner resurrects the old criteria, passing review and alignment. lib/audit-specification.mjs:8 then lets that older live record override newer archived history, making the old audit current again. The resurrected completion is also release-eligible. Reject stale resurrection and fail closed on conflicting live/archive revisions. The 64 passing specification tests omit this interleaving.

bin/chalk.mjs:869 persists an immutable release contract before tag-collision preflight. Reproduced: release --commit refuses an existing tag without changing release artifacts; another task completes; the suggested retry with --no-tag now fails with 'release candidate changed'. lib/release-admission.mjs:31 treats this artifact-free refusal as an interrupted candidate. Defer the record until preflight succeeds, or safely retire records for attempts that produced no artifacts, and cover this retry.

findings.note: Criteria 1/3: Legacy bases remain mutable. lib/review-inputs.mjs:45 resolves the configured branch on every capture, while lib/approval-inputs.mjs:48 binds only task.reviewBase. Criteria 1/3: lib/review-inputs.mjs:64–71 does not enumerate submodule changes. A temporary fixture containing vendor/new.js reported files=["vendor"], untracked=[], and only a dirty gitlink marker. Criterion 1: lib/review-inputs.mjs:67 captures the effective working tree but loses staged content overwritten by unstaged edits. Capture effective contents faithfully or reject transformation-dependent inputs, and add a regression test.

lib/review-inputs.mjs:94: Git clean filters can hide effective working-tree changes from both the complete file list and diff. Reproduced with a filter that removes selected lines: modify a tracked JavaScript file, stage it, and add another untracked file. Capture lists only the untracked file, omitting the modified JavaScript and its runtime behavior without rejecting preflight. --no-textconv does not disable clean filters. Capture effective contents faithfully or reject transformation-dependent inputs, and add a regression test.

findings.note: Criterion 3 fails: lib/review-evidence.mjs:211–214 publishes timestamp strings verbatim. Date.parse accepts comments containing private data. In an isolated fixture, timestamps ending with '(/Users/private/api.env)' and '(API_KEY=PRIVATE_SENTINEL)' passed validation; buildPrBody published both while reporting current evidence and recordedGreen:true. Normalize timestamps to canonical ISO values or reject noncanonical timestamps before publication. All 31 focused tests passed independently, but their redaction assertions miss this case.

title: feat: reuse verification only with validated inputs and execution provenance

acceptanceCriteria.text: Inspect existing receipt, observer, approval and executor trust boundaries before implementation. Establish explicit identity for relevant source, tests, dependencies, gate configuration, toolchain and environment; unknown coverage disables reuse.

Permit done to reuse only a successfully completed execution whose provenance and retained evidence are validated and whose relevant inputs still match. A matching hash or editable green field alone must never open the gate. Failed, interrupted, malformed, stale and untrusted receipts require fresh execution.

Retain fresh locked-test integrity and admission checks, detect changes during execution and reuse admission, and support an explicit force-rerun option. Unchanged verify-review-done avoids duplicate expensive execution; meaningful regressions prove relevant changes and damaged evidence close the gate.
